items.headline: Lamar buys Newman Outdoor's 2,250 faces and becomes North Dakota's leading billboard owner
items.dek: The cash deal for the 70-year-old family firm adds 73 digital displays across four upper-Midwest states, the latest in a run of US roadside consolidation.
items.source: Billboard Insider, on Lamar Advertising's acquisition of Newman Outdoor Advertising
keyPoints: Lamar has bought the assets of Newman Outdoor Advertising, more than 2,250 billboard faces including 73 digital displays, in North Dakota, Minnesota, Montana and South Dakota.
Chief executive Sean Reilly said the deal immediately makes Lamar the leading OOH player in North Dakota and strengthens it across the upper Midwest.
The purchase was paid in cash; the price was not disclosed and the deal closed the week it was announced.
Newman, founded in North Dakota in 1956, had already sold its New Mexico billboards and non-billboard businesses.
body: Lamar Advertising announced on 11 November that it had acquired the billboard business of Newman Outdoor Advertising, a family company founded by Harold Newman in 1956 that later added traffic-sign manufacturing and large-format printing. The deal covers more than 2,250 faces, 73 of them digital, across four states. Delancey Street Partners advised Newman; Kean Miller advised Lamar.

The purchase comes days after Lamar raised its 2026 guidance on third-quarter revenue up 6.6%, and amid a wave of US roadside deals, including New Tradition's purchase of Connell Outdoor and continued buying by Adams Outdoor. For listed owners, regional family portfolios remain the quickest way to add scale and digital conversion opportunities in secondary markets.
items.relevance: Consolidation is concentrating US roadside inventory in fewer hands, especially outside the big metros. Buyers planning regional US campaigns will increasingly deal with one national owner per market; independents face stiffer competition for local advertisers.

pitch.line: Lamar has added more than 2,250 billboard faces, including 73 digital displays, across four upper-Midwest states by buying Newman Outdoor (Lamar via Billboard Insider).

items.headline: Australia's foreign-investment regulator clears I Squared's takeover of oOh!media
items.dek: With FIRB's approval and shareholders already on side, only the court stands between the infrastructure investor and Australia's largest listed real-world media owner.
items.source: Kalkine Media, on oOh!media's ASX announcement
keyPoints: The Treasurer has no objection to I Squared Capital's acquisition of oOh!media through its vehicle OOH BidCo, satisfying the FIRB condition of the scheme.
Shareholders approved the A$1.68-a-share scheme, valuing the company at about A$1.04bn including debt, with 99.89% of votes cast on 2 November.
The scheme still needs court approval at a second hearing scheduled for 18 November, with implementation expected on 10 December.
Once complete, oOh!media will leave the ASX, following Clear Channel Outdoor's move into private ownership under Mubadala Capital in October.
body: oOh!media told the ASX on 13 November that the Foreign Investment Review Board had cleared I Squared Capital's proposed takeover under the Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Act, satisfying a key condition of the scheme implementation agreement. The decision had been delayed past its original deadline, pushing back the second court hearing.

The deal followed a four-way bidding contest earlier this year. If the court approves the scheme on 18 November, it is expected to become effective the next day and be implemented on 10 December, ending oOh!media's life as a listed company.
items.relevance: Two of the world's larger real-world media owners, oOh!media and Clear Channel Outdoor, are moving into private hands within two months, a sign that infrastructure investors value the medium's long-term contracts and steady cash flows. Expect more investment in digital conversion, and less public disclosure from both companies.

pitch.line: Infrastructure investor I Squared Capital is paying A$1.68 a share for oOh!media, about A$1.04bn including debt, after shareholders and FIRB approved the deal (oOh!media ASX releases).

links.label: Kalkine Media: second court hearing moved to 18 November

items.headline: Rotana Signs brings CESP-validated audience measurement to its Saudi OOH network
items.dek: Mobility-data firm SEIKI now measures audiences across the media owner's sites in twelve Saudi cities, laying the ground for programmatic planning and buying.
items.source: Campaign Middle East
keyPoints: Rotana Signs has partnered with SEIKI to measure audiences on its OOH networks across twelve Saudi cities, including Jeddah, Makkah, Madinah, Dammam and Al Khobar, covering more than 15m people.
SEIKI's methodology has been audited and validated by France's CESP, the independent body that certifies audience measurement.
The data shows each site's audience profile, reach and frequency contribution and overlap, and lets new sites be evaluated against the existing estate.
Rotana Signs plans to use the measurement as the basis for programmatic OOH planning and buying.
body: Rotana Signs, one of Saudi Arabia's main real-world media owners, has been rolling out SEIKI's mobility-based audience measurement since June 2026 across formats such as digital megacoms, digital bridges and premium billboards. SEIKI's platform is used in more than 40 markets and has measured premium billboard campaigns for French luxury groups and Orange's OOH networks in six countries.

Chief commercial officer Georges Yazbeck said data and audience understanding are essential to effective planning. The measurement shows that some locations skew affluent while others reach broader age and income groups, information advertisers can use to match sites to targets.
items.relevance: Independently validated audience data is the entry ticket for international and programmatic budgets. Saudi Arabia's OOH market is adopting the same standards as Europe, which will make Gulf inventory easier to plan alongside other media and across borders.

pitch.line: Rotana Signs now measures audiences across twelve Saudi cities and more than 15m people with a CESP-validated methodology from SEIKI (Campaign Middle East).

items.headline: Pakistan's brands put 18% of media spend into OOH, more than three times the global norm, WOO interview shows
items.dek: WOO's ambassador in Pakistan says the market reached $131m in 2025, with digital already 31% of OOH spend and DOOH up 59% in a year.
items.source: WOO (World Out of Home Organization), interview with Ahsan Sheikh

figures.label: Pakistan OOH revenue, FY2025 (+38% in two years)
Share of brands' media spend in OOH (global ≈5%)

keyPoints: Pakistan's OOH market reached $131m in FY2025, up 38% in two years and growing faster than digital media while TV and print declined.
Brands put 18% of their media spend into OOH, against a global average of about 5%.
Digital already accounts for 31% of OOH spend, ahead of India's 18%; DOOH spend rose 59% to PKR11.3bn in 2025 across more than 5,000 screens and 1,300 brands.
Spend per head is about $0.51, the lowest among Asian peers, which Sheikh sees as headroom for growth.
body: In an interview published by WOO a week after Karachi's IRL Conference drew more than 325 delegates, Ahsan Sheikh, chief executive of Kinetic Pakistan and WOO's ambassador for the country, set out the market's numbers. Programmatic DOOH has been live since 2023, and AI-driven planning and creative are the next steps.

Sheikh placed Pakistan in the context of Asia-Pacific's strong run, which he said led global OOH growth at close to 30% in 2025. The combination of a high OOH share of budgets, fast digital conversion and very low spend per head makes Pakistan one of the medium's most promising frontier markets.
items.relevance: Pakistan shows how quickly OOH can digitise in a fast-growing market: digital share there is already well ahead of India's. International brands entering South Asia should expect OOH to be a core, not supporting, channel in the plan.

pitch.line: Brands in Pakistan put 18% of their media spend into OOH, more than three times the global average of about 5% (WOO interview with Kinetic Pakistan's Ahsan Sheikh).

items.headline: blowUP media adds a giant banner outside Leeds Station to its UK landmark portfolio
items.dek: The new site faces a station used by about 27.3m passengers a year, next to the city's main luxury and leisure districts.
items.source: Outsmart, on blowUP media

figures.label: Passengers with significant monthly disposable income

keyPoints: blowUP media is launching a giant banner directly outside the Leeds Station exit, in a prime city-centre position.
About 27.3m passengers pass through the station each year, 60% of them with significant monthly disposable income, according to the media owner.
The site overlooks Boar Lane, Victoria Quarter and Trinity Leeds, home to more than 1,000 stores including Harvey Nichols and Louis Vuitton, and the nightlife of Call Lane.
body: blowUP media, which specialises in large building-wrap and banner sites, has added Leeds Station to its premium UK portfolio. The banner faces commuters, shoppers and visitors leaving one of northern England's busiest stations.

The launch extends landmark-format competition beyond London, following Ocean Outdoor's new Birmingham banner earlier this month. Regional city centres with dense rail footfall and luxury retail are becoming attractive for brands that want London-style impact at a lower cost.
items.relevance: Large-format landmark sites are spreading to the UK's regional cities, giving luxury, fashion and entertainment brands new ways to make an impression outside London. Planners can use station footfall as a proxy for both reach and affluence.

pitch.line: blowUP media's new giant banner at Leeds Station faces about 27.3m passengers a year, 60% of them with significant disposable income (Outsmart).

brief: AI is eating budgets faster than it proves its worth: Peec AI finds 89% of marketers raised AI-search spend this year but only 24% can show a return, and Validity says 61% face boardroom pressure to prove AI gains in 2027.

Shoppers are delegating, but not surrendering: half of Spain's online buyers used AI in a purchase, German retailers expect agents to dominate product search, yet only 4.5% of Brazilian AI users always follow its advice.

In real-world media, Ströer's digital OOH rose 11% and programmatic 21% while classic posters fell 4.4%, China's OOH spend passed CNY202bn in nine months, and VIOOH opened GSTV's 29,000 US forecourt screens to programmatic buyers.

Diary: SPT's west of Scotland bus shelter tender and FIRB's oOh!media decision fall on 13 November, oOh!media's scheme goes to court on 18 November and Schiphol's €426m advertising tender closes on 20 November.

numberOfDay.line: Programmatic DOOH revenue at Ströer grew 21.1% in the third quarter, almost twice the pace of its digital OOH business overall, while classic posters fell 4.4% (Ströer).

steal.title: Make them want it
steal.text: Havas finds 84% of brands in Italy sit in a 'zone of indifference', and those that build desire on every front are 2.4 times more likely to grow. The idea worth stealing: audit your brand for desire, not just awareness, and use big, unmissable public formats to make it feel wanted rather than merely known.

items.headline: Nine in ten marketers raised AI search spend this year, but only a quarter can prove it pays, Peec AI finds
items.dek: A survey of 700 marketing decision-makers in the US, UK and Germany, plus data from more than 100 million AI chats, shows budgets racing ahead of measurement as ChatGPT changes how it searches and what it cites.
items.source: Peec AI, Primary Sources Q3 2026

figures.label: Raised AI search spend in the past year
Can prove a return on AI search
ChatGPT conversations triggering a single search, September (98% in July)
Product pages' share of AI citations, end of Q3 (13.8% before)

keyPoints: 89% of marketing teams raised AI search spending in the past year and 81% plan to raise it again, yet only 24% can show what the channel returns, according to a Sapio Research survey of 700 decision-makers for Peec AI.

Platform volatility is the biggest barrier (33%): between July and September the share of ChatGPT conversations that ran a single search fell from 98% to 39%, and average sources per answer rose from 11 to 19.

Citations are moving towards brands' own assets: company websites rose from 52% to 58% of weekly citations and product pages from 13.8% to 20.1%, while 'best X' listicles fell from 16.2% to 7.3% and Reddit citations collapsed.
Integration pays: 43% of companies with an integrated AI search strategy can prove ROI, against 23% of those without one; only 3% let communications or PR lead the work.
The US is ahead on proof: 31% of US firms can show ROI, against 19% in the UK and 18% in Germany.
body: Peec AI, a Berlin-based AI search platform, has launched a quarterly research series, Primary Sources. The first edition combines a Sapio Research survey of 700 marketing decision-makers (manager level and above, at companies with 100+ staff) in the US, UK and Germany, fielded in September 2026, with Peec's own platform data from more than 100 million AI chats on ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Gemini and Claude between July and September.

The money is flowing: 89% raised AI search budgets over the past year and 61% call AI visibility a top priority. Pressure comes mainly from competitors showing up in AI answers (43%) and customers using AI to research or buy (42%). But only 24% can prove a return, and among firms that raised spend significantly, 64% cannot. Fast platform change (33%), brand safety (30%) and unreliable measurement (28%) are the top barriers, and 88% of multi-team companies report coordination problems.

The platform data shows why. After a change of default model in August, ChatGPT's search behaviour shifted sharply: single-search conversations fell from 98% to 39%, searches limited to one website rose from almost zero to 21%, and 'best' queries dropped from 19% to 8%. Company websites and product pages gained citation share, while listicles and Reddit lost it. Teams with metrics they trust are far less likely to abandon tactics: 7% have stopped optimising for AI recommendations, against 31% of others.
items.relevance: As AI assistants cite brands' own pages more and third-party lists less, brand fame and clear owned content matter more for being recommended. The measurement gap is a reminder that budgets moving into new channels still need proof, which gives media with established effectiveness evidence, including OOH, a useful contrast in planning talks.

pitch.line: 89% of marketers raised AI search spend this year, but only 24% can prove it pays (Peec AI, Primary Sources Q3 2026).

items.headline: Two-thirds of marketers expect bigger 2027 budgets, but six in ten must prove AI pays, Validity finds
items.dek: Validity's winter survey of more than 250 B2B and B2C marketers finds AI taking a growing share of 2027 plans, while paid media was the most common target of mid-year cuts.
items.source: Validity, Winter 2026–2027 Marketer Survey

figures.label: Expect overall marketing budgets to rise in 2027
Plan to put at least 10% of budget into AI
Under C-suite pressure to show measurable AI gains
Use AI agents to run workflows with minimal oversight today

keyPoints: 66% of marketers expect their budgets to rise in 2027 and 53% plan to put at least 10% into AI, but 61% face C-suite pressure to show measurable AI gains.
Half say 2026 AI investments met or beat ROI expectations; 26% say returns fell short or could not be measured, and 24% cannot yet tell.
Paid media was the most common mid-year cut (20%), ahead of AI tools and agents (16%), in-house headcount and email (15% each) and events (11%).
Only 7% let AI agents run workflows with little oversight now, but 42% expect performance reporting to run that way by the end of 2027.
Marketers are hedging: 32% hold budget back for mid-year reallocation and 26% are moving to quarterly or rolling plans.
body: Validity, a marketing data and AI software firm, surveyed more than 250 B2B and B2C marketing professionals for its Winter 2026–2027 Marketer Survey. The mood on budgets is positive: two-thirds expect overall marketing spend to increase next year, and 88% are at least somewhat confident their 2027 plans will hold. More than half plan to allocate at least 10% of budget to AI.

The catch is accountability. 61% report pressure from the C-suite to demonstrate measurable AI gains, with marketing ROI or ROAS (25%), revenue and pipeline (19%) and customer acquisition cost (16%) the measures leaders care most about. Half say this year's AI spend met or beat expectations, mostly through cost savings (41%), better engagement (39%) and time saved (35%); only 26% of those seeing returns measure revenue against AI cost.

Plans are also becoming more flexible. Paid media was the line most often cut mid-year, and economic conditions (17%) and AI's effect on how customers discover brands (15%) top the list of uncertainties. A third keep money in reserve for reallocation, a third invest in scenario planning, and a quarter have moved to quarterly or rolling planning.
items.relevance: With paid media the first line cut mid-year and planning cycles shortening, sellers should expect more flexible, shorter-notice bookings and sharper ROI questions in 2027. Clear outcome evidence and flexible buying options, such as programmatic DOOH, fit how these budgets are now managed.

pitch.line: 61% of marketers face C-suite pressure to prove measurable AI gains as AI takes a bigger share of 2027 budgets (Validity, Winter 2026–2027 Marketer Survey).

items.headline: China's OOH spend passes CNY202bn in nine months as video screens grow 7%, CODC finds
items.dek: CODC's tracking of rate-card spend shows Chinese real-world media edging up 4% in the first three quarters of 2026, with video formats and transit hubs carrying the market while liquor brands pull back.
items.source: Sohu, on CODC's 2026 Q1–Q3 OOH advertising market analysis

figures.label: Share of rate-card spend from top 10 categories

keyPoints: Rate-card spend on OOH in China reached CNY202.2bn in the first nine months of 2026, according to CODC; video formats accounted for CNY140.3bn, about 69% of the total.
Video OOH grew 7% and drew 7,221 advertising brands, while traditional OOH rose 3% to CNY61.9bn; after adjusting for rate-card changes, video was roughly flat (-0.6%) and traditional up 2%.

Transport hubs anchor traditional OOH: metro is the largest format, and metro, airports and railway stations together take more than 80% of spend; metro, airport and bus-shelter placements grew, while railway stations, bus bodies and street networks declined.

The ten largest advertiser categories now account for 80% of spend, up eight points; software spend roughly doubled and food and personal care each rose by more than 40%, while liquor fell by nearly 30%.
body: China's real-world media market kept growing modestly through the first three quarters of 2026, according to CODC's analysis of OOH advertising placements, published on Sohu on 11 November. Total rate-card spend reached CNY202.2bn. Video formats, which include building and commercial-district screens, brought in CNY140.3bn, up 7% year on year, and the number of brands using them rose to 7,221, although the average spend per brand dipped slightly. Traditional OOH grew 3% to CNY61.9bn. The figures are at rate-card value; after adjusting for price changes, CODC puts growth at about 2% for traditional media and slightly below zero for video.

Transit dominates the traditional side. Metro is the single biggest format, and metro, airports and railway stations together make up more than 80% of traditional OOH spend. Metro, airport and bus-shelter placements grew in the period, while railway stations, bus bodies and street networks lost spend. The context is a slow economy: national GDP grew 4.6% in the first three quarters.

Spend is concentrating among fewer categories. The top ten industries now account for 80% of rate-card spend, eight points more than before. Software and internet platforms, such as Meituan and Xianyu, roughly doubled their outlay, and food and personal care each grew by more than 40%. Beverages remain the largest category for a third year, though their share is shrinking, and liquor spending fell by nearly 30%.
items.relevance: China's OOH growth is coming from video screens and transit hubs, and from app, food and personal-care advertisers, so these are the formats and categories to target. Because the figures are at rate-card value, sellers should quote the price-adjusted growth alongside the headline numbers when pitching China plans.

pitch.line: Chinese brands spent CNY202bn at rate card on OOH in the first nine months of 2026, with video screens up 7% (CODC, via Sohu).

items.headline: Retail media makes more French shoppers want to buy, but in-store screens still struggle for attention, iligo finds
items.dek: The fourth wave of iligo's Retail Media barometer shows weekly exposure to shop-window and in-store screens rising, but only 15% of French people pay close attention to the ads on them.
items.source: iligo, Baromètre Retail Media (4th edition)

figures.label: Say retail media ads online make them want to buy (+4 pts)
Visit places with shop-window ad screens at least weekly (+4 pts)
Pay close attention to ads on in-store screens
Want more ads on in-store screens (+2 pts)

keyPoints: 55% of French adults who see retail media online say the ads make them want to buy, up four points in a year, according to iligo's survey of 2,011 people aged 18–69.
Weekly exposure to physical retail screens is rising: 34% pass shop-window screens at least once a week (up from 30%) and 32% visit stores or malls with in-store screens (+2 points).
Attention is the weak spot: only 15% say they pay close attention to in-store screen ads, barely up from 14%, and interest in new-product messages on window screens fell from 44% to 39%.
Appetite is growing: 33% want more retail media on e-commerce sites and apps (from 29%) and 32% want more on in-store screens, though 25% would still prefer fewer ads online.
Grocery retailers' sites are gaining influence: 26% say their ads prompt a product search at least monthly, up from 22%.
body: Research firm iligo has published the fourth wave of its Baromètre Retail Media, a tracker launched in January 2024 to measure how French consumers perceive advertising run by retailers both online and in physical stores. Fieldwork took place from 29 September to 7 October 2026 among a sample of 2,011 people aged 18 to 69. The headline finding is that retail media is becoming more visible and more persuasive: 55% of respondents exposed online say these ads make them want to buy, four points more than in 2025, while weekly visits to e-commerce sites are stable at 46%.

Physical retail media is reaching more people. 34% now pass shop-window advertising screens at least weekly, up from 30%, and 32% visit shops or shopping centres equipped with in-store screens each week, up two points. But exposure is not translating into engagement: only 15% say they pay close attention to ads on in-store screens, against 14% a year earlier, and interest in new-product announcements on window screens has slipped from 44% to 39%.

On the digital side, grocery retailers' sites are the main gainers: 26% of respondents say their ads lead them to look up a product at least once a month, up from 22%, while generalist e-commerce sites gained just one point. Social media ads prompt 23% to buy at least monthly (from 20%). Consumers are increasingly open to the format, with 33% wanting more retail media on e-commerce sites and 32% more on in-store screens, but iligo stresses that expectations remain focused on promotions and tangible benefits. Its division director Hortense de Nantois describes a shift away from simply multiplying touchpoints towards making each interaction more useful.
items.relevance: The gap between rising reach and flat attention on in-store screens is a reminder that in-store DOOH needs relevant, offer-led creative to earn its place. Real-world media sellers can use the data to argue that screens close to the point of purchase work best when content is useful, not just present.

items.headline: Radio wins the most attention per gram of carbon, a UK attention-to-emissions study finds
items.dek: Ebiquity, Net Zero Media and Lumen propose a new attention-to-emissions ratio across TV, VOD, digital, OOH, print and radio, based on campaigns from ten UK advertisers.
items.source: Ebiquity, Net Zero Media and Lumen, A Metric for Effective & Responsible Advertising

figures.label: Print's estimated emissions per £1 vs study average
Top-ranked advertisers whose plans all included radio

keyPoints: Radio delivers the highest attention-to-emissions (A/E) ratio of six channels, according to a new study by Ebiquity, Net Zero Media and Lumen of campaigns from ten UK advertisers in 2024 and 2025.
The A/E ratio compares attention seconds bought per £1 of media with estimated grams of CO2e emitted per £1; TV ranked second and had the lowest estimated emissions per £1.
All six advertisers with the highest ratios used radio; none of the four lowest-ranked did.
Print scored lowest, with emissions per £1 estimated at 2.45 times the study average, though its sample covered only five advertisers.
Direct buying beat guaranteed deals and the open marketplace; the open marketplace generated the most attention per £1 but also the highest estimated emissions.
body: Effectiveness consultancy Ebiquity, carbon measurement firm Net Zero Media and attention specialist Lumen have proposed a new 'attention-to-emissions' (A/E) ratio, published on 12 November. It sets the attention seconds generated per £1 of media spend against the estimated grams of CO2-equivalent emissions per £1, so a higher score means more attention for less carbon. The analysis covers campaigns from ten UK advertisers run in 2024 and 2025 across TV, video on demand, digital, OOH, print and radio.

Radio came out on top, driven by delivering more attention seconds per pound than other channels; the six advertisers with the highest ratios all used radio, while none of the four lowest did. TV was second and had the lowest estimated emissions per £1. Digital had the second-lowest ratio overall, though digital audio scored well ahead of display and video. Print ranked last, with estimated emissions per £1 at 2.45 times the study average, but the researchers caution that the print sample covered only five advertisers. The coverage read did not give separate figures for OOH.

Buying method mattered too: direct buys had the highest A/E ratio, followed by preferred or guaranteed deals and then the open marketplace, which delivered the most attention per pound but also the highest estimated emissions, a gap Lumen's Mike Follett partly links to the energy demands of programmatic trading. Ebiquity's Paul Elliott stressed the results are not a ranking of channels to favour, and the authors describe them as directional, to be used alongside reach, brand and sales measures. The next step, Follett said, is to validate the link between attention and business outcomes.
items.relevance: Advertisers are starting to judge media on attention and carbon together, so OOH sellers should be ready with channel-specific attention and emissions data rather than relying on general sustainability claims. The finding that direct buying beats open-marketplace programmatic on this measure is worth noting for programmatic DOOH strategies.

pitch.line: Print's estimated emissions per £1 are 2.45 times the average, while radio delivers the most attention per gram of carbon across ten UK advertisers (Ebiquity, Net Zero Media and Lumen).

study.sample: Campaigns from 10 UK advertisers, 2024–2025, across TV, VOD, digital, OOH, print and radio

items.headline: German retailers bet on AI shopping agents, but only 14% use them yet, Salesforce finds
items.dek: Salesforce's fourth State of Commerce report finds that 77% of German commerce leaders see AI models as essential to product search within a year, while classic search discovery falls.
items.source: W&V, on Salesforce's State of Commerce report (4th edition)

figures.label: German retailers already using agentic AI
German commerce leaders who expect LLMs to be indispensable in product search within 12 months
Growth in agentic search as start of the customer journey (global, one year)
Fall in discovery via classic search, Aug 2025–May 2026

keyPoints: Only 14% of German retailers already use agentic AI, even though 77% of German commerce leaders expect large language models to be indispensable in product search within 12 months, Salesforce's State of Commerce report finds.
Worldwide, agentic search as the starting point of the customer journey grew 200% in a year.

Between August 2025 and May 2026, product discovery via classic search fell 15% and discovery directly at retailers and brands fell 7%, while new channels such as AI assistants, AI features in social apps and delivery apps grew 38%.
80% of German commerce leaders say AI is raising customer expectations and 43% find those expectations harder than ever to meet.
42% name introducing or expanding AI as their top strategic priority for next year.
body: Salesforce's fourth State of Commerce report, reported by W&V, highlights a gap between ambition and action among German retailers. 77% of German commerce leaders believe large language models will be indispensable for product search within 12 months, and 42% say introducing or expanding AI is their top strategic priority for next year. Yet only 14% of German retailers already use agentic AI, the autonomous assistants that can search, compare and buy on a shopper's behalf.

The wider data suggest the shift in discovery is already under way. Globally, agentic search as the first step of the customer journey grew by 200% in a year. Between August 2025 and May 2026, product discovery through classic search fell 15% and discovery directly at retailers and brands dropped 7%, while newer channels, including AI assistants, AI features inside social networks and delivery apps, grew 38%.

German commerce leaders also feel the pressure on service. 80% say AI is raising customer expectations, and 43% say those expectations are harder than ever to meet. W&V notes that hesitation may be partly justified, as not every AI investment pays off. Coverage did not give the report's sample size or methodology.
items.relevance: As discovery shifts from search boxes to AI agents, brands risk losing visibility at the moment of choice; channels that build memory and preference before a query is made become more important. Real-world media can position itself as a way to make sure a brand is the one shoppers ask their assistants for.

pitch.line: 77% of German commerce leaders expect AI models to be indispensable in product search within a year, but only 14% of retailers use agentic AI today (Salesforce State of Commerce).

items.headline: Half of Spain's online shoppers now use AI to buy, but Amazon still starts the search, IAB Spain finds
items.dek: IAB Spain's annual e-commerce study counts 27.9 million online buyers. AI is now the fifth-biggest product search channel, while Amazon remains the first place 53% of shoppers look.
items.source: IAB Spain and Elogia, Estudio Anual de Ecommerce 2026

figures.label: Used AI tools in at least one purchase in the past year
Use Amazon as a product search channel

keyPoints: Half of Spain's online shoppers used an AI tool in at least one purchase in the past year, rising to 58% of Gen Z, IAB Spain and Elogia's 2026 e-commerce study finds.
AI is now the fifth product search channel with 16% penetration, up seven points, but 83% want to keep control of the final purchase decision.
Amazon is the leading search channel (53%), ahead of Google and Bing (45%); 89% of Amazon searchers compare prices there and 63% of their online purchases end up on the platform.
Spain now has 27.9 million online buyers (77% of internet users), averaging 2.4 orders a month at a €64 basket; 26% buy almost everything online, up eight points.
Physical stores still matter: 78% expect to keep mixing online and in-store shopping and 54% have collected or returned an online order in a shop.
body: IAB Spain's annual e-commerce study, produced with consultancy Elogia and presented on 11 November, finds the Spanish online market has reached maturity. There are 27.9 million online shoppers aged 16 to 75, up from 27.4 million in 2025, a penetration of about 77% of internet users that has barely moved since 2022. Shoppers place an average of 2.4 orders a month with an average basket of €64. The share who buy almost everything online jumped eight points to 26%.

Artificial intelligence is the big change. Half of online shoppers used an AI tool in at least one purchase in the past year, mainly to resolve doubts and find product information (52%) or to compare features and alternatives (49%). Use peaks at 58% among Gen Z. AI has become the fifth product search channel with 16% penetration, up seven points, yet 83% want to keep the final decision themselves and only 17% would let an assistant prepare or complete a purchase. Among e-commerce professionals, 51% say adapting to AI agents is their main area for improvement.

Search is still dominated by Amazon, used by 53% of shoppers to look for products, ahead of Google and Bing at 45%; 89% of Amazon searchers compare prices on the platform. Free delivery is the most valued factor in choosing a store (43%), followed by price (40%), and 41% of those who abandoned a basket blame hidden costs. Returns are routine: 86% have returned an item, and 14% of returners admit to 'bracketing', ordering several sizes to keep one. Yet the channels are blending rather than replacing each other: 78% expect to keep combining online and physical shopping, and 54% have used a store to collect or return an online order.
items.relevance: With AI and Amazon shaping more of the online search journey, brands need ways to build demand before shoppers type a query. The persistence of mixed online and in-store shopping supports real-world media near stores and in shopping environments as part of omnichannel plans.

pitch.line: Half of Spain's 27.9 million online shoppers used AI in at least one purchase last year, but 78% still plan to mix online and in-store shopping (IAB Spain Estudio Ecommerce 2026).

items.headline: Most Italian brands sit in a 'zone of indifference', Havas finds, and desire is what pulls them out
items.dek: Havas's 'The Science of Desire' study says 84% of brands in Italy struggle to be chosen, while brands that grow attraction, affinity and attachment together are 2.4 times more likely to grow.
items.source: Havas, The Science of Desire

figures.label: Brands in Italy in the 'zone of indifference'
Likelihood of growth for brands improving all three desire levers
Likelihood of generating word of mouth and social mentions
More willing to pay a premium price

keyPoints: 84% of brands in Italy sit in a 'zone of indifference' where consumers find it hard to choose them, according to Havas's global 'The Science of Desire' study.
Brands that improve attraction, affinity and attachment at the same time are 2.4 times more likely than average to grow and 2.2 times more likely to generate word of mouth and social mentions.
The same brands are 1.9 times more likely to convert awareness into consideration, and consumers are 87% more willing to pay a premium for them.
Food, pharma and home care benefit most from attachment, while energy, telecoms and finance, seen as purely functional, have untapped potential to build attraction through innovation and service.
Havas proposes a 'Desire Score' to diagnose gaps, coordinated creative, media and data actions across the journey, and continuous measurement of desire's business impact.
body: Havas presented the Italian results of its proprietary global study 'The Science of Desire' at its Milan offices. The research treats desire as a measurable driver of brand growth, built on three levers: attraction (emotional magnetism and perceived superiority), affinity (alignment with a person's values and identity) and attachment (a bond built over time through habits and good experiences). Its starkest finding for Italy is that 84% of brands sit in what Havas calls the zone of indifference, where consumers struggle to choose between them.

Brands that manage to improve all three levers at once perform markedly better. Havas says they are 2.4 times more likely than average to grow, 2.2 times more likely to generate word of mouth and social mentions, and 1.9 times more likely to turn awareness into consideration, while consumers are 87% more willing to pay a premium price for them. Coverage of the study did not give its sample size or fieldwork details.

The levers matter differently by sector. Food, pharma and home care slot easily into daily life and gain most from attachment. Energy, telecoms and finance, which consumers see as purely functional, have high untapped potential and should prioritise attraction through innovation and service quality. Havas's chief strategy officer Francesca Casadei said desire becomes 'a concrete metric' for steering growth strategies, combining behavioural data with behavioural science. The agency's framework runs from a diagnostic 'Desire Score' to coordinated creative, media and data activity and ongoing measurement.
items.relevance: If most brands are interchangeable in consumers' eyes, the channels that build emotional distinctiveness and fame at scale become more valuable. OOH sellers can use the attraction and premium-price findings to argue for large-format, high-impact creative in functional categories such as energy, telecoms and finance.

pitch.line: 84% of brands in Italy sit in a 'zone of indifference', and brands that build desire on all fronts are 2.4 times more likely to grow (Havas, The Science of Desire).

items.pdfNote: Proprietary Havas study presented in Milan; no public report or Havas page found. Engage.it (10 November 2026) is the source read.

items.headline: India's D2C brands grow festive sales 45%, but Tier 3 towns carry the volume and one in five brands shrinks
items.dek: Shipping, commerce and ad data compiled by MediaNews4U shows brand websites outgrowing marketplaces this Diwali, while commerce-media budgets rose 27% and acquisition costs climbed.
items.source: MediaNews4U, on ClickPost, Unicommerce, Growster, Kearney and Datum Intelligence data

figures.label: Share of D2C shipments going to Tier 3 towns (ClickPost)
Commerce and retail media ad spend growth (Datum)

keyPoints: Indian D2C brands grew festive sales value 45%, and orders on brand websites rose 30% against 8% on marketplaces, but more than one in five brands saw shipments fall by over 25%.
Tier 3 towns took 45% of D2C shipments and Tier 2 cities 22%; 85% of festive orders were under ₹1,000.
Commerce and retail media ad spend rose about 27%, against 13–17% for festive advertising overall, and the cost of acquiring a D2C customer rose 15–20% to ₹600–650.
The top 10–15% of brands took nearly 65% of festive creator spend, and regional-language ads drew 38% more engagement than English creative.
body: India's 47-day festive season, from 20 September to 5 November, was good for direct-to-consumer brands on average, according to figures from several data firms compiled by MediaNews4U on 11 November. ClickPost puts the growth in D2C sales value at 45%. Unicommerce says orders on brand websites rose 30%, compared with 8% on marketplaces. Average order values moved in opposite directions: they rose about 14% in ClickPost's sample of around 400 brands but fell about 3% across Unicommerce's wider dataset, where 85% of festive orders were worth less than ₹1,000.

The averages hide a wide spread. In an early-sale analysis of 200 D2C brands, the typical brand's shipments grew about 19%. Nearly a third grew by more than 50%, but over one in five saw shipments drop by more than 25%. Small towns did much of the buying: Tier 3 towns took 45% of shipments and Tier 2 cities 22%. Growster says premium categories such as jewellery, skincare and wellness had bigger baskets, while mass-market baskets shrank.

Media got more expensive. Datum Intelligence estimates commerce and retail media spend rose about 27%, against 13–17% for festive advertising as a whole. Kearney puts the cost of acquiring a D2C customer up 15–20% at ₹600–650. Growster says acquisition cost per rupee of sales rose 19–24% for mass-market brands but only 1–5% for premium ones, and suggests that brands with too little fresh creative fell behind. Qoruz finds the top 10–15% of brands took nearly 65% of creator spend, and Admerly says regional-language ads drew 38% more engagement than English ones.
items.relevance: Festive growth in India is coming from Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns while performance-media costs climb, which supports broad-reach regional OOH and local-language creative. Retail and commerce media are taking a growing share of festive budgets, so OOH sellers should present their offer as complementary reach rather than compete on cost-per-click logic.

pitch.line: 45% of Indian D2C festive shipments went to Tier 3 towns this year, while commerce-media budgets rose 27% (ClickPost and Datum Intelligence, via MediaNews4U).

items.headline: 85% of Brazilian AI users now bring it into their shopping, but few let it decide, Troiano finds
items.dek: A Troiano and Nico.ag study of 1,200 Brazilians splits AI users into four shopper types and finds AI is used most to compare options, while the final choice stays with people.
items.source: Troiano and Nico.ag, As Faces da IA no Brasil

figures.label: Brazilian AI users who use it at some stage of the purchase journey
Use AI mainly to compare options

keyPoints: 85% of Brazilians who use generative AI use it at some point in their purchase journey, but only 4.5% say they always follow its recommendation.
Comparison is the heaviest use: 28% use AI to compare, 25% for research, 22% to find deals and 15% at the moment of purchase; comparison is the top use in 10 of 11 product categories.
Users fall into four types: 'IApédia' (38%), 'Faz-Tudo' or do-it-all (31%), 'Concierge' (20%) and 'BFF' (11%); 11% of Concierge users would let AI decide for them, versus 0.4% of IApédia users.
Too much choice (49%) and not knowing a category (46%) are the main reasons for turning to AI; mobile phones (31%), air tickets (16%) and cars (15%) are where people think it helps most.
body: Brand consultancy Troiano and agency Nico.ag combined 1,200 online interviews with Brazilians aged 18 to 55 who use AI, 20 ZMET interviews and 20 digital ethnography sessions for 'As Faces da IA no Brasil'. Meio & Mensagem reported the study on 6 November and Mundo do Marketing on 10 November. Its headline finding is that AI has become part of shopping: 85% of users apply it somewhere in the purchase journey. Most do so in the middle of the process, once they have seen a few options, and only 3% never use it for buying decisions.

Comparison is where AI matters most. 28% use it to compare products, 25% for research, 22% to find the best deal, 15% to buy and 9% after the sale. Comparison leads in 10 of the 11 categories studied. The main reasons are too many options (49%), not knowing the category (46%), lack of time (32%) and wanting to confirm a near-final choice (29%). Respondents see the most value in high-consideration purchases such as mobile phones (31%), airline tickets (16%) and cars (15%), and much less in everyday items like deodorant (2%).

The study sorts users into four types. 'IApédia' (38%) treats AI as an encyclopaedia, 'Faz-Tudo' (31%) uses it for everything, 'Concierge' (20%) hands it tasks, and 'BFF' (11%) treats it as a companion. People keep control of the decision: about 40% say AI narrows their options but leaves the choice to them, 34% say it raises their confidence without changing what they pick, and only 4.5% always do what it suggests. Even among Concierge users, just 11% would let AI choose for them.
items.relevance: AI is reshaping how Brazilians compare and shortlist products, but the decision still rests with people, so brand familiarity built before the comparison stage still counts. Real-world media can supply that familiarity and the reassurance shoppers seek when a category is unfamiliar or the choice is crowded.

pitch.line: 85% of Brazilian AI users now use it while shopping, yet only 4.5% always follow its advice (Troiano and Nico.ag, As Faces da IA no Brasil).

items.headline: Brazilians will pay up to three times more to save time, and quick top-up trips are rising, Scanntech finds
items.dek: Scanntech's retail data shows smaller households, pets and busier lives reshaping the Brazilian shopping basket, with quick shopping missions up 15% and weekly stock-up trips losing share.
items.source: Mundo do Marketing, on Scanntech data

figures.label: Price premium shoppers will pay for time-saving products
Spent for every 30 minutes saved on meal preparation
Quick or occasional shopping missions, share of trips (+15%)

keyPoints: Brazilian shoppers will pay up to three times more for products that save time, spending an average of R$26 for every 30 minutes saved on meal preparation, Scanntech finds.
Quick or occasional shopping missions now make up 27% of trips, up 15% on 2025, while weekly and stock-up missions together fell 1.9 points to a 55% share.
Year to date, fresh and animal proteins are up 5.5%, cat food 12.2% and specialised home cleaning 11.1%, while rice and beans fell 1.9% and infant products 11.7%.
Faster-to-prepare foods grew 3% in volume in the first quarter, while categories needing more kitchen time fell 2.5%.
body: Retail data firm Scanntech, whose figures Mundo do Marketing reported on 11 November, says Brazilian shoppers are trading money for time. Consumers will pay up to three times more for products that save them effort, and spend an average of R$26 for every 30 minutes they save on cooking. In the first quarter, faster-to-prepare foods grew 3% in volume, while categories that need more time in the kitchen fell 2.5%.

The way people shop is changing too. Quick or occasional missions now account for 27% of shopping trips, up 15% on 2025. Weekly and replenishment trips together still make up 55% of missions, but their share fell 1.9 points. In the year to date, compared with 2025, fresh and animal proteins rose 5.5%, specialised home cleaning 11.1% and cat food 12.2%, while basic cleaning slipped 1%, rice and beans fell 1.9% and infant products dropped 11.7%.

The article links these shifts to demographic data from IBGE: the average household shrank from 3.83 people in 2000 to 2.79 in 2022, one-person homes rose to 18.6% of households, and births fell to 2.4 million in 2024, the lowest since 2004. Brazil's pet population, meanwhile, reached about 161 million in 2023. Scanntech's Felipe Passarelli says brands need to adapt formats and assortments to smaller, more convenience-driven households.
items.relevance: More frequent, quicker shopping trips give brands more moments to reach Brazilian shoppers on the move, which favours OOH near convenience stores, transit and neighbourhood retail. Convenience, smaller pack sizes and pet care are the categories with momentum.

pitch.line: Brazilian shoppers will pay up to three times more for products that save them time, and quick shopping trips are up 15% (Scanntech, via Mundo do Marketing).

items.headline: South Africa's health and beauty market reaches R116.8bn as shoppers spread across stores and own labels
items.dek: Trade Intelligence's latest Health and Beauty Report finds a market growing 6.7% a year, with shoppers using several store types, relying on reviews and sticking with private labels.
items.source: Trade Intelligence (Ti), Health and Beauty Report

figures.label: South African health and beauty market, 2026
Township personal care shoppers using pharmacies or specialists

keyPoints: South Africa's health and beauty market is worth R116.8bn in 2026 and growing 6.7% a year, according to Trade Intelligence (Ti).
Shoppers spread their spending: health care shoppers use an average of 2.4 store types and personal care shoppers 2.2.
Nearly half of personal care shoppers say online reviews often or very often influence them, and two-thirds of health and personal care shoppers are holding or increasing private-label purchases.
In townships, 81% of personal care shoppers buy at pharmacies or specialist health and beauty retailers and 63% at supermarkets or hypermarkets; mass-market lines account for 84% of fragrance.
body: Trade Intelligence's latest Health and Beauty Report, reported by Bizcommunity on 11 November, values South Africa's health and beauty market at R116.8bn in 2026, growing 6.7% a year. Personal care accounts for just over half of spending. Health care is the smallest segment but is expected to grow fastest this year.

The shopper surveys show a fragmented, value-conscious path to purchase. Health care shoppers use an average of 2.4 types of store and personal care shoppers 2.2, so no single channel has them to itself. Nearly half of personal care shoppers say online reviews influence them often or very often. Two-thirds of health care and personal care shoppers are keeping or increasing their private-label purchases, which puts pressure on branded suppliers.

Township shoppers stand out. 81% of township personal care shoppers buy at pharmacies or specialist health and beauty retailers, and 63% use supermarkets or hypermarkets. In fragrance, mass-market products take 84% of the category, showing how much of the market is driven by price. Ti does not give the survey sample in the published summary.
items.relevance: With South African beauty shoppers moving between several store types and own labels gaining ground, brands need to stay visible close to pharmacies, malls and township retail hubs, not just online. Real-world media near those stores can reinforce brand choice at the point where shoppers compare branded and private-label products.

pitch.line: South Africa's R116.8bn health and beauty market is growing 6.7% a year, but two-thirds of shoppers are holding or raising private-label buying (Trade Intelligence).

items.headline: Ströer grows third-quarter revenue 4% as digital OOH rises 11% and classic posters slip
items.dek: Germany's biggest real-world media owner kept its 2026 outlook as digital screens and programmatic trading offset a 4.4% fall in classic OOH.
items.source: Ströer, Q3 2026 results and quarterly statement
keyPoints: Ströer's third-quarter group revenue rose 4% to €513m, with digital OOH up 11.0% to €102.5m and programmatic DOOH up 21.1%.
Classic OOH revenue fell 4.4% in the quarter while OOH services grew 34.2%; the OoH Media segment as a whole rose 3.6% to €245m.
Segment adjusted EBITDA in OOH slipped to €111m from €114m; group adjusted EBITDA was €148m, against €147m a year earlier.
Nine-month revenue reached €1,550m, up 5%, with organic growth of 2.1% after a 0.4% decline a year earlier.
Ströer confirmed its 2026 outlook and expects continued positive business in the fourth quarter.
body: Ströer reported third-quarter revenue of €513m, up from €491.5m a year earlier, and said digital OOH remained the main engine of its core business. In the OoH Media segment, digital revenue rose 11.0% to €102.5m and programmatically traded DOOH grew 21.1%, while classic poster revenue fell 4.4%. Segment revenue rose 3.6% to €245m, but segment adjusted EBITDA eased to €111m from €114m. Chief executive Udo Müller said digital OOH 'remains the most important growth driver of our core business'.

Elsewhere in the group, Digital & Dialog Media grew 15.7% to €239m, driven by a 30.4% jump in the Dialog business, while DaaS & E-Commerce revenue fell to €74m from €85m after Statista sold its consulting unit and weak consumer demand hit Asam. Group adjusted EBITDA was €148m (€147m) and adjusted net profit €35m (€34m). Over nine months, revenue rose 5% to €1,550m, organic growth was 2.1%, and operating cash flow improved to €258m.

Ströer confirmed the 2026 outlook set out in its annual report and expects positive business to continue in the fourth quarter. According to dpa-AFX, the outlook calls for organic growth in the low-to-mid single digits and largely stable adjusted EBITDA; the agency noted that operating profit beat analysts' forecasts while revenue fell slightly short.
items.relevance: Europe's largest listed national OOH player is now growing only through digital: programmatic DOOH grew twice as fast as DOOH overall while paper fell. Sellers can use the numbers as evidence that automated, data-led buying is pulling budget into real-world media; buyers should expect continued pressure on classic inventory pricing.

pitch.line: Programmatic DOOH revenue at Ströer, Germany's largest real-world media owner, grew 21.1% in Q3 2026, while classic OOH fell 4.4% (Ströer).

keyPoints: OUTFRONT's third-quarter revenue rose 9% to $511m, led by a 20% rise in transit and a 6% gain in billboards.
Billboard yield rose 9% to $3,318 and OIBDA grew 6% to $145m.
The company added 29 digital billboards during the quarter.

body: OUTFRONT Media grew third-quarter revenue by 9% to $511m, according to Billboard Insider's summary of the results. Transit revenue rose 20%, while billboard revenue rose 6%. Billboard yield, a measure of revenue per display, climbed 9% to $3,318. OIBDA increased 6% to $145m, and operating expenses rose 5% to $243m. The company added 29 new digital billboards in the quarter.

Chief executive Nick Brien said revenue momentum was strong and would accelerate into the fourth quarter, though no numerical guidance was reported. The figures follow Lamar Advertising's third-quarter update, in which revenue rose 6.6% to $625m, national revenue grew 20%, airport revenue 14% and local sales 4%; Lamar ended the quarter with 5,883 digital billboard faces and said political spending would top $40m for the year.
items.relevance: Both big US roadside and transit operators are growing faster than the wider ad market, with national budgets and transit doing the heavy lifting. Rising yields signal pricing power that international sellers can cite when making the case for premium urban and transit inventory.

items.headline: VIOOH opens GSTV's 29,000-site fuel-forecourt network to programmatic buyers
items.dek: Full-sound video at US petrol pumps, reaching 115 million adults a month, can now be bought through VIOOH's supply-side platform.
items.source: Billboard Insider, on VIOOH and GSTV
keyPoints: VIOOH has added GSTV's US fuel-retail video network, with screens at more than 29,000 fuel and convenience sites reaching 115 million adults a month, to its programmatic marketplace.
GSTV runs full-sound video in a non-skippable loop of about four minutes, roughly the length of a fill-up.
Retail partners include 7-Eleven, BP, Chevron, ExxonMobil, Shell, Speedway and Casey's.
VIOOH trades in 49 markets and connects to more than 50 demand-side platforms.
The deal comes in the same week VIOOH added Adams Outdoor's digital billboards to its marketplace.
body: VIOOH, the London-based DOOH supply-side platform, announced on 10 November that GSTV's national fuel-and-convenience network can now be bought programmatically through its existing workflow. GSTV screens sit at more than 29,000 retail locations, including 7-Eleven, Arco, BP, Casey's, Chevron, ExxonMobil, Shell, Speedway and Sunoco, and reach 115 million unique US adults a month. Content plays as full-sound video in a roughly four-minute non-skippable loop timed to a typical fill-up.

VIOOH's global chief commercial officer Gavin Wilson said GSTV brings 'a distinctive advertising environment' to programmatic DOOH. GSTV's head of programmatic, Evan Pfeffer, said the network reaches consumers when they are attentive and often close to a purchase. VIOOH says it trades in 49 markets with more than 50 DSPs; the GSTV deal lands in the same week that it opened Adams Outdoor's digital billboards to programmatic buyers.
items.relevance: Programmatic access to a captive, sound-on audience at the pump lets omnichannel video buyers extend reach into real-world media without a separate direct deal. For sellers, it raises the bar on what place-based networks must offer: audio, dwell time and proximity to purchase.

pitch.line: GSTV's screens at 29,000+ US fuel and convenience sites reach 115 million adults a month and are now bought programmatically via VIOOH (Billboard Insider).

items.headline: oOh!media adds digital billboards in Perth and keeps two council street-furniture contracts
items.dek: New Canning Highway screens and renewals in Cottesloe and South Perth arrive as the I Squared takeover awaits foreign-investment clearance.
items.source: oOh!media, company release

figures.label: Trips past new Como billboard (28 days)

keyPoints: oOh!media has renewed street-furniture contracts with the City of Cottesloe and the City of South Perth and is adding digital billboards on Perth's Canning Highway.
A new double-sided digital billboard in Como, about 5km from the CBD, passes 233,895 trips every 28 days; a second in Palmyra launches in early 2027.
The Ocean Reef Road supersite in Wanneroo has been upgraded to double-sided digital.
Thirteen digital panels are already live in Melville, with digital sites planned in Cottesloe's beachside precinct and South Perth.
The street-furniture network spans more than 1,000 assets across 120 suburbs and reaches 85% of Perth metro audiences each week.
body: oOh!media is digitising more of its Western Australian estate. It has opened a double-sided digital billboard on Canning Highway in Como, roughly 5km from Perth's CBD, which it says passes 233,895 trips every 28 days, and will open another on the same road in Palmyra in early 2027. An existing supersite on Ocean Reef Road in Wanneroo has been converted to double-sided digital. The company also renewed its street-furniture contracts with the City of Cottesloe and the City of South Perth; contract lengths were not disclosed.

The street-furniture network now has more than 1,000 assets in 120 suburbs and, oOh! says, reaches 85% of Perth metro audiences weekly. Thirteen digital panels are live in Melville, and new digital locations are planned in Cottesloe and South Perth. Chief commercial operating officer Robbie Dery called Western Australia 'an important market for us'. The expansion comes as the company's sale to I Squared Capital awaits Foreign Investment Review Board approval, with a decision deadline of 13 November and a second court hearing set for 18 November.
items.relevance: Council street-furniture renewals plus roadside digitisation is the standard growth playbook for national OOH owners; the Perth deal shows councils continuing to back long-term partners that add digital panels. Buyers gain more premium digital reach outside Australia's east-coast capitals.

steal.title: Show the receipts

items.headline: Fewer than half of marketers expect business to improve in 2027, WARC's Toolkit finds
items.dek: WARC's annual survey of more than 1,000 marketing executives shows optimism falling for a third year, as AI agents, a weakening social model and short-form video reshape 2027 plans.
items.source: WARC, The Marketer's Toolkit 2027

figures.label: Expect business conditions to improve in 2027
Expect consumers to use AI agents for product research within three years
Say social advertising is becoming less effective

keyPoints: Only 46% of marketers expect business conditions to improve in 2027, the third annual decline in a row and almost 20 points below the level of three years ago.

69% expect consumers to use AI agents for product research within three years, but only 8% expect shoppers to hand over purchases entirely; PHD and WARC put agent-facilitated spending at $944bn in 2026 and $3.4trn by 2030.

43% of advertisers say social advertising is becoming less effective, yet 58% say established buying practices make it hard to drop platforms; WARC Media still sees social spend rising 21.3% to $394.6bn in 2026.
83% call short-form video a popular consumer format, but 40% doubt it can match TV, film and events for brand building.
45% have not seriously considered how hotter summers could affect their category; only 25% have acted.
body: WARC's Marketer's Toolkit, now in its 16th year, is based on a global survey of more than 1,000 marketing executives conducted in September and October 2026, plus interviews with senior marketers. The mood has darkened again: 46% expect business conditions to improve next year, the third straight fall and nearly 20 points down on three years ago, although fewer respondents now expect budget cuts. WARC Media forecasts global advertising spend to grow 8.4% to $1.46trn in 2027, a slower pace than this year.

The report groups its findings into five trends. In the 'delegation economy', brands must appeal to AI systems as well as people: 69% of marketers expect consumers to use AI agents for product research within three years, though only 8% foresee full delegation of purchases. A 'post-social' era sees algorithms rather than friends deciding what audiences see; 43% of advertisers think social advertising is losing effectiveness, but 58% say buying habits make it hard to pull platforms from plans. In the 'clip economy', 83% see short-form video as popular, yet 40% question whether it can build brands like TV, film and live events.

The other two themes are climate and trust. 45% of marketers have not seriously considered how rising summer temperatures could change demand in their category, and a quarter have acted. On AI and effectiveness, opinion is split: 42% expect a positive impact, a similar share are unsure and 19% expect a negative one. P&G's Marc Pritchard argues brands need far more content to build memory 'in the algorithm', while Unilever's Selina Sykes warns against simply bolting AI onto old ways of working.
items.relevance: Growing doubts about social effectiveness and short-form video's brand-building power give real-world media a timely argument as a shared, unskippable brand channel in 2027 plans. As AI agents take over product research, sellers can position OOH as a way to build the brand memory that shapes what people, and their agents, ask for.

pitch.line: 43% of advertisers say social media advertising is becoming less effective, yet 58% find it hard to drop platforms from their plans (WARC Marketer's Toolkit 2027).

items.headline: Nearly six in ten senior marketers have made a major decision on faulty AI insight, GWI finds
items.dek: GWI's survey of 1,883 marketing, insight and agency leaders in the US, UK and Singapore finds AI is used daily but rarely checked, with outdated data and stereotyped audiences slipping into decisions.
items.source: GWI, Artificial Confidence: The AI Trust Gap

figures.label: Made a significant decision on AI insight later proved wrong
Report at least one negative business consequence
Verify AI insights most of the time

keyPoints: 58% of senior marketing, insight and agency professionals say they have made a significant business decision based on an AI insight that later proved wrong or misleading.
88% use AI tools every day and 80% often come across inaccurate or misleading AI findings, yet only 36% verify AI insights most of the time (43% in the US, 29% in the UK).
82% report at least one negative consequence, led by internal rework (38%), delayed decisions (36%) and customer complaints (34%); 27% cite financial loss.
63% have unknowingly acted on outdated data, and 72% say AI interfaces make old information look more relevant than it is.
70% say AI audience insights often rely on stereotypes, and 75% believe AI will never fully replace direct consumer research.
body: GWI surveyed 1,883 senior marketing, insight and agency professionals at companies with at least 500 staff or £20m in turnover: 850 in the US, 665 in the UK and 368 in Singapore. AI is now part of the daily routine for 88% of them, and 80% say they frequently encounter inaccurate, misleading or untrue AI-generated findings. The headline result is that 58% have made a significant business decision on the strength of an AI insight that turned out to be wrong; an earlier preview of a smaller sample, published in September, had put the share at 72%.

The damage is mostly operational but not trivial. 82% report at least one negative consequence: internal rework (38%), delayed decisions (36%), customer complaints (34%), financial loss (27%), reputational damage (26%) and weaker campaign performance (21%). Although 85% rate decisions based on inaccurate AI as a significant risk, only 36% verify AI insights most of the time, with Americans (43%) more diligent than Britons (29%); 36% cross-check with another AI tool rather than a primary source.

Stale data is a particular blind spot: 63% admit to unknowingly acting on outdated information and 72% say AI interfaces make old data seem current. 70% think AI-generated audience insights lean on stereotypes rather than real behaviour. Most still see a role for people: 80% say understanding motivations requires human research, and 75% say AI will never fully replace talking to consumers. GWI, which sells survey-based audience data, has an obvious commercial interest in that conclusion.
items.relevance: Buyers are learning to question AI-generated audience claims, so media owners that can show where their audience data comes from, how fresh it is and how it is validated will have an edge. For OOH, independently audited audience currencies and human-validated research are a selling point, not a footnote.

pitch.line: 58% of senior marketers have made a significant business decision based on AI insight that later proved wrong, yet only 36% routinely verify it (GWI, Artificial Confidence).

items.headline: Brands think customers love their AI service; only half of consumers agree, Twilio finds
items.dek: Twilio's survey of 7,652 online shoppers and 660 business leaders in 18 countries finds a wide gap between how companies rate their AI agents and how customers experience them.
items.source: Twilio, Customer Insights Series 2026: The AI Expectations Gap

figures.label: Companies that think customers are satisfied with AI service
Consumers who have tried to bypass AI agents
Consumers who want AI agents to identify themselves

keyPoints: 86% of companies believe customers are satisfied with their AI-powered customer service, but only 51% of consumers say AI interactions are satisfactory.
AI agents already handle half of customer service interactions, a share businesses expect to reach 63% by 2027.
76% of consumers want an AI agent to say it is an AI at the start of a conversation, but only 32% of businesses prioritise AI transparency.
78% of consumers have tried to get around an AI agent to reach a human, and 63% want an easy route to a live person at any time.
73% of brands think consumers want more human-like AI, against 54% of consumers; 91% of consumers say personalised AI interactions feel more real.
body: Twilio's Customer Insights Series surveyed 7,652 consumers who had bought online in the previous six months and 660 director-level business leaders at companies with 500 or more staff, across 18 markets including the US, UK, France, Germany, Spain, Italy, Brazil, Mexico, India, Japan and Australia, between 9 April and 1 May 2026. Its central finding is a perception gap: 86% of companies believe customers are happy with AI-powered service, while just 51% of consumers agree.

The gap matters because AI agents are already doing much of the work, handling half of service interactions today and an expected 63% by 2027. Consumers want transparency and an exit: 76% want an AI agent to identify itself up front, but only 32% of businesses make AI transparency a priority, and 78% of consumers have tried to bypass an AI agent to reach a person. Companies also overestimate appetite for human-like bots (73% of brands against 54% of consumers), although 91% of consumers say personalised AI interactions feel more real and 64% think chatbots have improved over the past year. Nearly all companies (99%) say major challenges stop them fully understanding their customers.
items.relevance: As brands hand more customer contact to AI, the human, physical touchpoints of a brand become more valuable for trust; marketers should check that the promise made in advertising survives the service experience. Clear disclosure of AI use is becoming a basic expectation in every channel.

items.headline: AI-assisted shoppers are likelier to buy on Black Friday, but delivery decides the basket, DHL finds
items.dek: DHL eCommerce's survey of 29,000 online shoppers in 29 countries finds 41% buy on Black Friday, while poor delivery and returns options remain the main reason baskets are abandoned.
items.source: DHL eCommerce, 2026 Black Friday Trend Report

figures.label: Online shoppers who buy on Black Friday
AI-assisted shoppers who bought on Black Friday
Would abandon without preferred delivery option
E-commerce businesses running Black Friday promotions

keyPoints: Half of shoppers who use AI to help them shop bought on Black Friday, against 42% of deal seekers and 41% of online shoppers overall.
84% of e-commerce businesses run Black Friday promotions, far more than the 41% of shoppers who actually buy on the day.

81% would abandon a purchase without their preferred delivery option and 74% without their preferred returns option; one Black Friday shopper in three is most likely to drop out at the shipping-options stage.
77% would not shop with a brand they did not trust to handle delivery or returns, and 45% want more pick-up and drop-off points away from home.
91% of Gen Z shoppers say they trust retailers' offers and prices during seasonal sales moments.
body: DHL eCommerce surveyed 29,000 online shoppers, about 1,000 per country in 29 countries, and 5,800 e-commerce businesses in 28 countries between December 2025 and February 2026. The result is a reminder that Black Friday is bigger for sellers than for buyers: 84% of businesses run promotions, but 41% of online shoppers purchase on the day itself. AI is changing who converts: half of shoppers who use AI assistants bought on Black Friday, compared with 42% of self-described deal seekers.

The decisive moment comes late in the journey. One Black Friday shopper in three is most likely to abandon at the point of choosing shipping, 81% would walk away without their preferred delivery option and 74% without their preferred returns option. Trust in fulfilment matters as much as price: 77% would not buy from a brand they did not trust to handle delivery or returns, and 45% want more collection and return locations away from home, such as lockers and pick-up points. Younger shoppers are the most receptive to seasonal offers, with 91% of Gen Z saying they trust retailers' prices during these events.
items.relevance: With most retailers fighting for a minority of Black Friday buyers, brands need to win consideration before the day and remove friction at checkout; delivery and returns promises are worth putting in the ad, not just the small print. AI-assisted shoppers convert better, so being the brand people already know when the agent searches is the real prize, which favours broad-reach brand media in the weeks before.

items.headline: NBA team brands jump 34% to $14.2bn and overtake the Premier League's, Brand Finance finds
items.dek: A $76bn media deal lifted every NBA franchise's brand value this year, putting the league's 30 teams ahead of England's top-flight football clubs, though still well behind the NFL.
items.source: Brand Finance, NBA 2026 ranking

figures.label: Combined brand value of 30 NBA franchises (+34%)
Combined brand value of 20 Premier League clubs
Most valuable NBA brand: Golden State Warriors

keyPoints: The 30 NBA franchises are now worth a combined $14.2bn in brand value, up 34%, overtaking the 20 English Premier League clubs at $11.3bn.
Every franchise grew, by between 14% and 88%, after an 8% fall in 2025; the catalyst was a 39% jump in league broadcasting revenue from the $76bn ESPN, NBC and Amazon deal.
The Golden State Warriors remain the most valuable brand for a fifth year at $1.4bn, ahead of the Los Angeles Lakers ($1.3bn) and the champion New York Knicks ($1.1bn, up 51%).
The Atlanta Hawks are the fastest risers, up 88% and nine places to sixth; the Lakers are the league's strongest brand.
The NFL still leads US sport at $28.6bn; the NBA is almost seven times the size of MLS ($2.1bn).
body: Brand Finance's annual NBA valuation puts the combined brand value of the league's 30 franchises at $14.2bn, up 34% and now ahead of the 20 Premier League clubs ($11.3bn). Every team grew, by between 14% and 88%, reversing an 8% decline last year. The driver was money from the new $76bn media agreement with ESPN, NBC and Amazon, which lifted league broadcasting revenue by 39%; combined franchise revenues for the 2025 season were just under $12.5bn and enterprise value rose to $175.6bn.

The Golden State Warriors are the most valuable brand for the fifth year running at $1.4bn (+14%), followed by the Los Angeles Lakers at $1.3bn (+34%) and the New York Knicks, who passed $1bn (+51%) after their first title in 53 years. The Atlanta Hawks grew fastest, up 88% to $525m. Four teams earned Brand Finance's top AAA+ strength rating, with the Lakers strongest; the Boston Celtics have the highest fan engagement at 22% against a league average of 12%.

Brand Finance notes that only a handful of teams are well known outside the US, but says bids of $500m or more in each of the 12 European cities targeted for a planned NBA European league show strong appetite, while warning of a clash with the EuroLeague, whose clubs have rejected a merger. Values are calculated with the ISO 10668-compliant royalty-relief method.
items.relevance: Media-rights money is turning US sports franchises into bigger brands, and the NBA's planned European league would bring that machinery to 12 European cities. Sponsors and real-world media owners near arenas and in transit hubs of candidate cities should watch for new event and fan-zone inventory.

items.headline: Britons want proof of past prices before they trust early Black Friday deals, YouGov finds
items.dek: Most British bargain-hunters now mix early-November offers with event-day shopping, but the chance of a bigger discount later keeps many waiting, and price transparency is the strongest lever to get them buying sooner.
items.source: YouGov, Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2026 survey

figures.label: Britons who take part in seasonal sales
Sales shoppers mixing early deals and event days
Would buy early if shown price history
Event-day shoppers who expect the biggest discounts then

keyPoints: 85% of British sales shoppers say seeing a product's price history would encourage them to buy in early-November deals rather than wait for Black Friday.
44% of Britons take part in seasonal sales; of these, 72% shop both early offers and the main event, 14% wait for Black Friday and Cyber Monday and 10% shop only early.
Among those who hold out for the event days, 45% expect the deepest discounts then, 39% are waiting for a specific item from a specific retailer and 18% doubt early deals are genuine.
Advance notice of discounts (81%), a refund if the Black Friday price turns out lower (78%) and visible stock levels (60%) would also pull purchases forward.
Only 21% of sales shoppers think early deals are better than Black Friday's; 49% see no difference.
body: YouGov polled 2,021 British adults on 5 and 6 November to see whether the stretched-out discount season is changing behaviour. Some 44% take part in seasonal sales, and the clear majority of them (72%) no longer pick sides: they buy in early-November promotions and on Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Only 14% hold out solely for the event days, and 10% shop only the early offers.

The reasons for waiting are mostly about value and trust. Among event-day shoppers, 45% expect the biggest discounts on the day, 39% are waiting for a particular product from a particular retailer and 18% doubt that early-sale reductions are real. Early shoppers, by contrast, want to get their buying done (44%), find a good deal (33%) or spread spending across the month (30%). Judgements on value are split: 21% think early deals are better, 15% think they are worse and 49% see little difference.

Retailers have clear levers. Asked what would encourage them to buy early, 85% cited transparency on price history, 81% advance notice of discounts, 78% a refund if the Black Friday price turned out lower and 60% visible stock levels. The findings suggest that proof, not just promotion, now drives the timing of purchases.
items.relevance: Retailers stretching promotions across November should put reference prices, price guarantees and stock levels into the creative, not just the discount. Digital OOH near stores and on high streets can carry that live price and stock messaging, which suits the early-November weeks when hesitant shoppers are deciding whether to wait.
