items.headline: French households raise their Christmas budget by €90 to €581, but plan fewer gifts
items.dek: The tenth Cofidis–CSA Research barometer finds festive spending intentions rebounding from a low 2025, even as worry about the economy jumps and shoppers start earlier and cut back on extras.
items.source: Cofidis and CSA Research, Les Français et Noël barometer (10th edition)
keyPoints: French households plan to spend an average of €581 on Christmas this year, €90 more than in 2025, yet expect to buy seven gifts rather than nine.
The median budget rises to €400 from €350; gifts account for €340 (from €297), the meal for €132 and travel for €33.
62% fear the economic climate will affect their festivities, up from 48%, rising to 77% of under-35s; among the worried, 58% cite fuel prices, against 24% a year ago.
72% start buying before December, five points more than last year, and 32% begin in October.
28% use or plan to use AI to organise Christmas, including 55% of under-35s, mostly for gift ideas (56%) and budget optimisation (43%).
body: The tenth edition of Cofidis's Christmas barometer, run by CSA Research among 1,009 adults online on 6–8 October, shows spending intentions bouncing back after a weak 2025. The average planned budget reaches €581, up €90, and the median rises €50 to €400, a gap that points to a group of high spenders pulling the average up. Gifts remain the main item at €340, up from €297, but households expect to buy seven of them rather than nine, and 30% say they prefer fewer, more expensive presents. The meal budget edges up to €132 and travel to €33.

Confidence has not followed spending. 62% fear the economic context will weigh on the holidays, up from 48% in 2025, and the share rises to 77% among under-35s and 71% among the least well-off. Food prices (72%) and fuel (58%, more than double last year's 24%) are the main worries. A third (33%) plan to spend less than last year, up from 23%; clothing (26%) and decorations (20%) are the first items to be cut. 63% say Christmas weighs heavily on their budget, and 62% save during the year to pay for it.

Shopping is starting earlier. 72% begin buying before December, five points more than last year, 32% start in October and 37% plan to use promotional events. AI is becoming part of the routine: 28% use or plan to use it to prepare Christmas, rising to 55% of under-35s, mainly for gift ideas, budget optimisation and meal planning. The survey measures declared intentions in October, not actual spending.
items.relevance: With seven in ten French shoppers buying before December and a third starting in October, festive campaigns, including OOH near shopping centres and on commuter routes, need to be live from early November rather than peaking in mid-December. Messages on value and fewer, better gifts fit a mood in which budgets rise but anxiety rises faster.

items.headline: Nivea tops German beauty rankings for quality, but dm's own-label Balea wins on value, YouGov finds
items.dek: YouGov's 2026 Health & Beauty Rankings, built from a year of daily BrandIndex interviews, show retailer brands closing in on manufacturer names as German shoppers weigh price against quality.
items.source: YouGov, Health & Beauty Rankings 2026 (BrandIndex)

figures.label: German cosmetics and personal care sales

keyPoints: Nivea is the brand German consumers most often consider for their next health and beauty purchase (51.9%), but dm's own-label Balea leads on value for money, 13.4 points ahead.
Balea is second on consideration (45.0%), ahead of Oral-B (34.7%), Nivea MEN (31.3%), Dove (30.7%) and Colgate (30.5%).
Nivea leads on perceived quality with a net score of 50.7, 11.6 points clear of Oral-B; Weleda and L'Oréal Paris make the quality top ten without reaching the consideration top ten.
Retailer and low-price brands, including Rossmann's Isana, rank strongly on value; only Nivea, Balea, Oral-B and Dove sit near the top on both quality and value.
The German cosmetics and personal care market is worth about €13.5bn, up 2.8%, with facial care up 4.0% and hair care 3.4%.
body: YouGov ranked 53 health and beauty brands in Germany using its BrandIndex tracker, which interviews a representative sample of adults online every day; each brand was rated by 7,700 to 7,900 people between October 2025 and September 2026. Three measures were used: consideration (whether a brand is in the shopper's set for the next purchase), and net scores for perceived quality and for value for money. YouGov's shopper panel puts the domestic cosmetics and personal care market at about €13.5bn, up 2.8% year on year.

Nivea dominates. It is considered by 51.9% of consumers and has the highest quality score (50.7), well ahead of Oral-B (39.1) and Gillette (36.9). But the drugstore chain dm's own brand Balea is close behind on consideration at 45.0% and leads the value-for-money ranking with a net score of 43.8, 13.4 points ahead of Nivea; Isana is third. Established names such as Weleda and L'Oréal Paris appear in the quality top ten but not the consideration top ten, suggesting a reputation that does not always translate into the shopping list.

Only four brands, Nivea, Balea, Oral-B and Dove, appear near the top on both quality and value, and Nivea and Balea are both in the top five for each. A second part of the ranking looks at heavy drugstore buyers and at women across generations.
items.relevance: Retailer own-labels now compete with the biggest manufacturer brands on consideration, not only on price, which raises the stakes for branded beauty advertisers at the point of sale and on drugstore retail media networks. Manufacturer brands that lead on quality but lag on consideration need broad-reach brand building to get onto the shopping list.

items.headline: Italian OOH grows 9% in nine months while the wider ad market barely moves, Nielsen finds
items.dek: Nielsen's Ad Intel figures to September show Italian advertising up just 0.5% for the year, with outdoor, transit and GO TV screens among the few traditional media still growing as TV, radio and print slip.
items.source: Engage, on Nielsen Ad Intel data for Italy
keyPoints: OOH advertising in Italy grew 9% in the first nine months of 2026 and GO TV screens 16.6%, while the total market rose just 0.5% and TV fell 1.6%.
September alone was up 0.2%, with OOH up 5% and GO TV up 15%.
Excluding search, social, classifieds and OTT, the market is down 1.9% for the year; Nielsen's total web estimate is up 3.3%.
Print and radio keep falling: daily newspapers -6.6%, magazines -7.5%, radio -3.6% and direct mail -10.9% over nine months; cinema is up 66.4% from a small base.
In September, public bodies (+29.7%) and finance and insurance (+22.5%) spent more, while travel (-23.1%) and drinks and alcohol (-20.8%) cut back.
body: Nielsen's latest Ad Intel estimates put Italian advertising investment up 0.2% in September and 0.5% for January to September 2026. Stripping out Nielsen's estimates for search, social, classifieds and OTT, the market is down 1.9% over the period. Nielsen Italia's managing director, Luca Bordin, described the sector as broadly holding up, helped by television avoiding any structural reversal, against a backdrop of falling consumer and business confidence.

Real-world media is one of the brighter spots. OOH, which Nielsen reports as outdoor and transit combined, grew 5% in September and 9% over nine months, and GO TV, Italy's OOH TV screen networks, rose 15% in the month and 16.6% for the year to date. Television fell 1.7% in September and 1.6% cumulatively, while daily newspapers (-6.6%), magazines (-7.5%), radio (-3.6%) and direct mail (-10.9%) declined. Cinema jumped 66.4%, though from a much smaller base. Nielsen's estimate for the total web universe grew 3.3%, but the narrower perimeter measured by FCP-AssoInternet fell 3.2%.

By sector, 13 categories grew in September, led by public bodies and institutions (+29.7%), finance and insurance (+22.5%) and industry and construction (+10.1%). Travel and tourism (-23.1%), household goods (-21.9%) and drinks and alcohol (-20.8%) cut spending most sharply.
items.relevance: In a flat Italian market, OOH and GO TV screen networks are taking share from TV, radio and print, which supports the case for shifting reach budgets into real-world media for 2027. Sellers can point to finance and public-sector advertisers, which are increasing spend, while travel and drinks brands pull back.

pitch.line: OOH advertising in Italy grew 9% in the first nine months of 2026, while the total market rose just 0.5% and TV fell 1.6% (Nielsen Ad Intel).

items.headline: Dutch OOH set to grow up to 12.5% this year as WPP Media raises its Netherlands forecast
items.dek: WPP Media now expects Dutch advertising to grow 8–10% in 2026 and 6–9% in 2027, with retail media and OOH, lifted by programmatic DOOH, the fastest-growing channels.
items.source: Marketing Report, on WPP Media's This Year Next Year forecast for the Netherlands
keyPoints: Dutch OOH advertising is forecast to grow 10.5–12.5% in 2026, outpacing pure digital (9.5–11.5%) and video (4–6%), with programmatic DOOH credited as a driver.
WPP Media has raised its 2026 forecast for the Dutch ad market to 8–10% growth from 5–8%, and expects 6–9% in 2027.
Retail media is the fastest-growing channel, at 17–19% this year and 14.5–17.5% next year.
OOH is expected to grow a further 7–10% in 2027; audio slows to between -0.5% and 2.5%, and print is roughly flat to slightly down.
WPP Media's chief investment officer argues that all the market's growth now comes from digital.
body: Remon Buter, chief investment officer of WPP Media in the Netherlands, used the agency's This Year Next Year event in Amsterdam to raise his forecast for Dutch advertising. He now expects growth of 8–10% in 2026, up from the 5–8% he predicted earlier, and 6–9% in 2027. In his reading, all of that growth is coming from digital channels.

Retail media leads, with forecast growth of 17–19% this year and 14.5–17.5% in 2027. OOH is next, at 10.5–12.5% in 2026 and 7–10% in 2027, a performance the report links partly to the spread of programmatic buying in digital OOH. Pure digital is forecast at 9.5–11.5% and 7.5–10.5%, video (TV, catch-up and streaming) at 4–6% and 3–6%, and audio at 1.5–3.5% this year before flattening to between -0.5% and 2.5% next year. Newspapers and magazines are expected to be roughly flat to slightly down.

Buter also called for TV and online video to be planned in a single currency, probably cost per thousand, to replace the split between GRPs and CPMs. He cited Sweden's cross-platform TV measurement and the Dutch Screenforce and NMO cross-media research as models.
items.relevance: A double-digit OOH forecast in one of Europe's most digitally mature markets shows how programmatic DOOH is pulling real-world media into digital budgets. OOH sellers in other markets can use the Dutch figures to argue that automated, data-led OOH grows alongside retail media rather than competing with it.

pitch.line: Dutch OOH ad spend is forecast to grow 10.5–12.5% in 2026, ahead of pure digital (9.5–11.5%) and video (4–6%), helped by programmatic DOOH (WPP Media Netherlands).

report.label: WPP Media: This Year Next Year forecasts

items.headline: Four in five Americans would host the holidays at home rather than travel to save money, Barclays finds
items.dek: Barclays' holiday spending and travel poll finds Americans trimming trips and everyday spending rather than skipping family gatherings, while more young adults lean on their parents to pay.
items.source: Barclays, 2026 Holiday Spending & Travel Pulse Survey

figures.label: Would host at home rather than travel to save money
Have skipped, or would skip, a gathering because of cost
Gen Z and Millennials whose parents help with holiday costs (from 26%)
Rewards cardmembers tapping points for the holidays

keyPoints: Americans are cutting back rather than cutting out the holidays: 79% would host at home instead of travelling to save money, and 82% say family gatherings are worth the time and cost.
Cost is the top pressure: 57% name travel or gift costs among their biggest holiday stressors, and 56% have skipped, or would skip, a gathering because of the expense.
Before giving up a gathering, 78% would cut everyday spending and 74% would shorten a trip or use rewards points.
37% of Gen Z and Millennials say parents are helping with holiday costs, up from 26%, mostly for meals and hosting (53%), gifts (40%) and flights (37%).
63% of rewards cardmembers are saving or redeeming points for the season, chiefly on gifts (35%), hotels (34%), fuel (33%) and flights (30%).
body: Barclays' annual Holiday Spending & Travel Pulse Survey, run with WPP's Burson among 1,002 US adults in mid-September, finds that affordability is reshaping the season rather than cancelling it. Some 57% cite the cost of travel or gifts among their top stressors and 56% have skipped, or would skip, a gathering on cost grounds. Yet 82% still say being with family is worth the time and money, and most would rather economise elsewhere: 79% would host at home instead of travelling, 78% would cut everyday spending and 74% would shorten a trip or use points before missing an event.

The squeeze is shifting costs across generations. 37% of Gen Z and Millennial respondents say parents are helping to pay for the holidays, up from 26% a year earlier, with help concentrated on meals and hosting (53%), gifts (40%) and flights (37%); a quarter of those receiving help say they feel guilty about it. Among parents of adult children, 38% are contributing, roughly flat on last year. Loyalty currencies are also doing more work: 63% of rewards cardmembers are saving, planning to redeem or already redeeming points, most often on gifts, hotels, petrol and flights.

The survey also captures the limits of togetherness: 34% say they reach breaking point with extended family within four hours of arriving, and 52% would feel guilty skipping a gathering for their own holiday.
items.relevance: A stay-closer, host-at-home season favours local reach: grocery, home and drive-time retail messaging around suburban routes and shopping centres should work harder than destination-led travel campaigns. Travel and card brands can lean on points and short-break offers to win the trips that do happen.

pitch.line: 79% of Americans would host the holidays at home rather than travel to save money, and 74% would shorten a trip before skipping a gathering (Barclays Holiday Spending & Travel Pulse Survey).

items.headline: Only 17% of Mexican households bought tech or durables in El Buen Fin, NielsenIQ finds
items.dek: NielsenIQ's review of last year's Buen Fin shows category sales up 12.9% as online grew 42% and stores slipped, while one non-buyer in six doubted the offers were real.
items.source: Merca2.0, on NielsenIQ data

figures.label: Households that bought tech or durables during El Buen Fin
Value sales growth, tech and durables
Online sales growth, tech and durables
Physical store sales, tech and durables

keyPoints: Only 17% of Mexican households bought technology or durable goods during El Buen Fin 2025, ranging from 25% of high-income households to 12% of low-income ones.
Tech and durables sales rose 12.9% in value, but the growth was online (+42%) while physical stores fell 5%.
Among non-buyers, 43% said they did not need anything, 23% had other spending priorities, 19% lacked cash and 16% believed the offers were not real.
In supermarkets, large-appliance sales were 352% above an average week, with 76% of washing machines and 71% of refrigerators on discount.
Online, whisky (+323%) and tequila (+263%) were among the fastest-growing categories.
body: Ahead of this year's El Buen Fin, Mexico's flagship discount weekend, NielsenIQ data reported by Merca2.0 suggest the event is narrower than its reputation. Only 17% of households said they bought technology or durable goods during the 2025 edition; participation was 25% among high-income households and 12% among low-income ones. Category sales still rose 12.9% in value, but entirely through e-commerce: online sales of tech and durables grew 42% while physical stores lost 5%.

Of the 83% who stayed out, 43% said they did not need the products, 23% had other priorities, 19% lacked immediate cash, 16% thought the offers were not genuine and 8% found them unattractive. Where shoppers did buy, the peaks were steep: in the supermarket channel, large appliances sold 352% more than in an average week, pots, pans and batteries 212% more, small appliances 169%, car tyres 105% and toys 52%, helped by deep promotion (76% of washing machines and 71% of refrigerators were discounted). Online, spirits stood out, with whisky up 323% and tequila 263%. Merca2.0 does not detail NielsenIQ's sample or method.
items.relevance: El Buen Fin concentrates demand among better-off households and online, so advertisers should target reach and credibility rather than blanket discount messaging; one in six non-buyers doubt the deals. With store sales slipping, retailers can use OOH near shopping centres and on commuter routes to steer the online-researching shopper back to physical outlets.

pitch.line: Only 17% of Mexican households bought tech or durable goods during El Buen Fin, as online sales in the category rose 42% and stores fell 5% (NielsenIQ, via Merca2.0).

items.headline: Six in ten Brazilians have felt sad scrolling social media, and 69% want AI-made content labelled
items.dek: A national survey by happiness researcher Renata Rivetti and Instituto IDEIA finds heavy screen use, passive scrolling and growing emotional reliance on AI, alongside strong support for transparency and age limits.
items.source: Mundo do Marketing, on research by Renata Rivetti and Instituto IDEIA

figures.label: Have felt sad or unhappy while on social media
Spend more than four hours a day on social and messaging apps
Want AI-made content to be labelled
Have believed content later found to be AI-made

keyPoints: 61.8% of Brazilian adults have felt sad or unhappy while consuming social media content, rising to 76% among 18–24-year-olds.
42.9% spend more than four hours a day on social networks and messaging apps, and 32.2% spend almost all that time watching others' posts without interacting.
65.8% have believed content they later discovered was AI-generated, and 69.2% want AI-made content to be labelled.
63.9% use AI routinely; 35.6% of users turn to it at least weekly for emotional conversation or advice.
53.5% tried to cut back on phone or social media use in the past year, and 62% back a minimum age of 16 for social media accounts.
body: A national survey of 1,542 adults, run from 2 to 4 October by Renata Rivetti, a researcher in the science of happiness and human relationships, with Instituto IDEIA, paints a picture of Brazilians who are heavily connected but often worse for it. 42.9% spend more than four hours a day on social networks and messaging apps, and 61.8% say they have felt sad or unhappy while consuming content there, a figure that rises to 76% among 18–24-year-olds, 77.5% of whom say they compare their lives with others. Much of the time is passive: 32.2% spend almost all of it watching others' posts without interacting. Half check their phone within 15 minutes of waking (50.3%) and more than half use it in the half-hour before bed (54.7%); 53.5% tried to cut back in the past year.

AI is now part of daily life: 63.9% use it routinely, 59.1% say it saves them time, and 35.6% of users turn to it at least weekly for emotional conversation or advice, with 32.1% saying they have felt more understood by AI than by people close to them. Trust is the fault line. Although 73.2% of those aware of AI think they can spot AI-made material, 65.8% have believed content that turned out to be artificial; 69.2% want such content labelled and 66% want companies to disclose when AI is used in decisions about people. Majorities also support a minimum age of 16 for social media accounts (62%) and a right to ignore work messages out of hours (56.1%). Rivetti argues the challenge is not choosing between people and technology.
items.relevance: Screen fatigue and passive scrolling mean time spent online overstates real attention and goodwill; non-intrusive, shared real-world media offers brands a less emotionally loaded context. Advertisers using generative AI in creative should label it, since undisclosed AI content risks the credibility consumers say they now demand.

pitch.line: 61.8% of Brazilian adults have felt sad or unhappy while on social media, rising to 76% among 18–24s (Renata Rivetti and Instituto IDEIA, national survey of 1,542 adults).

items.headline: Indians booked 38.5% more restaurant tables on Diwali Day, Swiggy data shows
items.dek: Swiggy's festive figures show food delivery up 10.7% over the Diwali weekend, but the sharper growth came from people going out to eat, in metros and in emerging cities alike.
items.source: Medianews4u, on Swiggy platform data

figures.label: Dineout reservations, Diwali Day (year on year)
Food delivery orders, Diwali weekend (year on year)
Dineout reservations, Diwali Eve (year on year)
Average food orders per hour over the weekend

keyPoints: Restaurant reservations through Swiggy's Dineout jumped 38.5% year on year on Diwali Day, far outpacing the 10.7% rise in food delivery orders over the festive weekend.
Swiggy handled an average of 97,545 food orders an hour across 6–8 November, compared with the 2025 Diwali period of 18–20 October.
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Delhi and Chennai led dining-out bookings, with Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Chandigarh the top emerging markets.
Masala dosa, kaju katli and paneer butter masala were the most-ordered dishes; kaju katli topped sweets ahead of motichoor ladoo, rasgulla and gulab jamun.
Group occasions stood out, from a Mumbai restaurant bill of INR 1,34,210 to 30-person bookings in Surat and Ahmedabad.
body: Swiggy's Diwali figures, comparing the festive weekend of 6–8 November with the equivalent 2025 period of 18–20 October, point to a festival celebrated increasingly outside the home. Food delivery orders rose 10.7% year on year, averaging 97,545 an hour over the three days, but restaurant reservations made through Swiggy's Dineout service grew faster: up 7.4% on Diwali Eve and 38.5% on Diwali Day itself.

Dining-out demand was led by Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Delhi and Chennai, while Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Chandigarh were the strongest emerging markets. Group celebrations featured prominently, with one Mumbai party running up a bill of INR 1,34,210 and bookings for 30 people recorded in both Surat and Ahmedabad. On the delivery side, masala dosa, kaju katli and paneer butter masala were the most-ordered items nationally, regional dishes such as appam and samosa broke into the top ten in emerging markets, and kaju katli led sweet orders, especially in Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Jaipur and Hyderabad. The figures are Swiggy's own platform data and were not independently audited.
items.relevance: Festive spending in India is moving into restaurants and social venues, not just onto doorsteps: brands should plan festive campaigns around dining districts, malls and evening hours, where real-world media meets people in a spending mood. The strength of tier-two cities argues for national, not metro-only, festive plans.

items.headline: Australia now has 67 car brands chasing 1.2 million sales a year, up 56% in five years, dealers warn
items.dek: The Australian Automotive Dealer Association says a wave of mostly Chinese entrants has left the market with too many marques, and is calling for a pause on new brands as dealer profits turn negative.
items.source: B&T, on Australian Automotive Dealer Association (AADA) data

figures.label: Car brands on sale in Australia, 2026
Car brands on sale in Australia, 2021
Growth in brand count over five years

keyPoints: Australia's new-car market now has about 67 brands competing for roughly 1.2 million sales a year, against around 40 brands for more than 2 million vehicles in the UK.
The brand count has risen 56% in five years, from 39 in 2021, driven mostly by new Chinese entrants.
Twelve more brands, including Changan, Hongqi, Jetour, Avatr and Wey, are reportedly preparing to launch in 2027.
The AADA says the September quarter brought the industry's first negative quarterly profitability result since the global financial crisis.
Its ten-point plan includes a pause on new brand entries and protection for dealers against excess stock and mid-stock price cuts.
body: The Australian Automotive Dealer Association has warned that the country's new-car market is oversupplied with brands. By its count, about 67 marques are now competing for roughly 1.2 million annual sales, up from 39 in 2021, a 56% increase in five years that has come mostly from Chinese newcomers. The association contrasts this with around 40 brands sharing a UK market of more than 2 million vehicles and 40 to 45 brands in a US market of about 16.4 million. Twelve further brands, among them Aito, Avatr, Changan, Hongqi, Jetour and Wey, are reported to be targeting Australian launches in 2027.

The AADA says the pressure is already visible in dealer results, with the September quarter producing the sector's first negative quarterly profitability figure since the global financial crisis, and points to Citroën's exit last November after 101 years as a sign that established names could follow. Chief executive James Voortman said there are "simply too many manufacturers" in the market and that pushing excess stock onto dealers is fuelling "a race to the bottom". The association's ten-point plan calls for a pause on new brand entries, the right for dealers to refuse excess stock without losing incentives, prompt compensation when manufacturers cut prices on stock already delivered, and stronger unfair-trading and consumer-law protections.
items.relevance: A crowded market means dozens of car brands, many with little awareness, fighting for share: fast, broad reach and salience formats such as roadside and large-format digital OOH are the obvious tools for launches. Sellers should also expect discount-led retail messaging, and possible budget cuts or exits, as margins tighten.

pitch.line: Australia's new-car market now has 67 brands competing for about 1.2 million annual sales, up from 39 in 2021 (Australian Automotive Dealer Association, via B&T).

items.headline: South Africa's festive season packs a fifth of annual retail sales into two months, Brand Journal report finds
items.dek: A free report pulling together official, payment and survey data shows December sales running 45% above a normal month, with stokvels, phone orders and data costs shaping how township shoppers buy.
items.source: Brand Journal, The Festive Trading Gap

figures.label: November and December share of annual retail sales
December 2025 retail sales vs average January–October month
Township residents put off engaging with brands online by data costs

keyPoints: November and December account for 21.1% of South Africa's annual retail sales, with December 2025 running about 45% above an average January–October month after price adjustments.
37% of township residents say data costs stop them engaging with brands online, while 41% have ordered from a local business by phone.
Around a third (34%) of township residents belong to a stokvel; Makro sees about 10,000 stokvel customers in December, against roughly 3,000 in a normal month.
Shoppers are sceptical: 76% of 2,410 OneDayOnly shoppers compare prices across platforms and 37% believe most Black Friday discounts are misleading.
Household budgets are stretched: 65% of more than 5,400 JustMoney respondents say every month is financially difficult and 43% needed to borrow before month-end.
body: The Festive Trading Gap, a free report published by Brand Journal on 9 November, assembles Statistics South Africa retail data, payment figures and several consumer surveys into one picture of the season. Price-adjusted retail sales in November 2025 ran about 23% above the average for January to October and December about 45% above, so the two months together delivered 21.1% of the year's sales. Festive spending through Yoco card machines in Soweto rose 35.2%. Yet household finances are tight: 65% of more than 5,400 respondents to JustMoney's Money & Me survey say every month is difficult and 43% had to borrow before month-end, while a monitored food basket cost R5,512.53 in October.

The report highlights how township and neighbourhood shoppers actually buy. Some 41% of township residents have ordered from a local business by phone, but 37% say data costs sometimes or often stop them engaging with brands online. A third belong to a stokvel or savings group, and Makro handles around 10,000 stokvel customers in December against a monthly average of about 3,000, much of it ordered in November. Price scrutiny is intense: 76% of 2,410 OneDayOnly shoppers compare prices across platforms, 37% think most Black Friday discounts are misleading, and 23% of 2,000 consumers already use AI search tools to compare products.

Brand Journal, which sells marketing services and discloses that interest, urges shops and wholesalers to confirm stock before advertising, keep 'previous price' claims honest, publish order cut-offs for group buyers and plan cash flow through January. The report is released under a Creative Commons licence.
items.relevance: With data costs keeping more than a third of township shoppers offline, low-data channels such as OOH, radio and in-store media remain essential to reach South Africa's mass market during its most important trading weeks. Plans should be timed to pay dates and stokvel buying in November, and promotional claims kept scrupulously accurate.

pitch.line: November and December deliver 21.1% of South Africa's annual retail sales, yet 37% of township residents say data costs stop them engaging with brands online (Brand Journal, The Festive Trading Gap).

items.headline: Mobimétrie launches France's first deduplicated audience measure across indoor and outdoor OOH
items.dek: France's OOH audience body will stop simply adding up contacts between street, mall, office and transport networks, starting with Cityz Media this month.
items.source: The Media Leader FR, on Mobimétrie

figures.label: French people reached by OOH each week

keyPoints: From mid-November, Mobimétrie will remove double counting between indoor and outdoor OOH audiences in France, replacing a system in which contacts were simply added together.
Cityz Media is the first network integrated; indoor networks from JCDecaux France and Phenix Digital follow in 2027, along with office network ECN and local indoor network DOOHYOULIKE.
Transport networks Extime JCDecaux Airport, JCDecaux Airport France and Mediatransports join in early 2027.
OOH reaches nearly 40 million French people a week, with 85% coverage in towns of more than 10,000 people.
The industry aims to lift the medium's share of French adspend above 10% by 2030.
body: Mobimétrie, the joint body that measures OOH audiences in France, has launched what it calls the first deduplicated audience measure covering both outdoor and indoor networks, classic and digital. Built on a methodology developed with Ipsos BVA since 2024 and on Mobimétrie's database of individual movements, it gives advertisers and agencies a consolidated audience without double counting between environments. Managing director Alexandre Scher said that previously 'contacts were simply added'.

The rollout is staged. Cityz Media's indoor audiences are integrated first this month. JCDecaux France and Phenix Digital add new indoor networks in 2027, and ECN (office screens) and DOOHYOULIKE (food stores, gyms and campuses) join through a simplified integration kit developed with the CESP. Airport and transport networks from Extime JCDecaux Airport, JCDecaux Airport France and Mediatransports follow in early 2027; buses and stations have already been processed and the metro is due by the end of November. Mobimétrie is also building MobiPlus, an interoperability platform for agencies, and says behavioural data could be added later.
items.relevance: Deduplicated reach lets OOH be compared with TV and digital on equal terms, a precondition for winning bigger shares of cross-media budgets. Sellers of indoor networks in France gain a currency; buyers should expect net reach figures to fall below today's summed contacts.

pitch.line: OOH reaches nearly 40 million French people every week, with 85% coverage in towns of more than 10,000 people (Mobimétrie).

items.headline: VIOOH opens 460 Adams Outdoor digital billboards in 14 states to programmatic buyers
items.dek: The JCDecaux-backed supply platform adds one of America's biggest regional roadside owners, with nearly 5bn monthly impressions.
items.source: Digital Signage Today, on VIOOH and Adams Outdoor
keyPoints: More than 460 Adams Outdoor digital billboards, delivering over 4.9bn impressions a month, can now be bought programmatically through VIOOH.
The inventory spans 14 states across the Southeast, Midwest and Northeast.
Markets include Charlotte, Raleigh-Durham, Charleston, Savannah, Norfolk-Virginia Beach, Detroit-Ann Arbor, Grand Rapids, Madison and the Ohio Valley including Pittsburgh.
VIOOH's Gavin Wilson says the deal gives buyers faster, more flexible access to established regional markets.
body: VIOOH, the programmatic supply platform majority-owned by JCDecaux, has signed Adams Outdoor, the acquisitive regional roadside operator, adding more than 460 digital billboards and over 4.9bn monthly impressions to its US marketplace. The screens sit in 14 states across the Southeast, Midwest and Northeast, from the Carolinas and coastal Georgia to Michigan, Wisconsin and the Ohio Valley.

The deal follows VIOOH's expansion into the Baltics with JCDecaux and extends its reach beyond the big coastal cities into mid-sized markets that national buyers often find harder to plan. Gavin Wilson, VIOOH's global chief commercial officer, said it gives buyers 'faster, more flexible access' to some of the country's most established regional markets. Commercial terms were not disclosed.
items.relevance: Regional roadside digital is becoming as easy to buy as metro inventory, which helps national brands add second-tier markets without separate negotiations. Independent operators that are not plugged into programmatic platforms risk being left out of automated plans.

pitch.line: More than 460 Adams Outdoor digital billboards, worth 4.9bn monthly impressions across 14 US states, are now programmatically buyable via VIOOH (Digital Signage Today).

items.headline: Al Arabia's loss deepens to SAR242m in the third quarter as Saudi ad spending softens
items.dek: Saudi Arabia's largest listed real-world media owner saw revenue fall 16% while carrying the cost of new sites whose networks are not yet complete.
items.source: Argaam, on Al Arabia (Arabian Contracting Services) third-quarter results
keyPoints: Al Arabia lost SAR241.9m in the third quarter on revenue down 16.2% to SAR346.8m, blaming lower advertising spending and the cost of running new sites before their networks are complete.
Over nine months revenue fell 25.2% to SAR1.03bn and the company swung to a SAR447.5m net loss from a SAR47.2m profit a year earlier.
Gross profit for the nine months collapsed to SAR8.1m from SAR533.8m, and the third quarter showed a gross loss of SAR68m.
Revenue did recover 31.4% on the second quarter, from SAR263.9m.
Higher lease, depreciation and project-financing costs also weighed on results.
body: Arabian Contracting Services, which trades as Al Arabia and is the biggest listed OOH company in Saudi Arabia, reported a third-quarter net loss of SAR241.9m, wider than the second quarter's SAR214.5m. Revenue fell 16.2% year on year to SAR346.8m, although it rose 31.4% from the weak second quarter. The operating loss for the quarter was SAR134.4m and the company recorded a gross loss of SAR68m.

The nine-month picture is starker: revenue down 25.2% to SAR1.03bn, gross profit almost wiped out at SAR8.1m against SAR533.8m a year earlier, and a net loss of SAR447.5m compared with a SAR47.2m profit. The company attributed the decline to reduced advertising spending, the cost of handling and operating several new advertising sites while the related networks under those contracts are still incomplete, and higher lease, depreciation and project-financing charges.
items.relevance: Saudi Arabia's big municipal concessions demand heavy up-front spending before the screens earn money, and a soft ad market exposes that gap. Buyers may find more negotiable pricing in the kingdom while operators work to fill newly built inventory.

pitch.line: Al Arabia's revenue fell 25% to SAR1.03bn in the first nine months of 2026 as Saudi ad spending softened (Al Arabia results via Argaam).

items.headline: E Ink makes its first investment in a media owner, backing solar-powered kiosk network Soofa
items.dek: The e-paper maker is betting on Soofa's off-grid street kiosks, which will move to 75-inch colour displays in major US cities.
items.source: invidis, on E Ink and Soofa
keyPoints: E Ink has made a strategic investment in Soofa, its first in a complete digital signage network operator; the amount was not disclosed.
Soofa runs solar-powered kiosks that need no wired power connection and partners with more than 60 US municipalities, including Boston, Atlanta and Los Angeles.
The network is upgrading from small monochrome screens to 75-inch Kaleido colour e-paper displays in major US cities.
For real-world media owners, low-power screens could open sites where cabling and energy costs rule out conventional LCD or LED.
body: E Ink, the Taiwanese maker of electronic-paper displays, has taken a strategic stake in Soofa, a Boston-founded company that operates solar-powered street kiosks. invidis reports that this is E Ink's first investment in a full network operator rather than a hardware partner. The amount was not disclosed.

Founded in 2014, Soofa has partnerships with more than 60 US municipalities, among them Boston, Atlanta and Los Angeles. Its earlier kiosks used small monochrome screens; the next generation will use 75-inch Kaleido colour e-paper panels, which draw so little power that they can run off grid. invidis argues that e-paper's future in signage depends on making large-format colour displays competitive with printed posters.
items.relevance: Off-grid colour e-paper could let cities and media owners digitise sites where connecting power is too costly, and helps answer energy and light-pollution objections to digital screens. Watch it as a planning argument in street-furniture tenders.

pitch.line: Soofa's solar-powered e-paper kiosks are already in more than 60 US municipalities, and are moving to 75-inch colour screens with E Ink's backing (invidis).

links.label: invidis: E-Paper needs the printing industry

items.headline: Duty Free Americas exits Atlanta, the world's busiest airport, as a new duty-free tender looms
items.dek: DFA's contract in Concourses E and F expired on 30 October and its business is suspended while the City of Atlanta prepares a fresh request for proposals.
items.source: Moodie Davitt Report, on Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International
keyPoints: Duty Free Americas has left its duty-free spaces in Concourses E and F at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta after its contract expired on 30 October.
A fresh tender for the spaces is expected soon; DFA is waiting for an updated request for proposals from the City of Atlanta Department of Aviation.
DFA says it will bid again as the previous incumbent.
The airport handled 106 million passengers in 2025, 14.8 million of them international.
body: Duty Free Americas has exited its duty-free locations at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International after its contract ran out on 30 October, a senior DFA executive told the Moodie Davitt Report. The business in Concourses E and F, the airport's international concourses, is suspended, and no interim operator was named.

The City of Atlanta Department of Aviation is expected to issue an updated request for proposals soon, though no date has been given. DFA, which says it will always bid on US airport duty-free contracts, plans to compete as the previous incumbent. Atlanta handled 106 million passengers in 2025, including 14.8 million international travellers.
items.relevance: One of the largest US duty-free opportunities is about to come to market, and the gap in trading leaves brands without international-departure shelf space in Atlanta for now. Brand owners should engage likely bidders early.

pitch.line: Atlanta handled 106 million passengers in 2025, and its international duty-free concession is about to be re-tendered (Moodie Davitt Report).

brief: Media costs will keep climbing: the WFA sees prices up 4.5% next year as premium digital inventory stays scarce, with paid search the dearest channel, while DigiCert finds 43% of shoppers deleting brand emails they cannot verify.
Consumers are holding fire for the peak: 40% of Britons are cutting back now to fund Christmas, and Quantum Metric says AI agent visits to brand sites have grown 25-fold in a year.

In real-world media, Global agrees to buy Alight Media and its 1,500 digital 48-sheets, iligo finds street-plus-mall OOH lifts recall by 19 points for Cityz Media, and Inglewood voters narrowly keep 60 WOW Media digital billboards.

Diary: Ströer reports on 12 November, SPT's Glasgow bus shelter tender closes and FIRB's oOh!media deadline falls on 13 November, Fraport Bulgaria's lounge EOI closes on 15 November, oOh!media's scheme goes to court on 18 November, and Schiphol's €426m advertising tender closes on 20 November.

numberOfDay.line: Campaigns seen on both street OOH and shopping-centre screens reached 48% ad recall, against 29% for street exposure alone (iligo for Cityz Media).

steal.title: Plan by the route, not the postcode
steal.text: GSTV's survey finds 78% of US drivers add a stop when a retailer is on their route and 69% bought something unplanned on their last errand run. The idea worth stealing: map the drive-time corridors between homes, workplaces and stores, and place roadside, fuel-station and near-store screens along them in the weeks before Thanksgiving and Christmas, with creative that names the nearest store and the turn to take.

items.headline: Scarce premium digital inventory will keep media inflation at 4.5% into 2027, WFA forecasts
items.dek: The World Federation of Advertisers' latest media-price poll nudges global inflation up for 2026 and sees no relief next year, with paid search and retail media the costliest channels.
items.source: World Federation of Advertisers (WFA), Outlook media inflation forecast
keyPoints: Media prices worldwide are set to rise 4.5% in both 2026 and 2027, with scarce premium digital inventory rather than advertiser demand setting the pace.
The 2026 forecast edges up from 4.4% in April; Turkey and Argentina are excluded because of hyperinflation.
Paid search (5.4%) and retail media (5.2%) are the fastest-inflating channels this year, ahead of social video (4.4%) and social display (4.1%).
US inflation is revised up to 4.6% from 4.0%, while India eases to about 9% from 9.5%.
Linear TV inflation is now forecast to be notably lower than the 7.7% expected in April, as streaming supply grows.
body: The WFA's twice-yearly Outlook poll of media price forecasts puts global media inflation at 4.5% for 2026, a fraction above April's 4.4% estimate, and holds it at 4.5% for 2027. The federation's reading is that the squeeze comes from the supply side: premium digital inventory is scarce, and that, more than demand from advertisers, is what is pushing prices up.

By channel, paid search (5.4%) and retail media (5.2%) lead the 2026 table, followed by social video (4.4%) and social display (4.1%). Linear TV is forecast to rise notably less than the 7.7% predicted in the spring, and expanding streaming inventory is generally holding connected-TV prices in check. Among markets, the US is revised up to 4.6% from 4.0%; India remains the highest of the big markets at about 9%. Forecasts strengthened in Germany, Mexico and the UAE and softened in the UK, South Korea, Spain, France and Belgium, though the WFA does not publish figures for those.
items.relevance: With search and retail media inflating faster than the market, cost-per-reach comparisons favour channels whose supply is growing, which strengthens the efficiency case for real-world media in 2027 budget talks. Planners should lock in rates early where inventory is scarce.

pitch.line: Paid search prices are forecast to rise 5.4% in 2026, the fastest of any channel, against 4.5% for media overall (WFA Outlook).

chart.title: Media price inflation forecast, 2026

report.label: WFA Outlook: media inflation forecast

items.headline: Four in ten shoppers bin brand emails they cannot verify, DigiCert finds
items.dek: A 6,000-person survey across five markets shows scams and deepfakes are eroding trust in owned digital channels: 43% have deleted a retail email because they doubted it was genuine.
items.source: DigiCert, via GlobeNewswire

figures.label: Deleted or abandoned an unverified email
Received a suspicious email in the past year
Would click an offer they can't verify
Pick the brand showing a verified logo

keyPoints: 43% of shoppers deleted or abandoned a retail email in the past year because they were not sure it was genuine.
17% delayed a purchase as a result, and more than one in ten bought from another retailer instead.
Nearly 90% received a suspicious email in the past year and 42% acted on one; only 3% would click an offer they cannot verify.
54% choose the brand that shows its official logo in the inbox, up from 49% in 2025, yet four in ten do not know verified logos exist.
More than a third decided against a purchase because they doubted an image or video was real.
body: DigiCert, a digital-certificate provider, commissioned Vitreous World to survey 6,000 adults in the US (2,000), the UK (2,000), Germany (1,000), Australia (800) and New Zealand (200). The headline finding is that doubt now costs sales: 43% deleted or abandoned a brand email in the past year because they could not tell whether it was real, 17% delayed a purchase, and more than one in ten took their money to a rival.

Exposure to fraud is near-universal. Nearly nine in ten received a suspicious message in the past year and 42% acted on one, which explains why only 3% would now open or click an unverifiable offer. Visible trust signals help: 54% pick the brand that shows a verified logo in the inbox, up from 49% last year, half say a trust mark makes them likelier to buy and three-quarters feel safer with one. Awareness lags, however: four in ten have never heard of verified logos, rising to 48% in Germany. More than a third have abandoned a purchase because they were unsure whether an image or video was authentic.
items.relevance: As AI-made fakes multiply, brands need channels people instinctively believe. Physical, public media that consumers can see in the street carries an authenticity that inboxes and feeds are losing, a point OOH sellers can make alongside the trust data.

pitch.line: 43% of shoppers in five markets deleted a retail email in the past year because they could not verify it was genuine (DigiCert / Vitreous World, 6,000 adults).

study.markets: US, UK, Germany, Australia, New Zealand

chart.title: What shoppers did with suspect emails

items.headline: Pairing street furniture with mall screens lifts ad recall by 19 points, iligo studies for Cityz Media find
items.dek: Three effectiveness studies commissioned by the French real-world media owner show combining formats along the same journey beats any single format on recall, consideration and attention.
items.source: CB News, on iligo research for Cityz Media

figures.label: Ad recall: street + mall vs street only

keyPoints: People exposed to OOH both in the street and in shopping centres recalled the campaign 48% of the time, against 29% for street exposure alone: a 19-point lift.
Consideration rose from 67% to 79% and purchase intent from 54% to 67% when the two environments were combined.
Adding buses to 8m² street furniture raised correct brand attribution among those who recalled the campaign from 67% to 75%.
Inside malls, giant screens caught 48% of visitors' attention within the first second, against 32% for totems.
Running giant screens and totems on the same route multiplied attention time by 1.3.
body: Cityz Media, the former Clear Channel France business, has commissioned iligo to test the effect of combining its formats. In the first study, people who saw a campaign both on street OOH and in shopping centres recalled it 48% of the time, against 29% for those exposed only outdoors. Consideration rose by 12 points to 79% and purchase intent by 13 points to 67%.

The second study compared 8m² street furniture alone with the same format plus bus advertising: among people who remembered the campaign, correct brand attribution rose from 67% to 75%, perceived differentiation by six points and the wish to talk about the campaign by four. The third, inside shopping centres, found giant screens captured 48% of visitors within the first second against 32% for totems, and that pairing the two along one route lifted attention time 1.3-fold. CB News notes that the methodologies were not published, so the figures are best treated as directional.
items.relevance: The studies give sellers a clean argument for multi-environment plans: repetition across the street, transport and the mall builds memory faster than more weight in one format. Buyers should ask for the methodology before using the numbers in an econometric model.

pitch.line: Campaigns seen on both street OOH and mall screens achieved 48% ad recall, against 29% for street exposure alone (iligo for Cityz Media).

chart.title: Street-only OOH vs street plus shopping-centre OOH

items.headline: AI chatbots reach 45 million French users a month, up 85%, Médiamétrie finds
items.dek: France's official audience measurer shows conversational AI tripling its daily reach in a year, while social networks still touch 80% of the population every day.
items.source: CB News, on Médiamétrie data

figures.label: Daily reach of social and messaging

keyPoints: Conversational AI reached almost 45 million monthly unique visitors in France in September 2026, up 85% in a year, and its daily audience tripled to 17 million.
OpenAI has ranked as France's 11th-largest internet brand since May 2026.
AI still takes only 1% of daily browsing time, about three minutes, though that has nearly tripled.
Social networks and messaging reach 47 million people a day, 80% of those aged 11+, and take 45% of internet time, rising to 64% among 15–24s.
50.7 million French people go online daily, for 3h25 on average.
body: Médiamétrie's latest internet audience dossier shows how quickly AI assistants have entered French daily life. Almost 45 million people used a conversational AI service in September 2026, 85% more than a year earlier, and daily users tripled to 17 million. OpenAI has been among France's top 11 internet brands since May. Yet AI remains a small share of attention: about three minutes a day, or 1% of browsing time, albeit nearly three times last year's level.

Social media is holding its ground. Social and messaging platforms reach 47 million people a day, 80% of the population aged 11 and over, and account for 45% of time online, rising to 64% among 15–24-year-olds. Overall, 50.7 million people (86%) go online each day for an average of 3h25, and 82% do so on a smartphone or tablet. Médiamétrie plans a dedicated measurement of AI usage in its MediaWeb service from the first quarter of 2027.
items.relevance: AI assistants are becoming a mass-reach gateway to information in France, which will reshape search and discovery budgets. For now they take little time, so the media-planning priority is visibility in the sources AI draws on, including earned and real-world presence.

pitch.line: Almost 45 million French people used an AI chatbot in September 2026, up 85% in a year (Médiamétrie).

items.headline: British shoppers hoard cash for Christmas as card spending hits a 15-month high
items.dek: Barclays data show October spending up 2.3%, driven by fuel, while 40% of consumers are cutting back now to afford the festive season; BRC figures show non-food sales flat.
items.source: Barclays Consumer Spend and BRC-KPMG Retail Sales Monitor, via SLR and FashionUnited

figures.label: Cutting back now to save for Christmas

keyPoints: 40% of Britons are cutting back now to save for Christmas, rising to 53% of Gen Z and 54% of Millennials.
Card spending rose 2.3% in October, the strongest growth since July 2025, but fuel (up 22.7% as diesel passed £2 a litre) did much of the work.
Retail spending grew only 0.5% on Barclays data; supermarkets fell 0.9% while food and drink specialists rose 4.6%.
BRC-KPMG figures show total sales up 1.5%, food up 3.2% and non-food flat, with in-store non-food down 1.1%.
Confidence in the economy slipped to 23% from 26%, and 58% expect Christmas to cost more than last year.
body: Barclays' October card data show spending up 2.3% year on year, its fastest pace in 15 months, but the rise was led by essentials (+3.1%), with fuel up 22.7% after diesel crossed £2 a litre. Non-essential spending rose 1.9% and retail just 0.5%. Consumers are deliberately holding back: 40% say they are cutting spending now to fund Christmas, including more than half of Gen Z and Millennials, 58% expect the festive season to cost more, and 34% have already started buying presents.

The BRC-KPMG Retail Sales Monitor, published the same day, tells a similar story. Total sales grew 1.5%, with food up 3.2% and non-food flat; in-store non-food sales fell 1.1%, while online grew 1.8% and took 38.6% of non-food sales. Confidence in the economy fell to 23% from 26%, and confidence in spending on non-essentials to 50% from 54%.
items.relevance: Money saved in October will be spent in a tight window from Black Friday to Christmas Eve, so retailers should concentrate weight in those weeks and close to stores, where real-world media meets shoppers with budgets ready.

pitch.line: 40% of UK consumers are cutting back now to save for Christmas, rising to 54% of Millennials (Barclays Consumer Spend, October 2026).

study.by: Barclays; British Retail Consortium and KPMG

items.headline: Germans buy fewer advent calendars but pay 26% more than in 2021, YouGov finds
items.dek: YouGov's shopper panel shows the seasonal confectionery category shrinking in volume as prices climb, with supermarkets and discounters still the main place to buy.
items.source: YouGov Germany

figures.label: Plan to buy an influencer calendar

keyPoints: The average confectionery advent calendar cost €8.38 in 2025, up 11.6% in a year and 26% since 2021.
Buyers fell 10.9% to about 11 million and units sold dropped 15% to 22.9 million.
Spend per buyer still rose 6.5% to €17.41.
41% buy their calendar at a supermarket or discounter, 19% online and 10% at a drugstore.
53% have heard of influencer advent calendars, but only 6% plan to buy one; 82% of those aware say buyers mainly pay for the name.
body: YouGov's FMCG shopper panel shows Germany's advent-calendar category contracting in volume. In 2025 the number of buyers fell 10.9% to about 11 million, household reach slipped from 18.2% to 16.2%, and units sold dropped 15% to 22.9 million. Prices moved the other way: the average calendar cost €8.38, 11.6% more than a year earlier and well above €6.66 in 2021, so spend per buyer rose 6.5% to €17.41.

A survey of 2,081 adults in late October suggests demand is stable this year: 54% plan to buy a ready-made calendar, unchanged, though fewer intend to buy one for themselves (23% against 27%). Grocery remains the main channel at 41%, ahead of online (19%) and drugstores (10%), and 52% would spend up to €20. Influencer-branded calendars have high awareness (53%) but little pull: just 6% plan to buy one.
items.relevance: Seasonal treats are increasingly a premium, considered purchase made in the grocery aisle, which favours brand-building before the season and reminders near the store rather than late discounting.

pitch.line: 41% of German advent-calendar buyers shop for them in supermarkets and discounters, against 19% online (YouGov Germany, 2026).

items.headline: Spanish shoppers are the most bullish on beauty spending of eight markets, Dailymotion finds
items.dek: Dailymotion's second-half shopping-intent study shows Spain above the international average for planned spending on beauty, luxury and cars, and for trust in premium publishers.
items.source: IPMARK, on Dailymotion research

figures.label: Spanish beauty buyers planning to spend more
Plan to spend more on cars (avg 27.7%)

keyPoints: 36.5% of Spanish beauty buyers plan to spend more in 2026, the highest of the eight markets surveyed.
31.4% of Spaniards plan to spend more on cars, against an average of 27.7%.
70.3% of 18–34-year-olds intend to raise luxury spending, and 20% of all respondents expect to spend much more on luxury (average 17.7%).
Overall, 27.9% plan to spend more, slightly above the 27.1% average.
Trust in ads is highest for search (23.2%) and social (21.7%); trust in premium publishers (15.1%) beats the 12% international average.
body: Dailymotion's H2 Shopping Intent Study, covering eight markets including Spain, the US, the UK, France and Mexico, finds Spanish consumers somewhat more willing to spend than their peers. Overall, 27.9% expect to spend more (average 27.1%) and 45.9% expect to cut back (average 47.9%). Beauty is the standout: 36.5% of Spanish beauty buyers plan to spend more, the highest of any market.

Luxury and cars also look resilient. One in five Spaniards expects to spend much more on luxury, rising to 70.3% of 18–34s who intend to increase spending, and 31.4% plan to spend more on cars. Creator videos influence 41.2% (average 46.6%), with a sharp gender gap among car buyers. Asked which ads they trust, Spaniards rank search (23.2%), social (21.7%) and connected TV (19.9%) ahead of premium publishers (15.1%), though the latter score above the 12% international average.
items.relevance: Spain's resilient intent in beauty, luxury and automotive points to categories likely to keep premium media budgets in 2027, including landmark and city-centre real-world media.

pitch.line: 36.5% of Spanish beauty buyers plan to spend more in 2026, the highest of eight markets (Dailymotion H2 Shopping Intent Study).

items.headline: ChatGPT changes its local business recommendations from one query to the next, Dutch test shows
items.dek: RankPilot asked ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Mode 1,050 questions about local trades in 14 Dutch cities and found the tools rarely agree, or even repeat themselves.
items.source: Frankwatching, on RankPilot research

figures.label: ChatGPT picks appearing in only one of three runs
Same business named by all three tools

keyPoints: 62% of the businesses ChatGPT recommended appeared in only one of three identical runs; just 7% appeared in all three.
All three AI tools named the same business for only 24% of questions.
Gemini named actual businesses in 88% of answers, ChatGPT in 66% and Google AI Mode in 59%.
Businesses with fewer than 10 Google reviews made up just 4% of ChatGPT's recommendations.
ChatGPT leaned on platforms, citing Trustoo in 49% of answers and Werkspot in 39%.
body: RankPilot, an SEO agency in Groningen, put 350 questions to each of ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Mode, covering 25 trades in 14 Dutch cities, on 13 October. Of the 1,050 answers, Gemini named real businesses most often (88%), ahead of ChatGPT (66%) and AI Mode (59%). Overlap with Google's top-three map listings was 53% for ChatGPT, 50% for Gemini and only 29% for AI Mode.

Consistency was poor. Running the same questions three times, 62% of the businesses ChatGPT recommended appeared only once and just 7% every time, and the three tools agreed on a business for only a quarter of questions. Review volume mattered: firms with fewer than 10 Google reviews were rarely recommended. ChatGPT also relied heavily on lead-generation platforms such as Trustoo and Werkspot.
items.relevance: If AI recommendations shift from query to query, brands cannot rely on them for local visibility. Physical presence, reviews and recognisable signage in the neighbourhood remain the stable route to being chosen.

pitch.line: 62% of the local businesses ChatGPT recommended appeared in only one of three identical runs (RankPilot test, 1,050 AI answers, Netherlands).

items.headline: Seven in ten US drivers bought something unplanned on their last errand run, GSTV survey finds
items.dek: GSTV's Consumer Pulse study suggests holiday purchase decisions are increasingly made on the road, with 78% adding a stop when a retailer sits on their route.
items.source: invidis, on GSTV Consumer Pulse research

figures.label: Bought something unplanned on last errand trip
Add a stop if a retailer is on the route
Expect extra trips in Thanksgiving week
Added an unplanned item at a c-store

keyPoints: 78% of drivers add a stop when a retailer is conveniently on their route, and 69% bought something unplanned on their most recent errand trip.
69% run more errands than usual during the holidays and 61% drive more.
55% expect extra trips during Thanksgiving week, mainly for a big grocery run (52%) or holiday and Black Friday shopping (48%).
45% only realise they need something once they are in the car or the store.
At convenience stores, 52% add at least one unplanned item, half of them simply because they saw it.
body: GSTV, which runs video screens at more than 29,000 US fuel stations, asked its viewers about holiday routines in its August Consumer Pulse survey, fielded by MFour. Holiday season means more time on the road: 69% run more errands than usual, 61% drive more, and 55% expect extra trips in Thanksgiving week, chiefly for groceries (52%) and Black Friday shopping (48%).

Many decisions are made en route. 69% bought something unplanned on their last errand trip, 78% add a stop if a retailer is on their way and 45% realise what they need only once they are already out. In convenience stores, 52% added at least one unplanned item, with cold drinks (49%) and snacks (36%) the most common buys. GSTV sells advertising on its network and did not disclose the sample size, so the results are best read as indicative.
items.relevance: The path to purchase runs through the car: roadside, fuel-station and near-store real-world media can reach shoppers in the minutes when unplanned decisions are made. Retailers should plan by route and drive-time, not just by home postcode.

pitch.line: 78% of US drivers add a stop when a retailer is on their route, and 69% bought something unplanned on their last errand trip (GSTV Consumer Pulse).

items.headline: Shoppers tune out peak sales as AI agents decide where and when they buy, Quantum Metric finds
items.dek: Quantum Metric's 2026 Peak Benchmark, covering the US and UK, shows AI agent visits to brand sites up 25-fold in under a year and attention to traditional sale moments fading.
items.source: Quantum Metric, via GlobeNewswire

figures.label: Growth in AI agent sessions on brand sites
Used AI to shop or book in six months
Paying less attention to early-October sales
Lost a purchase to a site problem at peak

keyPoints: AI agent sessions on brand websites grew 25-fold in under a year, and two in three consumers used AI to shop, book or choose services in the past six months.
Consumers say they are paying less attention to phone launches (55%), holiday travel sales (48%) and early-October sales (34%).
Retail AI agents abandon 48 baskets for every completed purchase, against about three for all traffic.
92% hit a problem during peak periods and 62% lost a purchase as a result.
One in five have let, or would let, AI complete a holiday gift purchase.
body: Quantum Metric combined a survey of 1,500 US and UK consumers with aggregated data from its digital-analytics platform. The behavioural data show agentic shopping arriving quickly: AI agent sessions on brand sites have grown 25 times in under a year, and AI-referred retail traffic in early October was 3.1 times the same week of 2025. Two in three consumers have used AI to shop, book or pick services in the past six months.

Traditional sale moments are losing pull. Shoppers report paying less attention to phone launches (55%), holiday travel sales (48%) and early-October events (34%). Agents are fickle buyers, abandoning 48 carts per completed purchase against roughly three for all visitors, and human shoppers are unforgiving: 92% hit a problem at peak times and 62% lost a purchase because of it. One in five would let AI complete a gift purchase.
items.relevance: When agents shortlist and promotions blur together, the brand a shopper already knows and asks for has the advantage. Salience built before the purchase moment, through broad-reach media, matters more than discount noise.

pitch.line: AI agent sessions on brand websites grew 25-fold in under a year (Quantum Metric 2026 Peak Benchmark, US and UK).

chart.title: Paying less attention to sale moments

items.headline: Only 6% of Australian marketers have a clear AI roadmap, and confidence trails the US by 21 points
items.dek: The Global Centre for AI in Marketing's first cross-market benchmark finds Australian marketing leaders less ready than their American peers, though few on either side have a documented plan.
items.source: B&T, on Global Centre for AI in Marketing research

figures.label: Clear, documented AI roadmap (AU vs US)
Fully ready to lead AI change (AU vs US)

keyPoints: Just 6% of Australian marketing leaders and 7% in the US have a clearly documented AI roadmap.
27% of Australians feel fully ready to lead AI-driven change, against 48% of Americans.
68% of Australian leaders say they must improve their own AI skills first, against 46% in the US.
'AI slop' is a top-three worry for 61% of Australians and 78% of Americans.
Only 17% of Australian organisations rate level four or above on a six-level maturity scale, against 29% in the US.
body: The Global Centre for AI in Marketing surveyed 126 Australian marketing leaders across 12 industries, with Kantar, and 126 US marketers, mostly CMOs, with The CMO Syndicate. The report, titled Confidence Outpaces Accountability, finds that very few organisations in either country have a clearly documented AI plan (6% in Australia, 7% in the US), though the US is further along on partly documented roadmaps (50% against 37%).

Australians are markedly less confident: 27% feel fully ready to lead AI-driven change against 48% of Americans, and 68% say they need to upskill themselves first. Skills gaps are widest in choosing AI tools (53% against 35%) and fitting them into daily work (64% against 56%). Concern about low-quality 'AI slop' is high in both markets, at 61% and 78%.
items.relevance: Marketers who are unsure how to use AI will lean on partners for clear planning tools and proof of outcomes. Media sellers that offer simple, measured AI-assisted planning, rather than black boxes, will find receptive buyers.

pitch.line: Only 6% of Australian marketing leaders have a clearly documented AI roadmap (Global Centre for AI in Marketing, 126 leaders).

items.headline: China's online ad market grows just 3.1% as AI apps reach 546 million users, QuestMobile finds
items.dek: QuestMobile's autumn report shows Chinese internet advertising barely growing, three platforms taking half of display spend and an ageing mobile audience.
items.source: QuestMobile, 2026 China Mobile Internet Autumn Report
keyPoints: China's internet advertising market reached RMB193.24bn in the third quarter of 2026, up only 3.1% year on year.
Douyin (17.4%), Taobao (15.8%) and Qianchuan (15.6%) took 48.8% of display-ad spend between them, and the top ten media 86.2%.
AI-native apps reached 546 million monthly active users, up 82.1%.
Users aged 46 and over now make up more than 40% of the mobile base, while 25–45-year-olds have fallen to 39%.
Monthly time per user rose 6.5% to 189.8 hours in September, driven by short drama and short video.
body: QuestMobile's tracking data show the Chinese online ad market maturing. Third-quarter spending was RMB193.24bn, 3.1% higher than a year earlier, even though the number of brand-display advertisers rose 10% to 8,356. Spending is concentrated: Douyin, Taobao and Qianchuan together take almost half of display budgets, and the top ten platforms more than 86%.

Audience trends are shifting underneath. China's mobile internet has 1.281 billion monthly users, little changed, but time spent per user rose 6.5% to 189.8 hours a month, with short drama and short video accounting for all the growth in September. AI-native apps now reach 546 million users, up 82%. The audience is also ageing: people aged 46 and over account for more than 40% of users, and those over 51 for 29.4%.
items.relevance: Slow growth and heavy platform concentration in digital spend make it harder for brands to stand out online in China, while an older, affluent urban audience is well reached by real-world media in cities and transit.

pitch.line: China's internet ad market grew just 3.1% year on year in Q3 2026, to RMB193.2bn (QuestMobile).

items.headline: Nearly three-quarters of UAE travellers choose greener trips, but price still decides, Trip.com finds
items.dek: Trip.com Group's Sustainable Travel Consumer Report shows strong intent among UAE travellers, led by Gen Z, and a clear link between sustainable offers and choice of booking site.
items.source: Communicate, on Trip.com Group research

figures.label: Changed plans because of extreme weather

keyPoints: 72.8% of UAE travellers have actively chosen more sustainable travel options, and 96.3% say sustainability matters in their decisions.
Price still rules: 64.1% cite it as a driver of choice, and higher prices are the main barrier (39.8%).
81.8% have changed at least one travel plan because of extreme weather.
Sustainable choices fall with age: Gen Z 69.5%, Millennials 63%, Gen X 50.6%, Boomers 40.6%.
92.3% say sustainable offerings would influence which booking platform they use.
body: Trip.com Group's 2026 Sustainable Travel Consumer Report for the UAE finds near-universal interest in greener travel: 96.3% say sustainability matters and 72.8% have actively chosen a more sustainable option. Barriers remain practical: higher prices (39.8%), limited availability (33.5%) and fears of greenwashing (26.8%). Price (64.1%) and quality and comfort (61.8%) still drive final decisions.

Climate is already changing behaviour: 81.8% have altered a trip because of extreme weather. Younger travellers lead, with 69.5% of Gen Z choosing sustainable options against 40.6% of Boomers, and 92.3% say sustainable offerings would affect which booking site they use. The report does not state its sample size.
items.relevance: Travel brands, airlines and booking platforms are among the biggest buyers of airport and city OOH in the Gulf; credible, price-conscious sustainability messages aimed at younger travellers are likely to resonate.

pitch.line: 72.8% of UAE travellers have actively chosen more sustainable travel options (Trip.com Group Sustainable Travel Consumer Report 2026).

items.headline: African outbound travel spending set to rise 61% to $30.4bn by 2030, Skift study finds
items.dek: A Skift Advisory white paper for Millat Group, launched at WTM London, identifies Africans as one of travel's fastest-growing source markets, with Nigeria the biggest spender.
items.source: Bizcommunity, on Skift Advisory research for Millat Group
keyPoints: African outbound travel spending is projected to grow about 61%, from $18.9bn in 2025 to $30.4bn in 2030.
Outbound trips are forecast to rise from 13.3m in 2025 to 17.7m in 2030 and 19.4m in 2035.
Nigeria leads at $7.7bn, about 41% more than South Africa despite roughly a fifth as many trips.
Average departure taxes are $68 per international departure in Africa, against $32 in Europe.
Gulf hubs carry about 28% of South Africa's connecting traffic to Europe.
body: Skift Advisory's 'Africa in Motion: The Next Great Traveller', commissioned by Millat Group and launched at World Travel Market in London, models outbound travel from Egypt, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa. It projects trips rising from 13.3 million in 2025 to 17.7 million by 2030, with spending up about 61% to $30.4bn. The analysis draws on a Skift inbound study with a weighted base of 14,115 across 14 markets, a 2026 brand tracker and expert interviews.

Nigerians are the highest-value travellers, spending $7.7bn, about 41% more than South Africans despite taking around a fifth as many trips. Costs remain a brake: departure taxes average $68 in Africa against $32 in Europe, and African airlines earn just $0.90 per passenger against $15.20 for Middle Eastern carriers. Gulf hubs already carry about 28% of South Africa's connecting traffic to Europe.
items.relevance: A growing, high-spending African travelling class passes through Gulf and European hubs, making airport media in Dubai, Doha and major African gateways a channel for brands targeting affluent African consumers.

pitch.line: African outbound travel spending is forecast to rise about 61% to $30.4bn by 2030 (Skift Advisory for Millat Group).

study.markets: Egypt, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa

items.headline: Brazilian marketing pay rises about 5% for 2027, with growth roles gaining most, Robert Half finds
items.dek: Robert Half's 2027 salary guide shows median marketing salaries in São Paulo up 5–5.2%, and entry pay for heads of growth jumping about 20%.
items.source: Mundo do Marketing, on Robert Half's Guia Salarial 2027

figures.label: Median rise, São Paulo marketing roles
Head of growth entry pay rise

keyPoints: Median salaries for 21 marketing roles in São Paulo rise 5–5.2% for 2027.
Entry-level pay (25th percentile) for heads of growth jumps about 20%, from R$25,000 to R$30,100 a month.
A marketing director at a large São Paulo company earns a median R$47,250 a month, up from R$45,000.
Top-quartile commercial director pay rises about 16% to R$65,100.
Marketing managers move to R$32,550 and digital marketing analysts to R$12,100.
body: Robert Half's 2027 salary guide, covering 21 marketing roles in São Paulo and 17 other Brazilian cities, shows steady pay inflation of 5–5.2% at the median. At large São Paulo firms, marketing directors move from R$45,000 to R$47,250 a month, heads of growth from R$36,500 to R$38,350 and marketing managers from R$31,000 to R$32,550.

The sharpest moves are at the edges of the range. Entry pay for heads of growth rises about 20%, to R$30,100, and top-quartile pay for commercial directors about 16%, to R$65,100. The pattern points to strong demand for executives who can link marketing directly to revenue.
items.relevance: Brazilian companies are paying a premium for growth and commercial leaders, so media pitches there land better when framed around revenue outcomes and measurement than around reach alone.

pitch.line: Entry-level pay for heads of growth in São Paulo rises about 20% for 2027 (Robert Half Guia Salarial 2027).
