The company says the larger footprint gives advertisers a wider choice of locations for regional campaigns, or for extending national activity beyond Australia's capital cities.

The acquisition continues a run of expansion for Bishopp across Victoria and New South Wales, which included adding Avalon Airport to its portfolio. Sales director Dominic Lis said advertisers need to approach regional Australia with a clear strategy, and referred to the combined offer spanning roadside and airport campaigns. Financial terms were not disclosed.
The deal comes as Australia's OOH market is being reshaped at the top end, with I Squared Capital's takeover of oOh!media heading for court approval later this month.
items.relevance: Regional coverage is often the gap in national OOH plans; a consolidated regional seller makes it simpler to buy. Sellers elsewhere can note how scale outside the capitals is being packaged as a strategic, not leftover, audience.

pitch.line: Bishopp Outdoor has added more than 450 regional sites by acquiring JAM Outdoor (B&T).

items.headline: Hangzhou plans a $1.2bn LED sphere to outshine the Las Vegas Sphere
items.dek: 'The Eye of the World' would carry 72,000 sq m of exterior LED, a third more than its Nevada rival, though construction has yet to start and no opening date has been set.
items.source: invidis
keyPoints: A joint venture of Xinshi International Investment and Vision Eye plans an LED sphere in Hangzhou's Qiantang district with 72,000 sq m of exterior display, against 54,000 sq m in Las Vegas.
Construction is estimated at $1.2bn, and the venue is projected to generate $400m a year, according to AV Magazine figures cited by invidis.
It would be larger on every measure: 168m diameter, 122m high and 20,000 seats.
The project was unveiled on 30 October, but design, permits and infrastructure are still being worked out and no LED supplier has been named.
Smaller spheres already exist in China, and similar projects are planned for Shanghai and Guangzhou.
body: Hangzhou has unveiled plans for 'The Eye of the World', an LED-clad sphere intended to exceed the Las Vegas Sphere. It was announced on 30 October at a conference in the Qiantang district, shortly after the developers, a joint venture of Hong Kong-based Xinshi International Investment and Vision Eye (Hangzhou), signed the contract.

The specifications are deliberately bigger than the US original: a diameter of 168m against 157m, a height of 122m against 112m, 20,000 seats against 17,600, and an exterior display of 72,000 sq m against 54,000 sq m. Construction is put at $1.2bn, with projected annual revenue of $400m. The interior would host immersive shows, concerts, brand launches and sport, while the exterior would be used for festivals and holiday events.

invidis cautions that the project is at an early stage: building has not begun, permits are pending, and no opening date or display maker has been announced. A smaller sphere with 7,500 sq m of exterior display opened in Qianjiang, Hubei, in May 2026, and further projects have been announced in Shanghai and Guangzhou.
items.relevance: Spectacular 'destination screens' are becoming a format in their own right, and China is moving to build several. Brands planning launches in China should watch whether these venues sell exterior time as advertising, as Las Vegas does.

pitch.line: Hangzhou's planned 'Eye of the World' would carry 72,000 sq m of exterior LED, a third more than the Las Vegas Sphere (invidis).

chart.title: Hangzhou plan vs Las Vegas Sphere: exterior display area

items.headline: Axel Springer turns its Berlin balloon into Germany's highest billboard
items.dek: The publisher is selling the 1,600 sq m surface of the tethered Welt balloon near Checkpoint Charlie, which rises to 150m, and has signed Deutsche Vermögensberatung as its first advertiser.
items.source: Axel Springer, via invidis
keyPoints: Axel Springer is offering the Welt tethered balloon over Berlin-Mitte as an advertising surface of 1,600 sq m, billed as Germany's highest OOH site.
Deutsche Vermögensberatung is the first client, running its 'Deutschland macht Rente' campaign for six weeks.
The balloon, operated by Air Service Berlin, rises to 150m near Checkpoint Charlie and carries 15–20 tourists per ascent.
Sales sit with Springer's Premium group (Welt, Politico Deutschland, Business Insider, Icon); its DOOH business runs through Framen.
body: Axel Springer is expanding into OOH with the Welt balloon, the tethered observation balloon on Zimmerstraße near Checkpoint Charlie that usually carries the newspaper's logo. The company now sells its 1,600 sq m surface to advertisers and markets it as Germany's highest outdoor advertising site, rising up to 150m above Berlin-Mitte. Air Service Berlin operates the balloon, which takes 15 to 20 passengers per ascent.

Financial adviser Deutsche Vermögensberatung is the first advertiser, with a six-week run of its 'Deutschland macht Rente' campaign. The surface is sold by Springer's Premium group, which bundles Welt, Politico Deutschland, Business Insider Deutschland and Icon and has handled luxury and events since a summer reorganisation of the publisher's advertising business.

Springer already sells digital OOH through Framen, the Berlin DOOH company in which it has held a majority stake since 2020, and which recently built an in-store retail media network for garden-centre chain Dehner.
items.relevance: Landmark one-off sites command attention and earned media that standard inventory cannot. Publishers and venue owners with visible physical assets are increasingly packaging them as OOH, adding new premium options for brands in capital cities.

pitch.line: Axel Springer's Welt balloon, rising 150m above Berlin, is now a 1,600 sq m ad site, Germany's highest (invidis).

items.headline: Yango Ads puts screens on Dubai's delivery bikes with Flyby
items.dek: Yango Group's advertising arm will sell Flyby's screen-equipped delivery boxes to its international clients, starting in Dubai Marina, JLT, JBR and Bluewaters.
items.source: Yango Ads and Flyby, via invidis
keyPoints: Yango Ads has partnered with UAE-German adtech firm Flyby to sell DOOH screens mounted on delivery motorcycles and vehicles in Dubai.
The launch covers Dubai Marina, Jumeirah Lake Towers, Jumeirah Beach Residence and Bluewaters.
Campaigns can be targeted by location and time of day.
Yango Ads will offer the network to its international advertisers; fleet size and terms were not disclosed.
body: Yango Ads, the advertising technology division of Yango Group, has teamed up with Flyby Advertising to bring mobile DOOH to Dubai. Flyby's 'Smart Delivery Boxes' are digital screens fitted to delivery motorbikes and vehicles, turning the city's courier fleet into a moving screen network.

The first areas covered are Dubai Marina, Jumeirah Lake Towers, Jumeirah Beach Residence and Bluewaters. Campaigns can be triggered by location and time, and Yango Ads will make the inventory available to its international client base. Neither the number of vehicles nor the financial terms were disclosed.
Evgenii Pavlov, Yango Ads' general manager for the Middle East and Africa, described the deal as bringing a bold new format to more brands.
items.relevance: Delivery fleets are a fast-growing, data-friendly form of mobile DOOH in dense Gulf districts. Buyers should ask for verified fleet counts and route data, which are not yet published.

pitch.line: Yango Ads and Flyby are launching delivery-bike DOOH screens across four Dubai districts (invidis).

items.headline: WOO president says trust is OOH's biggest growth lever as scrutiny of social media mounts
items.dek: Opening WOO's Central European Forum in Warsaw, Tom Goddard argued that OOH's standing as a trusted, public medium is its strongest card against embattled online channels, and set out four priorities for growth.
items.source: WOO (World Out of Home Organization)

figures.label: OOH media owners represented by WOO

keyPoints: Tom Goddard, president of the World Out of Home Organization (WOO), called OOH's reputation as the most trusted medium the sector's biggest growth lever.
He said OOH is growing at double-digit rates, led by digital, but still trails online media globally – a gap he expects to narrow over the next five years.
He pointed to regulatory pressure on Big Tech, including under-16 social media bans being considered after Australia's, ad fraud and 'AI slop' as factors eroding trust in online channels.
WOO's four priorities: proving effectiveness, audience measurement and data, ad-tech connectivity, and promoting OOH's competitive advantages.
He called for platform and ad-tech consolidation and more dynamic national trade associations.
body: Tom Goddard, president of the World Out of Home Organization (WOO), used his opening address at the organisation's Central European Forum in Warsaw on 22 October to argue that trust is the strongest growth lever available to OOH. He said the medium is growing at double-digit rates, driven by digital OOH, but still trails online media worldwide – something he expects to change over the next five years and beyond.

Goddard contrasted real-world media with online channels under pressure: several countries are weighing under-16 social media bans following Australia, large fines against Meta mark what he called "Social Media's tobacco moment", and fake impressions, clicks and conversions cost brands billions. He cited a recent Outfront study in the US ranking OOH first for consumer trust, and quoted World Federation of Advertisers chief Stephan Loerke: "Trust is and shall remain marketers' North Star."

He set out four priorities for WOO, which now represents 300 OOH media owners: an industry-wide initiative to prove effectiveness; better audience measurement and data in the many markets that lack unified systems; ad-tech connectivity, with a call for platform consolidation because most trading remains fragmented; and stronger promotion of OOH's advantages, including more dynamic national trade associations.
items.relevance: The trust argument and WOO's planned industry-wide effectiveness initiative give marketers and OOH sellers a ready framing for brand-safety and trust conversations with advertisers. Watch for the effectiveness work as a source of cross-market proof points.

items.headline: WOO adds ten members across five continents, including Pakistan's OOH association
items.dek: The World Out of Home Organization (WOO) has welcomed seven national media owners, two suppliers and one national association, which it links to the momentum from its record London Congress.
items.source: WOO (World Out of Home Organization)
keyPoints: New media-owner members: Yeoul Ad (South Korea), ONEIC Media-Seraj (Oman), Inova Media (Qatar), SkyBlue Group (UAE), Vertex (Monaco), Mobile Media (UK) and Anic Media (Croatia).
Two suppliers joined: ClearLED (USA) and Mortal (New Zealand).
Pakistan's national OOH association, APOAA, also joined, ahead of WOO's first Pakistan Country Forum in Karachi on 5 November.
WOO links the intake to its June London Congress, attended by more than 800 delegates.
body: The World Out of Home Organization (WOO) has added ten members from five continents. Seven are national media owners – Yeoul Ad (Republic of Korea), ONEIC Media-Seraj (Oman), Inova Media (Qatar), SkyBlue Group (UAE), Vertex (Monaco), Mobile Media (UK) and Anic Media (Croatia) – alongside two suppliers, ClearLED (USA) and Mortal (New Zealand), and one national body, Pakistan's APOAA.

WOO connects the intake to its record-breaking London 2026 Congress in June, which drew more than 800 delegates. Chief operating officer Mark Flys said the spread of territories showed OOH sectors worldwide see value in membership, singling out APOAA's arrival ahead of the Pakistan Country Forum in Karachi on 5 November.
The list leans towards the Gulf, with members joining from Oman, Qatar and the UAE, reflecting the region's growing presence in the global real-world media community.
items.relevance: A useful snapshot of who is joining the global OOH conversation, particularly in the Gulf and emerging Asian markets. International sellers can use it to spot potential partners and new national counterparts in multi-market plans.

items.headline: WOO backs Pakistan's first OOH conference and names its first ambassador there
items.dek: The #IRL Conference in Karachi, scheduled for 5 November and run by the Pakistan Advertisers Society with WOO, was billed as the country's first dedicated OOH event, and Kinetic Pakistan's Ahsan Sheikh was named WOO's first ambassador for the market.
items.source: WOO (World Out of Home Organization)
keyPoints: The #IRL Conference ('Be Unskippable, In Real Life') was scheduled for 5 November 2026 in Karachi, presented by the Pakistan Advertisers Society in association with WOO.
It was billed as Pakistan's first dedicated OOH conference and WOO's first Pakistan Country Forum, expecting 250+ delegates from brands, agencies, media owners and government.
Themes: digital OOH and smart cities; measurement, audience data and programmatic trading; creativity, AI-driven production and effectiveness.
Ahsan Sheikh, CEO of Kinetic Pakistan, was named WOO's first ambassador for Pakistan.
body: The World Out of Home Organization (WOO) partnered with the Pakistan Advertisers Society on the #IRL Conference, scheduled for 5 November 2026 at the PC Marquee in Karachi. Announcing it, WOO described the event as Pakistan's first dedicated OOH conference and its own first Pakistan Country Forum, with more than 250 delegates expected from brands, agencies, media owners and government bodies.

The programme was set to cover digital OOH and smart cities; measurement, audience data and programmatic trading; and creativity, AI-driven production and brand effectiveness. Announced international speakers included WOO president Tom Goddard and WOO creative in residence Dino Burbidge. WOO also named Ahsan Sheikh, CEO of Kinetic Pakistan, as its first ambassador for the country; Goddard called Pakistan one of the most exciting emerging OOH markets.

WOO set the event against its latest global figures: OOH spend of $54.2bn in 2025, forecast to reach $56.4bn in 2026, with digital formats close to half of revenues and Asia-Pacific accounting for about 55% of the total.
items.relevance: Pakistan is moving onto the global OOH map, with a national association now inside WOO and a named ambassador as a point of contact. Worth tracking for brands and sellers with South Asian expansion plans, especially around measurement and programmatic readiness.

pitch.line: Global OOH spend reached $54.2bn in 2025 and is forecast to hit $56.4bn in 2026 (WOO).

items.headline: Private deals dominate programmatic DOOH, with retail the leading advertiser category
items.dek: The second report from WOO's inaugural global programmatic DOOH study finds that private marketplace deals and OOH-specialist DSPs account for most spend, suggesting a premium, relationship-led channel.
items.source: WOO (World Out of Home Organization)

figures.label: pDOOH spend via private marketplace deals

keyPoints: Private marketplace (PMP) deals account for 75.7% of global programmatic DOOH spend, pointing to a premium, relationship-driven channel rather than an open-exchange commodity.
OOH-specialist DSPs handle 65.5% of spend versus omnichannel DSPs, showing sector expertise still matters.
Retail, finance and business & industrial lead the advertiser vertical rankings; consumer electronics is the exception, with 72% bought through omnichannel platforms.
Data covers full-year 2025 revenue from 12 SSPs, aggregated by PwC; WOO plans to repeat the study annually.
body: The World Out of Home Organization (WOO) has published the second of two reports from its inaugural Global pDOOH Expenditure Study, covering advertiser verticals, demand-side platforms and transaction types. Its central finding is that programmatic DOOH behaves differently from online programmatic: private marketplace deals make up 75.7% of the $1.339bn global spend, and OOH-specialist DSPs account for 65.5% against omnichannel platforms.

Retail, finance and business & industrial top the vertical rankings. WOO's measurement adviser Gideon Adey of GUROOH attributes retail's lead to the channel's geographic and time-of-day precision, and notes that consumer electronics stands out with a 72% omnichannel share. WOO's Charles Parry-Okeden expects the omnichannel opportunity to grow as consolidated, verified OOH measurement aligns with the wider digital ecosystem.
The data comes from full-year 2025 revenue submitted by 12 SSPs and aggregated by PwC, with scaling factors used where market coverage was incomplete. Both reports are free on registration with WOO.
items.relevance: For buyers, the findings suggest programmatic DOOH is mostly accessed through curated deals and specialist platforms, so planning should allow for PMP set-up rather than assuming open-exchange buying. For sellers, the retail and finance lead offers a starting point for vertical prospecting.

pitch.line: Private marketplace deals account for 75.7% of global programmatic DOOH spend (WOO Global pDOOH Expenditure Study 2026).

study.by: WOO, with data aggregated by PwC
study.markets: 40+ markets across the Americas, EMEA and Asia-Pacific

items.headline: Programmatic DOOH worth $1.34bn worldwide in 2025, just 7% of digital OOH spend
items.dek: WOO's first global programmatic DOOH study puts the US top by volume and Germany top by penetration, and flags Eastern Asia as the biggest untapped opportunity.
items.source: WOO (World Out of Home Organization)
keyPoints: Global programmatic DOOH spend reached $1.339bn in 2025, 7.0% of total DOOH spend.
By region: Americas $667m (14.1% penetration), EMEA $521m (9.4%), Asia-Pacific $151m (1.7%).
The US is the largest market at $545.5m; Germany has the highest penetration of any major market at 31.8%, with Belgium (25.5%) and France (16.7%) also in the top five.
Eastern Asia (Japan, South Korea, mainland China) has a $7.3bn DOOH base but only 0.6% programmatic penetration.
Figures are indicative estimates from 12 SSPs across 40+ markets, aggregated but not audited by PwC.
body: The World Out of Home Organization (WOO) has released the first report of its inaugural Global pDOOH Expenditure Study, dated 14 September 2026. It values programmatic DOOH at $1.339bn in 2025, or 7.0% of global DOOH spend. The Americas lead with $667m (14.1% penetration), ahead of EMEA at $521m (9.4%) and Asia-Pacific at $151m (1.7%).

The US is the biggest market by volume at $545.5m, while Germany shows the highest penetration of any major market at 31.8%. Western Europe overall reached $346.7m at 21.3% penetration, and Australia and New Zealand together account for about 61% of Asia-Pacific spend. The study identifies Eastern Asia – Japan, South Korea and mainland China – as the largest structural growth opportunity, with a $7.3bn DOOH base but only 0.6% bought programmatically.

Twelve SSPs submitted confidential market-level revenue data to PwC, which aggregated and sense-checked it but did not audit it; WOO describes all figures as indicative. Country figures are shown only where at least three SSPs contributed. The report is free on registration.
items.relevance: The study gives the first global benchmark for programmatic DOOH by market, useful for setting realistic automation targets in multi-market plans. The penetration gaps, notably Eastern Asia versus Germany, indicate where programmatic real-world media is most and least mature.

pitch.line: Global programmatic DOOH spend reached $1.339bn in 2025, 7% of all DOOH spend (WOO Global pDOOH Expenditure Study 2026).

study.by: WOO, with data aggregated by PwC
study.markets: 40+ markets across the Americas, EMEA and Asia-Pacific

items.headline: WOO puts regulation on the agenda as European legislators target OOH
items.dek: Ahead of its Warsaw forum, WOO warned that pressure groups and some lawmakers are taking aim at OOH, naming Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Hungary as flash points.
items.source: WOO (World Out of Home Organization)
keyPoints: Pressure groups and some legislators are targeting OOH over its impact on cityscapes and the content of some campaigns, including fossil-fuel advertising.
Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Hungary (after a change of government) are named as flash points.
WOO expects the trend to continue as parties such as the UK Greens gain votes.
Legal and political affairs expert Dr Kai-Marcus Thäsler led the regulation pillar at the Warsaw forum in October.
body: The World Out of Home Organization (WOO) made regulation one of four pillars of its Central European Forum in Warsaw (21–23 October), warning that pressure groups and some legislators are taking aim at OOH. Concerns centre on the medium's impact on urban environments and on the content of high-profile campaigns, including those for fossil fuels.

WOO named Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Hungary – the latter following a change of government – as flash points, and said the pressure is likely to grow as parties such as the Greens in the UK win more votes. Dr Kai-Marcus Thäsler, a legal and political affairs expert, was lined up to address tighter legislation alongside wider pressures such as inflation, government debt and the rise of more extreme parties.
WOO president Tom Goddard said the industry must stay on the right side of legislation so it can grow in an orderly and socially responsible way.
items.relevance: Advertisers in categories under scrutiny, such as fossil fuels, should check local rules before planning European OOH campaigns. Sellers can expect more questions on content standards and self-regulation, particularly in the markets named.

brief: Kearney values beauty, health and wellness at $937bn, with services now outselling products, while B2B marketers shift money into live events as AI search drains their web traffic.

Holiday shoppers on both sides of the Atlantic are budgeting hard: half of Americans plan to spend less, Spaniards cap Black Friday at about €220, and nine Mexicans in ten will shop El Buen Fin on credit.
For OOH, Germany's ma 2026 study now measures four times as many digital small-format screens, Cityz Media takes every Paris bus, and Adams Outdoor keeps buying US billboards.

Diary: SPT's Glasgow bus shelter tender closes on 13 November, Fraport Bulgaria's lounge EOI on 15 November, oOh!media's takeover goes to court on 18 November, and Schiphol's €426m advertising tender closes on 20 November.
editions.take: Today's studies share a theme: people are using AI more but trusting it less with the final decision. Japanese shoppers follow their gut over the algorithm, Americans won't give agents their cards, and brand websites barely feature in AI answers. If machines increasingly mediate the search, the brands that win will be the ones people already know, and that is built in the real world.

numberOfDay.line: Germany's ma 2026 OOH study measures more than 4,500 digital small-format screens, four times last year's count (ag.ma).

steal.title: Close the awareness gap
steal.text: Research for RioMarket finds 36% of Brazilians only discover national films once they are already showing, or gone, and just 31% hear about them before release. The idea worth stealing: sell film distributors a fixed pre-release OOH window, two to three weeks before opening, and measure how many more people know about the film on opening weekend.

items.headline: Beauty becomes a $937bn wellness market, and services now outsell products
items.dek: Kearney's 2027 Beauty Outlook, based on 2,500 consumers in five countries, finds that clinics, medspas and treatments have overtaken the bathroom cabinet. Loyalty is drifting from brands to individual products and the advocates who recommend them.
items.source: Kearney, via PR Newswire
keyPoints: Services now take more than half of global beauty spending, and more than half of monthly spend in four of the five markets studied.
The blended beauty, health and wellness market is worth $937bn and growing by more than 5% a year; beauty products alone account for $430bn.
Fragrance is the fastest-growing category, at 10% a year.
Clinical or aesthetic treatments are a monthly habit for more than a third of consumers.
Product loyalty beats brand loyalty in every market, and advocates increasingly shape how shoppers define their needs.
body: Kearney surveyed 2,500 beauty consumers in France, the UK, China, Japan and the US in June 2026. Its central finding is that the category has outgrown its old boundaries: beauty, health and wellness now form one $937bn market, and services such as dermatology, IV therapy and medspas are growing at around 7% a year, faster than products.
Consumers are about twice as likely to buy beauty for wellness as for self-expression. In the US, cosmetic dermatology and IV therapy each reach 47% of consumers and medspas 43%.

The warning for marketers concerns loyalty. Shoppers are attached to specific products rather than to brands, and advocates and social commerce increasingly decide what people think they need. Kearney also cautions that leaning too heavily on AI for claims and creative risks making brands look alike, and calls for the physical store to be connected to an AI-mediated journey.
items.relevance: When loyalty attaches to products rather than brands, distinctive brand assets matter more, not less. Beauty and wellness brands moving into services need local, physical visibility near clinics, salons and malls, which suits roadside and mall OOH.

pitch.line: Beauty, health and wellness is now a $937bn market, and services take more than half of spending (Kearney).

items.headline: B2B marketers bet on events and owned media as AI search eats their traffic
items.dek: The Content Marketing Institute's 17th annual survey finds 82% of B2B marketers funding live experiences, and nearly a third giving them a large share of budget. Most blame AI search for falling web traffic.
items.source: Content Marketing Institute and MarketingProfs

figures.label: Large share of budget on experiences
Blame AI search for traffic loss

keyPoints: Nearly a third of B2B marketers now put a large or majority share of budget into experiences, up from 17% a year ago.
82% invested in experiential marketing in 2026, and in-person events are the top format.
79% of those seeing traffic decline blame AI search; 42% name owned media as a top investment for 2027, up 10 points.
88% use AI to create content and 59% use AI agents, yet 52% have no policy on disclosing AI use.
Only 60% rate their own marketing as effective.
body: The survey, fielded between June and August 2026, drew 1,132 responses worldwide; the report analyses 861 B2B marketers, most of them in North America. It depicts a profession producing more with AI while losing confidence in the channels that used to carry the content.

The response is a shift towards the physical and the owned. Experiential spending has nearly doubled as a share of budget, and marketers cite brand trust and credibility (43%) and awareness (41%) as the main benefits. Owned media has climbed the investment list as search referrals dry up.
Pressure is rising too: 65% say they have been pushed to produce content faster. WARC's coverage of the same study noted that only 12% strongly agree they are highly effective.
items.relevance: B2B budgets are moving towards real-world presence. OOH sellers can package event-city takeovers, airport and business-district formats around trade shows and conferences, where B2B buyers are concentrated.

pitch.line: 31% of B2B marketers now give experiences a large or majority share of budget, up from 17% (CMI).

chart.title: Share of B2B budget on experiences
chart.unit: % of marketers putting a large or majority share

items.headline: AI shopping answers cite publishers, not brands
items.dek: An analysis of 40,000 unbranded shopping queries finds that brand websites earn only one AI citation in seven. Three answers in four send shoppers to retailers instead.
items.source: OptimizeGEO, via PR Newswire
keyPoints: Brand websites account for only one in seven citations in AI shopping answers; editorial publishers supply 72%.
Three AI shopping 'shelves' in four direct consumers to retailers rather than to brand sites.
More than 15% of products were described inaccurately by the language models.
14% of answers carried an advertisement.
body: OptimizeGEO analysed 40,000 unbranded shopping queries across 12 consumer categories. The release does not specify the period, platforms or markets, and it accompanies a product launch, so the figures are best read as directional.

Even so, the pattern is striking. When shoppers ask AI assistants what to buy, the answers lean on editorial coverage and retailer listings. A brand's own site is a minor input, and a meaningful share of product descriptions is simply wrong.
The findings add to growing evidence that brands are losing control of how they are described at the moment of choice.
items.relevance: If AI intermediaries decide what shoppers see, the brand must already be in the shopper's head before the query is typed. That strengthens the case for broad-reach brand media such as OOH, and for earning editorial coverage that AI engines cite.

pitch.line: Brand websites earn only one AI shopping citation in seven; publishers supply 72% (OptimizeGEO).

items.headline: AECOM tops Brand Finance's first ranking of engineering and design brands
items.dek: The ten most valuable engineering, construction and design advisory brands are worth $12bn combined. Jacobs is the strongest.
items.source: Brand Finance
keyPoints: AECOM leads the new ranking with a brand value of $2.6bn, ahead of Jacobs ($2.3bn) and WSP Global ($2.2bn).
Jacobs is the strongest brand, with a Brand Strength Index of 82.9 out of 100; Arcadis follows on 79.8.
The sector was worth about $202.8bn in 2025 and is forecast to reach $296.2bn by 2035.
Worley, at $1.1bn, is the only Australian brand in the ranking.
body: Brand Finance has added engineering, construction and design advisory to its sector rankings. The top ten brands are worth $12bn between them, led by AECOM, whose brand strength is consistent across the US, the UK and Canada.

Jacobs earns the highest brand-strength score, while Arcadis's equity is particularly strong in continental Europe. The consultancy expects the sector to grow from about $202.8bn in 2025 to $296.2bn by 2035.
items.relevance: Engineering and infrastructure firms compete for talent and public contracts as much as for clients. Airport, transit and business-district OOH reaches the engineers, officials and commuters they need to impress.

pitch.line: AECOM is the world's most valuable engineering and design advisory brand, at $2.6bn (Brand Finance).

chart.title: Most valuable engineering and design brands

items.headline: American shoppers feel poorer but refuse to cancel Christmas
items.dek: Circana's holiday intentions study finds that half of consumers plan to spend less, but three-quarters will trade down and hunt for deals rather than skip the season.
items.source: Circana

figures.label: Rate the economy fair or poor

keyPoints: Half of US consumers (49%) plan to spend less this holiday season, yet close to three-quarters will adapt with cost-saving tactics rather than opt out.
57% rate current economic conditions as fair or poor.
The most common tactics are buying on sale (30%), redeeming rewards points (19%), choosing store brands (18%) and leaning on loyalty programmes (18%).
More than half have already prepared, for example by limiting impulse buys (23%) or shopping for gifts year-round (18%).
Shoppers who rate their own finances as weak are more likely to plan gifts for themselves.
body: Circana's 2026 US Holiday Purchase Intentions Study shows sentiment sliding while commitment to the season holds. The firm's verdict is that consumers are adjusting how they celebrate, not whether they do.
That means more promotions, more own-label and more loyalty redemptions. Preparation has started early, with shoppers cutting back earlier in the year and setting aside dedicated holiday funds.
The self-gifting finding is a reminder that stretched households still look for small rewards.
items.relevance: Value messaging will dominate December, but brands that simply shout discounts risk blending in. Local, near-store OOH can carry retailer reputation and loyalty offers at the moment shoppers decide where to spend a tighter budget.

pitch.line: 49% of US consumers plan to spend less this holiday season, but three-quarters will trade down rather than opt out (Circana).

items.headline: Holiday marketers rediscover television as gift guides and hauls fall from favour
items.dek: Modern Retail's survey of brand and retail marketers finds planned use of CTV doubling and linear TV rising sharply. Brand experiences slip but remain among the best performers.
items.source: Modern Retail+ Research
keyPoints: Planned use of CTV and streaming ads this holiday season nearly doubles to 45%, and TV ads jump from 13% to 33%.
Brand experiences fall from 50% to 41% and lose the top spot.
Gift guides drop 19 points and influencer hauls and unboxing videos 14 points.
Historically, gift guides (31%), brand experiences (28%) and pop-up shops have performed best.
body: Modern Retail+ Research surveyed 90 brand and retail professionals and interviewed marketing executives about their holiday plans. The headline is a swing back to the big screen: CTV and linear TV are the fastest-rising tactics.

Social-first tactics such as gift guides and influencer hauls are being cut, even though gift guides have historically been the best performer. Brand experiences have slipped but still rank second, and pop-up shops third, among tactics that have worked.
items.relevance: Holiday budgets are moving to broad-reach video. OOH sellers can pitch roadside and DOOH as the outdoor complement to CTV, and keep pop-ups and experiences in the plan, since marketers still rate them among their best performers.

pitch.line: Planned use of CTV in US holiday marketing rises from 23% to 45% (Modern Retail+ Research).

chart.title: Holiday tactics planned, 2026 vs 2025

items.headline: Americans use AI agents every week, but won't hand them a credit card
items.dek: A survey of 2,026 US adults finds two-thirds use an AI agent weekly, yet half are uncomfortable letting one pay. If fraud occurs, most would blame the AI company.
items.source: SEON, via GlobeNewswire

figures.label: Uneasy letting an agent use their card
Would blame the AI firm for fraud

keyPoints: 68% of Americans use an AI agent at least weekly, but half are uncomfortable letting one use their card.
Discomfort is generational: 65% of Boomers object, against 34% of Millennials.
Only 15% would share financial information with an agent, and 32% would share nothing at all.
65% would blame the AI company if an agent committed fraud.
Human support is the top trust-builder (50%); 23% say nothing would raise their trust.
body: The online survey, conducted between 2 and 6 October 2026 and weighted on nine variables, comes from SEON, a fraud-prevention company, so its focus on risk is unsurprising. Still, the gap between use and trust is wide.

Americans happily use agents to research and organise, but stop at payment. 43% lack confidence in judging whether an agent's request is legitimate, and access to a human remains the most reassuring safeguard.
items.relevance: Agentic commerce is arriving more slowly than retailers hope. Brands still need to win the human who approves the purchase, which keeps brand familiarity and trust, built through visible media such as OOH, at the centre of the plan.

pitch.line: 68% of Americans use an AI agent weekly, but half won't let one use their card (SEON).

items.headline: Five holiday shopper tribes, from Black Friday bargain-hunters to Christmas Eve stragglers
items.dek: SalesFuel's AudienceSCAN profiles the season's key shopping days and the media that reach each group. Streaming TV and social reach about half of each audience.
items.source: SalesFuel AdMall, via GlobeNewswire
keyPoints: A quarter of US adults plan to shop on Cyber Monday, and 22% are in-store Black Friday shoppers.
Small Business Saturday draws 17% of adults; local media helps 23% of them discover new businesses, and 32.5% have household incomes above $150,000.
Super Saturday (19 December) attracts 12%, and 31% of that group try to buy American.
17% will shop on Christmas Eve, and about a quarter of them buy something for themselves.
Streaming TV and social network ads reach roughly half of every group.
body: SalesFuel's AudienceSCAN data splits the US holiday season into five shopper audiences, each with a distinct profile. Black Friday in-store shoppers are frequent store visitors, with 24% shopping at retail stores twice a week.

Cyber Monday shoppers are reached through social and search ads (41% each), and 51% have recently bought online for pickup. Small Business Saturday shoppers are the most affluent, and lean on local media for discovery.
items.relevance: Each shopping day has its own audience, and in-store days favour media near the shop. OOH sellers can build day-parted packages around Black Friday, Small Business Saturday and the last-minute rush, particularly near retail parks and high streets.

pitch.line: 17% of US adults shop on Small Business Saturday, and local media helps 23% of them find new businesses (AudienceSCAN).

chart.title: US adults planning to shop, by day

items.headline: US marketing hiring recovers, and brand-marketing jobs rise 17.5%
items.dek: An analysis of nearly 84,000 in-house job listings finds US marketing vacancies up 9% year on year in the third quarter, with entry-level roles rebounding and salaries climbing.
items.source: Taligence and Aspen Technology Labs, via PR Newswire
keyPoints: US in-house marketing vacancies stood at 36,832 at the end of September, up 9% on a year earlier.
Growth marketing roles rose 20.2%, product marketing 18.0% and brand marketing 17.5%.
The median advertised salary rose 14% to $97,500.
Entry-level vacancies rose 10.2% on the quarter, while C-suite openings fell 14.3%.
New York vacancies were up 22%.
body: Taligence and Aspen Technology Labs tracked 83,916 active full-time in-house marketing listings drawn from employer career sites and applicant-tracking systems during the third quarter.

After a difficult period, hiring is turning up. Director-level-and-above roles rose 15.5% year on year, and junior roles are rebounding. Product marketers command a median advertised salary of almost $164,000.
items.relevance: Rising demand for brand marketers suggests advertisers are rebuilding brand capability after a period dominated by performance. That is a good backdrop for brand-building media such as OOH heading into 2027 planning.

pitch.line: US brand-marketing job vacancies rose 17.5% year on year in Q3 2026 (Taligence).

items.headline: Britain's Gen X holds a third of the wealth, but only 12% feel seen by advertisers
items.dek: Research from The Guardian and Initiative finds the generation born between 1965 and 1980 overlooked by marketers despite its spending power and seniority at work.
items.source: The Media Leader, on The Guardian and Initiative research
keyPoints: Gen X makes up 26% of the UK population and holds 33% of household wealth, yet only 12% feel consistently well represented in advertising.
Gen X is the least happy generation, scoring 5.7 out of 10, almost a point below the others.
Only 30% believe they are wealthier than their parents, compared with 57% of Boomers and 49% of Millennials.
Gen X holds 37% of founder or owner roles and 40% of senior director roles.
56% of Gen X parents with adult children still have them living at home.
body: 'Generation Remix: Meet Gen X in Midlife' surveyed 2,900 people, including 2,000 members of Gen X, and conducted 14 in-depth interviews. It portrays a squeezed but powerful cohort: decision-makers at work and at home, yet largely absent from advertising.
Financial pressure is real: 29% have struggled with personal debt in the past five years. So is reinvention: 45% have made a major professional change. Many are supporting adult children at home.
items.relevance: Gen X is a large, affluent and under-served audience that commutes, drives and still notices traditional media. Advertisers and OOH sellers can build commuter and roadside plans aimed at midlife decision-makers instead of defaulting to youth targeting.

pitch.line: Gen X holds 33% of UK household wealth, but only 12% feel well represented in advertising (Guardian/Initiative).

items.headline: Storms drive UK footfall down 4.7% in October, with high streets hit hardest
items.dek: The BRC–Sensormatic monitor recorded the steepest fall since April. High streets lost 5.2% of visitors as shoppers stayed home or chose places with easier parking.
items.source: FashionUnited, on the BRC–Sensormatic Footfall Monitor
keyPoints: UK footfall fell 4.7% year on year in October, the steepest decline since April, after a 2.9% fall in September.
High streets fell 5.2%, shopping centres 4.1% and retail parks 3.6%.
Wales suffered most (−6.3%), followed by England (−4.6%), Scotland (−4.3%) and Northern Ireland (−3.1%).
Halloween gave only a brief lift.
body: The British Retail Consortium and Sensormatic measured footfall from 4 to 31 October 2026. Stormy weather and low consumer confidence kept shoppers at home or pushed them towards destinations with easier parking.
Retail parks held up best, though they too weakened compared with September. The figures arrive just as retailers enter the Black Friday and Christmas trading period.
items.relevance: Weak footfall is a challenge for retailers and for high-street OOH audiences alike. Sellers should expect advertisers to ask for audience guarantees, and can point to retail parks' relative resilience; for retailers, reaching people on the move before they choose where to shop matters more when visits are scarce.

pitch.line: UK retail footfall fell 4.7% in October 2026, and 5.2% on high streets (BRC–Sensormatic).

chart.title: UK footfall, October 2026, year on year

items.headline: M&S wins the early Christmas ad vote, but shoppers would rather have lower prices
items.dek: OnePulse's tracker rates M&S's festive ad highest among the supermarkets. Majorities of some audiences say the money would be better spent on cutting prices.
items.source: OnePulse, Christmas Ad Tracker 2026
keyPoints: M&S leads with a 4.0 out of 5 rating; 74% liked or loved its ad and 58% said it made them more likely to shop there.
Aldi scores 3.9, Sainsbury's 3.8, Tesco 3.6, Lidl 3.5 and Asda 3.3.
56% of Sainsbury's viewers and 54% of Lidl's would rather the money went on lower prices.
73% want Aldi's Kevin the Carrot back next year, up from 63% before launch.
71% said Tesco's celebrity casting worked, although only 17% wanted famous faces beforehand.
body: OnePulse asks about 500 UK adults to rate each supermarket ad within hours of release, on a five-point scale, alongside a pre-launch survey of about 1,500 adults. The early results favour M&S and Aldi, whose long-running character continues to build affection.

The tension is price. Retail Gazette, citing OnePulse, reports that 57% of consumers would prefer retailers to spend less on Christmas ads and cut prices, and 61% say a Christmas ad has never changed where they do their main festive food shop.
items.relevance: Christmas storytelling still builds warmth, but shoppers want value too. Supermarkets can pair TV storytelling with price and availability messages in roadside and near-store OOH, where the shopping decision is closer.

pitch.line: M&S tops OnePulse's early Christmas ad ratings at 4.0/5, with 74% liking or loving its ad.

chart.title: Supermarket Christmas ad ratings

items.headline: Germany's new OOH currency counts 266,000 sites, and digital small screens have quadrupled
items.dek: The ma 2026 OOH study, built on 77,703 people's travel, now covers more than 4,500 digital small-format screens. OOH spending is rising faster than the wider market.
items.source: invidis, on ag.ma's ma 2026 OOH
keyPoints: Germany's official OOH audience study now covers about 266,000 advertising sites, including about 10,000 digital roadside products.
More than 4,500 digital small-format screens are measured, over four times as many as last year.
The study is built on the mobility of 77,703 people aged 14 and over, including 17,501 tracked by GPS for two weeks.
Nielsen data show gross OOH advertising investment up 5.8% in January to September 2026.
body: The Arbeitsgemeinschaft Media-Analyse (ag.ma) has published ma 2026 OOH, the joint currency for German OOH. More than 60,000 people described their trips on maps and a further 17,501 carried GPS trackers for two weeks; the data are combined to give performance values for classic posters, city-lights, columns and digital formats.

The rapid growth in measured digital small-format screens reflects the expansion of DOOH in stations, malls and street furniture. ag.ma presents the study as giving uniform metrics and transparency, positioning OOH as a core part of the media mix.
items.relevance: A larger, more digital currency makes German OOH easier to plan and buy alongside online media. International advertisers and sellers can use ma figures as a model for how measured DOOH inventory supports programmatic and cross-media planning.

pitch.line: Germany's ma 2026 OOH study measures over 4,500 digital small-format screens, four times last year's count (ag.ma).

items.headline: France's creator economy reaches $10.1bn, the world's seventh-largest
items.dek: A report launched at Paris Creator Week values the French market up almost a quarter in a year. Advertisers fund nearly four-fifths of the global creator economy.
items.source: CB News, on the Creator Economy Report 2026
keyPoints: France's creator economy is worth $10.1bn in 2026, up 23.7%, making it the world's seventh-largest.
France accounts for 24.7% of the European market and 4.6% of the global one.
The global market is worth $217.3bn, up 26.2%, and creators keep 42.6% of it.
Partnerships and sponsorships make up 49.8% of global revenue; advertisers' share of the market has risen from 77.2% in 2021 to 79.5%.
The French sector supports about 227,000 full-time-equivalent jobs.
body: The Creator Economy Report 2026, produced by Coherent Market Insights with BNP Paribas and Influential, combines economic modelling with 369 interviews with creators, platforms, agencies and advertisers.

Its picture is of an advertiser-funded industry growing far faster than media overall. Partnerships dominate revenue, followed by advertising income on content (22.7%) and subscriptions (13.8%). The French market's direct value added equals 0.17% of GDP.
items.relevance: Creator budgets are coming partly out of traditional media. OOH sellers can respond by offering formats that amplify creator campaigns in public space, turning a social idea into a city-wide moment.

pitch.line: France's creator economy is worth $10.1bn in 2026, up 23.7% (Creator Economy Report 2026).

study.by: Coherent Market Insights with BNP Paribas and Influential

items.headline: Young French users love Google's AI answers, and click through less
items.dek: iProspect and dentsu find 87% of 18–34s rate AI Overviews useful. Clicks to websites are falling in every age group.
items.source: CB News, on iProspect and dentsu research
keyPoints: 87% of French 18–34s find Google's AI Overviews useful, against 71% of all adults.
Clicks to websites are falling across all ages, reported by 44% of 18–34s and 35% of over-65s.
Nearly one French adult in three already uses Google's AI for purchase searches.
Only about one in three often or always checks the cited sources.
body: dentsu Insights surveyed a representative sample of 1,001 French adults online in September 2026 for iProspect's 'Future of Search' special edition. Nearly two-thirds of 18–34s often or always read the AI answers.
Awareness is high across generations: 84% of over-65s already know Google's AI. A minority (18%) say they click through more than before to verify information.
items.relevance: Search is becoming an answer engine that keeps users on the results page. Brands need to be known before the search begins, a job for awareness media such as OOH, and to be cited by the sources AI relies on.

pitch.line: 87% of French 18–34s find Google's AI Overviews useful, and clicks to websites are falling (iProspect/dentsu).

items.headline: Italian shoppers juggle five retail touchpoints, and the paper leaflet still holds its own
items.dek: YouGov's panel of 18,000 households finds paper and digital leaflets reaching the same share of families. In-store screens lag far behind.
items.source: Engage, on YouGov Shopper
keyPoints: Paper leaflets reach 51.6% of Italian families and digital leaflets 51.4%: the printed flyer is holding its ground.
Families visit 9.5 retailers on average, hold six loyalty cards and use 5.5 retailer touchpoints.
Shoppers using five or six channels generate 60.7% of grocery and household spending.
In-store digital screens and totems are used by only 15.5% of shoppers on average.
Young adults without children prefer digital leaflets (64% vs 41%); retirees prefer paper (51% vs 41%).
body: YouGov Shopper's consumer panel covers more than 18,000 Italian households, representing 26.5m families. It describes a disloyal, multi-channel shopper who spreads spending across many retailers and touchpoints.

Personalised offers matter: 43.6% use offers in apps or loyalty areas and 37.5% use coupons based on past purchases. Half use loyalty schemes and digital coupons, rising to 63% among families with young children.
items.relevance: Retail media is fragmenting across many touchpoints, and physical ones still reach half of families. OOH and in-store media sellers should sell reach and frequency across channels rather than single screens, which on their own reach few shoppers.

pitch.line: Paper leaflets still reach 51.6% of Italian families, level with digital ones (YouGov Shopper).

items.headline: Italian cinema advertising rises by two-thirds as audiences return
items.dek: FCP-Associnema reports cinema ad revenue up 66.4% in the first nine months of 2026. A Havas study puts cinema ad recall at almost three times that of TV.
items.source: Engage, on FCP-Associnema data
keyPoints: Italian cinema advertising revenue rose 66.4% in January to September 2026, and 54.5% in September alone.
A Havas study presented at the Intersections conference found cinema ad recall almost three times that of TV.
The figures come from FCP-Associnema, the cinema arm of Italy's federation of advertising concessionaires.
body: Cinema is one of the fastest-growing media in Italy this year. FCP-Associnema's figures show strong growth through the autumn, and the Havas research gives advertisers an attention-based reason to follow the audience back into theatres.
The trend echoes France, where CNC data show cinema admissions up 17.1% in October and 24.8% for the year to date.
items.relevance: High-attention venue media are winning budgets as audiences return. OOH sellers can bundle cinema-adjacent formats, such as mall, multiplex and leisure-district screens, with cinema buys to extend high-recall campaigns.

pitch.line: Italian cinema advertising revenue rose 66.4% in January to September 2026 (FCP-Associnema).

items.headline: Spaniards plan to spend more on almost everything, and kitchen budgets nearly double
items.dek: Observatorio Cetelem finds purchase intentions rising in most sectors for the coming year. Physical shops still take more than two-thirds of purchases.
items.source: Marketing4eCommerce, on Observatorio Cetelem
keyPoints: Purchase intentions for the next 12 months rise by one to three points in most sectors, with travel (78%) and sport (77%) the only declines.
Planned spending on kitchens jumps 86% to €1,867, while renovation budgets slip 6%.
42% prefer large chains and 27% local shops, against 30% who prefer to buy online.
47% of online buyers returned something last year; clothing and footwear account for about half of returns.
Tech (39%) and travel (29%) are the products most bought with AI help, but 46% still prefer human assistants to chatbots.
body: Cetelem's 'Dinámicas del consumo en España 2026' paints a cautiously optimistic consumer. Intentions are edging up across most categories, led by the home.
Research is part of the routine: 48.1% look for recommendations before buying. AI is entering the journey for higher-value purchases, but human help remains preferred.
items.relevance: Most Spanish purchases still happen in shops, so media near the point of sale stays important. Home and kitchen brands entering a stronger year can use OOH near retail parks and DIY destinations to capture rising intent.

pitch.line: Spaniards plan to spend 86% more on kitchens in the coming year, €1,867 on average (Observatorio Cetelem).

items.headline: Nine Spaniards in ten will join Black Friday, with an average budget of €220
items.dek: Klarna's research finds Spanish shoppers planning ahead and setting budgets. Tech, fashion and beauty lead the gift list.
items.source: Europa Press via PressDigital, on Klarna research

figures.label: Plan a week or more ahead

keyPoints: 91% of Spanish consumers say they take part in Black Friday and Cyber Week, and plan to spend about €220 on average.
79% set a budget, and 37% expect to spend more than €200.
55% start organising purchases at least a week before the offers begin.
21% will buy most or all their tech gifts during the sales, ahead of fashion (18%) and beauty (14%).
27% use the discounts to bring forward purchases planned for later in the year.
body: Klarna's research describes a disciplined Black Friday shopper in Spain: most budget, plan early and combine savings tools, with 23% stacking discount codes, cashback and loyalty benefits.
The article does not give the sample size or fieldwork dates, so the figures are best read as indicative.
items.relevance: Spanish shoppers decide early, so Black Friday messages need to land in the week before the sales. OOH booked from mid-November can catch budget-setters at the planning stage.

pitch.line: Spanish shoppers plan to spend about €220 on Black Friday and Cyber Week, and 91% will take part (Klarna).

items.headline: A quarter of Japanese shoppers buy with AI's help, but most still trust their gut
items.dek: Rakuten Insight finds 25.6% of Japanese adults used AI to help with a purchase in the past year. When AI and instinct disagree, instinct usually wins.
items.source: MarkeZine, on Rakuten Insight research
keyPoints: When AI advice and intuition conflict, 48.8% of Japanese AI shoppers follow their instinct and only 13.4% follow the AI.
25.6% of Japanese adults used AI to help buy something in the past year.
Shoppers want AI to suggest things that suit them (51.2%), save time (40.4%) and avoid mistakes (34.0%).
20.7% have had a bad experience after following AI advice, and 34.5% say choosing has become less fun.
32.2% worry AI will make everyone's choices the same.
body: Rakuten Insight screened 5,000 people aged 20 to 69 and surveyed 1,003 who had used AI to research or buy, between 24 and 28 July 2026. Daily goods and appliances were the most common AI-assisted purchases (10.0%).

Most see AI as a search engine or dictionary (53.4%), rising to 63.6% among people in their 60s. A quarter of people in their 20s describe it as a friend, yet even this group is the most likely to follow intuition (53.9%).
items.relevance: AI is a research tool in Japan, not a decision-maker. Brands still win at the moment of instinct, which is shaped by familiarity built in the real world, from station media to roadside screens.

pitch.line: When AI and intuition disagree, 48.8% of Japanese shoppers follow their gut and only 13.4% the AI (Rakuten Insight).

chart.title: When AI advice and intuition conflict

items.headline: India's festive shoppers came to buy, not browse, and paid media got dearer
items.dek: HiveMinds' campaign data show returns soaring for brands that captured high-intent demand, while marketplace click costs rose up to 2.5 times.
items.source: MediaNews4U, on HiveMinds analysis
keyPoints: Indian festive shoppers arrived ready to buy: in electronics, the first four sale days delivered about 60% of the whole event's sales.
Click costs on Flipkart rose up to 2.5 times normal, and generic searches lost half their efficiency.
Fashion needed about ten times the spend for six times the sales.
Conversion in electronics halved from 4% to 2% when delivery slipped from next-day to four to seven days.
Home-care multi-packs rose from about 25% to over 40% of sales.
body: HiveMinds, a performance-marketing agency, drew on its client campaigns rather than a market-wide survey, so the numbers are illustrative. One two-wheeler brand on Flipkart earned about 48 times its ad spend during the festival, against about six times in a normal month.
The lesson is about timing and intent. Demand was concentrated in the opening days, and delivery speed shaped conversion as much as price.
items.relevance: Festive performance spend gets expensive fast. Brands that build awareness before the sale with OOH and other reach media can lower their reliance on costly marketplace clicks when demand peaks.

pitch.line: Flipkart click costs rose up to 2.5 times normal during India's 2026 festive sales (HiveMinds).

items.headline: Double 11 loses its sparkle in Taiwan as constant promotions dull the festival
items.dek: Eastern Online finds only 15% of Taiwanese consumers eagerly awaiting Singles' Day. Most will decide on the strength of the discounts.
items.source: China Times, on Eastern Online research
keyPoints: Only 15% of Taiwanese consumers are highly looking forward to Double 11, and 41.4% say promotions are now so frequent that the festival no longer feels special.
14.2% are sure they will take part; 43.6% will decide based on the discounts.
60.6% will compare prices, rising to 70.9% of people in their 20s.
38.5% have bought something unplanned after seeing a special price.
59.8% will spend the same as last year, 22.8% more and 9.3% less.
body: Eastern Online's survey shows Singles' Day maturing into one promotion among many. Daily consumables (45.7%), food and drink (35.7%) and electronics (31.3%) top shopping lists.
A separate LINE Shopping survey found 54.2% of Taiwanese shoppers wait for shopping festivals to buy, so the events still matter, even if the excitement has faded.
items.relevance: Promotion fatigue is spreading across Asia's shopping festivals, echoing global findings on Black Friday. Brands need reasons beyond price to stand out, and memorable public-space creative can restore some of the event's sense of occasion.

pitch.line: Only 15% of Taiwanese consumers are eagerly awaiting Double 11 (Eastern Online).

items.headline: Collingwood is Australia's most valuable club brand as the Brisbane Lions close in
items.dek: Brand Finance values AFL and NRL club brands at A$2.9bn combined. Collingwood takes the cross-code crown from Penrith.
items.source: Brand Finance

figures.label: AFL and NRL club brands combined

keyPoints: Collingwood is the most valuable club brand across both codes, at A$144m, taking the title from the Penrith Panthers (A$140m).
AFL and NRL club brands are worth A$2.9bn combined.
The Brisbane Lions rose 14% to A$132m after a third successive premiership, and the Brisbane Broncos 11% to A$133m.
West Coast Eagles grew fastest, up 19% to A$95m.
Collingwood (91.3) and the Broncos (90.7) are the strongest brands.
body: Brand Finance's annual ranking of Australia's two main football codes shows AFL clubs gaining ground. Collingwood leads on both value and strength, while Brisbane, home to both the Lions and the Broncos, has two of the four most valuable club brands.
Some NRL brands slipped: Melbourne Storm fell 2% and the Sydney Roosters 3%.
items.relevance: Sports clubs are powerful brand platforms for sponsors, and stadium and roadside media around match days reach their fans. Brisbane's rise is relevant to sellers in a city preparing for the 2032 Olympics.

pitch.line: Collingwood is Australia's most valuable football club brand, at A$144m (Brand Finance).

chart.title: Most valuable AFL and NRL club brands

items.headline: South African grocery shoppers are happier, and print still sparks the shopping list
items.dek: Caxton's Project EAT finds far fewer shoppers distressed by grocery costs than in 2023. Delivery apps have become the fourth-largest 'retailer'.
items.source: Bizcommunity, on Caxton Media's Project EAT 2026

figures.label: Look for deals in printed brochures

keyPoints: Shoppers feeling 'very bad' about grocery costs fell from 61% in 2023 to 29%.
Grocery delivery apps are now the fourth-largest 'retailer' in South Africa.
Before shopping, 70% look for deals online, 64% in catalogues and 59% in printed brochures or newspapers.
Print inspires more meal choices (25%) than social media (21%) or AI (4%).
Home-cooked main meals rose from 82% to 87%, and restaurant meals fell from 5% to 2%.
body: Caxton Media interviewed 3,000 grocery shoppers in every province, 100 a day between 10 August and 8 September 2026, and compared the results with 2023. Shoppers visit stores more often: 57% shop on an average day, up from 43%, while monthly bulk shopping holds at 45%.
Loyalty is near-universal, with cards used by 88% of in-store and 78% of app shoppers. In store, shelf pricing (47%) remains the main influence.
items.relevance: Physical and printed media still drive grocery decisions in South Africa. Brands and OOH sellers can plan near-store and commuter formats alongside print and digital, since frequent, smaller shopping trips put shoppers on the move more often.

pitch.line: Only 29% of South African shoppers now feel 'very bad' about grocery costs, down from 61% in 2023 (Caxton Project EAT).

items.headline: 85% of UAE workers use AI, far ahead of Europe and North America
items.dek: The Oliver Wyman Forum finds UAE adoption well above the global norm, with most residents also using AI for health and money decisions.
items.source: The National, on Oliver Wyman Forum research
keyPoints: 85% of UAE workers use AI at work, against 72% in North America and 66% in Europe.
Nearly half use it daily, compared with 21% internationally.
67% fear losing their job to AI, yet 42% would prefer an AI colleague or manager.
About eight in ten use AI for health, and around two-thirds use it to guide investments.
body: The UAE edition of the Oliver Wyman Forum's '300,000 voices' research draws on 5,285 participants over five years and a 503-person survey in April 2026. It shows the Emirates among the world's most enthusiastic adopters of AI.
Enthusiasm sits alongside anxiety: two-thirds fear for their jobs even as many welcome AI as a co-worker.
items.relevance: UAE consumers will meet brands through AI assistants sooner than most. Advertisers there need strong brand recall to be the name people ask for, and the Gulf's premium OOH inventory is well placed to build it.

pitch.line: 85% of UAE workers use AI at work, against 66% in Europe (Oliver Wyman Forum).

items.headline: Nine Mexicans in ten shop El Buen Fin, and eight in ten pay with credit
items.dek: Ipsos finds El Buen Fin far ahead of Hot Sale and Black Friday in Mexico. Shoppers split evenly between stores and online, and favour home-grown brands.
items.source: El Economista via ANTAD, on Ipsos research

figures.label: Prefer a Mexican brand at equal price

keyPoints: 90% of Mexicans usually shop during El Buen Fin, against 70% for Hot Sale and 52% for Black Friday.
Eight in ten pay with credit; 44% use savings, 20% work extra hours and 12% take out a loan.
92% compare prices before buying, and six in ten set a budget.
Purchases split roughly evenly between physical stores and online, and 72% of store shoppers check promotions online first.
At equal price, 76% would choose a Mexican brand, and 89% recognise the 'Hecho en México' seal.
body: Ipsos México surveyed 500 adults aged 18 to 74 online ahead of El Buen Fin, which runs from 13 to 17 November. The most common budget is 1,000 to 4,999 pesos, spent mainly on fashion accessories, appliances and electronics.
Shoppers are drawn by the number of promotions (54%) and by payment and financing options (53%). Direct discounts motivate 61%, interest-free instalments 23%.
items.relevance: Mexico's biggest sales event is omnichannel and credit-driven. Retailers and banks can use OOH near malls and on commuter routes to carry financing and 'Hecho en México' messages to shoppers who plan online and buy in store.

pitch.line: 90% of Mexicans usually shop during El Buen Fin, far ahead of Black Friday's 52% (Ipsos).

items.headline: Brazilians discover national films too late, often after they've left cinemas
items.dek: Research for RioMarket finds 36% learn of Brazilian films only once they are already showing, or gone. Only 31% hear about them in the weeks before release.
items.source: Mundo do Marketing, on Casa Mundo Latam and RioMarket research

figures.label: Say Brazilian cinema is in a good phase

keyPoints: 36% of Brazilians discover national films only when they are already showing, about to leave cinemas or on streaming.
77% say Brazilian cinema is in a good phase, but only 26% name a national film among recent trips.
Only 31% hear about releases a few weeks or days before opening.
Trailers and scenes (54.2%) and TV advertising (43.8%) are the main ways people learn about films.
Going out (42.1%) and big-screen immersion (35.8%) are the main reasons to visit a cinema.
body: Casa Mundo Latam conducted 18 in-depth interviews and 240 online interviews across Brazil in September 2026 for RioMarket, the Festival do Rio's industry market. The study is small and unweighted, but the finding is clear: goodwill towards Brazilian cinema is not turning into tickets because awareness arrives too late.
Price is the main barrier (42.1%), followed by the cost of food and drink (30%). Yet 55.8% go to the cinema at least monthly.
items.relevance: Film launches are a classic OOH category, and this is evidence of the awareness gap. OOH sellers can pitch distributors on pre-release bursts that put titles in the street two to three weeks before opening.

pitch.line: 36% of Brazilians only discover national films once they are already in cinemas, or gone (RioMarket).

items.headline: Chile's consumers are the gloomiest in Latin America
items.dek: Ipsos's monthly index ranks Chile 28th of 30 countries for consumer confidence. Brazil, Peru and Mexico are the region's most upbeat.
items.source: Mediabanco, on the Ipsos Consumer Confidence Index

figures.label: Know someone who lost a job

keyPoints: Chile's consumer confidence index fell to 38.8 in October, the third-lowest of 30 countries and the lowest in Latin America.
It is the second time this year below 40, last seen in 2023; the index is down 4.2 points on the year.
57% of Chileans say they or someone close lost a job in the past six months.
Across the region, Brazil scores 54.1, Peru 52.9, Mexico 52.7, Colombia 49.7 and Argentina 40.4; the Latin American average is 48.1.
body: Ipsos measures consumer confidence monthly across 30 economies. Chile's slide contrasts with a slightly improving regional average (+0.5 points).
Job insecurity is the main drag: only 32% of Chileans feel more secure about their job.
items.relevance: Confidence varies widely across Latin America, so one regional media plan will not fit. Advertisers can lean into value and reassurance in Chile and Argentina, while Brazil and Mexico offer more room for growth messaging.

pitch.line: Chile's consumer confidence fell to 38.8 in October, the lowest in Latin America (Ipsos).

chart.title: Ipsos consumer confidence, October 2026

items.headline: Oman Duty Free and China's CTG Duty-Free agree to work together
items.dek: The two airport retailers have signed a memorandum to share expertise and explore merchandise supply and franchising.
items.source: TRBusiness
keyPoints: Oman Duty Free and CTG Duty-Free have signed an MOU to share know-how and explore supply and franchising.
A joint working group will follow to take the co-operation forward.
The deal links a Gulf airport retailer with the world's largest travel-retail group by sales.
body: The memorandum is a framework rather than a contract, but it shows Chinese travel-retail groups looking for partners beyond the mainland, and Gulf operators seeking scale in sourcing.
The two sides will explore merchandise supply arrangements and franchising, through a joint working group.
items.relevance: Partnerships like this can change the brand mix in airport stores. Airport media sellers in the Gulf should watch for Chinese brands and a Chinese traveller focus that could bring new advertisers.

pitch.line: Oman Duty Free and CTG Duty-Free have signed an MOU to explore supply and franchising (TRBusiness).

items.headline: Cityz Media takes every Paris bus as Metrobus's 76-year reign ends
items.dek: Since 1 November Cityz Media sells advertising on all twelve Île-de-France bus concessions, including RATP's 3,500-bus central-Paris network. It has launched a new mobility unit.
items.source: The Media Leader FR
keyPoints: Cityz Media now sells advertising on 100% of buses in Paris and Île-de-France, ending Metrobus's 76-year run.
The final switch came on 1 November, when the RATP Cap Île-de-France lots covering central Paris changed hands.
Cityz Media targets at least €20m of revenue in 2027 from the twelve concessions.
Nationally it claims nearly 13,000 buses and more than 40,000 faces, close to three French advertising buses in four.
A new unit, Cityz Media Mobility, will manage the business.
body: Cityz Media, formerly Clear Channel France, won the RATP Cap Île-de-France contract in autumn 2025 and has since collected the other Île-de-France operators' bus concessions, including those of Transdev, Keolis and ATM.
Local advertisers already provide 15% of revenue on the Paris lots. Cityz Media Mobility is modelled on its retail-media unit and relies on a new production platform in Nanterre opened in July.
items.relevance: A single seller for all Paris-region buses simplifies buying for advertisers. For rivals, it shows how a challenger can build scale quickly by winning a series of transit concessions as they are re-tendered.

pitch.line: Cityz Media now sells advertising on all 12 Île-de-France bus concessions, ending Metrobus's 76-year run.

items.headline: Adams Outdoor keeps buying as US roadside consolidation continues
items.dek: Adams has added billboard portfolios in Myrtle Beach and western Pennsylvania, and more than 1,600 faces this year. New Tradition has bought into Las Vegas.
items.source: Billboard Insider
keyPoints: Adams Outdoor has added more than 1,600 faces since January, including nearly 90 digital, and now runs more than 12,000 faces in 14 states.
It has bought Haynes Sign Co's 115 faces on 60 structures around Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, 11 of them digital.
It has also closed the purchase of Penneco Outdoor's 83 faces in western Pennsylvania, 15 of them on the Pennsylvania Turnpike.
Separately, New Tradition has acquired Connell Outdoor's 88 faces on routes from Harry Reid International Airport to the Las Vegas Strip.
body: The deals, announced between 3 and 5 November, show private roadside operators continuing to consolidate local portfolios. Prices were not disclosed.

The Penneco deal lifts Adams to more than 1,160 faces in eastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania. New Tradition's Las Vegas purchase also includes two faces near LAX, according to OOH Today and Billboard Insider.
items.relevance: Consolidation gives national buyers fewer, larger roadside partners in secondary US markets. Regional brands should expect more digital inventory and more professional selling as acquirers upgrade portfolios.

pitch.line: Adams Outdoor has added more than 1,600 billboard faces in 2026 and now runs 12,000+ in 14 states (Billboard Insider).

links.label: OOH Today: Adams buys Haynes Sign Co
Billboard Insider: New Tradition buys Connell Outdoor

items.headline: Ocean Outdoor unveils Birmingham's biggest digital screen
items.dek: The Lancaster Circus Banners pair a 500 sq m main screen with two portrait banners, under Ocean's long-term contract with Birmingham City Council. Nintendo is the launch advertiser.
items.source: invidis
keyPoints: Ocean Outdoor's Lancaster Circus Banners combine a 500 sq m main screen with two 60 sq m portrait banners.
The site sits under Ocean's long-term OOH contract with Birmingham City Council.
Ocean now operates 242 screens in Birmingham; Nintendo is the launch partner.
body: The new landmark adds a premium large-format digital site on one of Birmingham's main road gateways. invidis reported the launch on 6 November, after Outsmart listed it earlier in the week.
It strengthens Ocean's presence in the UK's second city, where its council partnership covers a large network of digital screens.
items.relevance: Landmark digital sites in regional UK cities give national advertisers London-style impact outside the capital. Sellers can pitch them as anchors for multi-city launches.

pitch.line: Ocean Outdoor's new Lancaster Circus screen in Birmingham covers 500 sq m (invidis).

brief: Trust is the theme of the sales season: BCG finds only 54% of shoppers believe Black Friday discounts, and Visa's tests show AI shopping agents fail 43% of tasks, often buying anyway.
From France to India, consumers are using AI more but trusting it unevenly, while Brazilians and Italians are shopping earlier and more sceptically.
For OOH, an IPA analysis of 569 campaigns links OOH, audio and print to 33% stronger brand effects; German advertisers say DOOH is gaining; Outfront's transit revenue rose 20%.
Diary: Fraport Bulgaria's lounge EOI closes on 15 November, oOh!media's takeover goes to court on 18 November, and Schiphol's €426m advertising tender closes on 20 November.
editions.take: The week's research is a study in misplaced confidence. Retailers are betting on AI agents and endless promotions, while shoppers doubt both and fall back on reputation, guarantees and brands they already know. That favours the media that builds familiarity in public, and the IPA's numbers suggest OOH does exactly that.

numberOfDay.line: Only 54% of shoppers in ten countries believe Black Friday prices are genuinely lower than usual (BCG).

steal.title: Measure the signage
steal.text: Dentsu matched viewers of Japanese baseball broadcasts at ID level and found that stadium signage plus a TV spot lifted brand awareness by 12.5%. The idea worth stealing: sell venue and roadside signage with a brand-lift study attached, and show the extra effect of buying it alongside TV.

items.headline: Black Friday's credibility problem: only half of shoppers believe the discounts
items.dek: BCG's sixth annual study of year-end sales finds promotion fatigue setting in across ten countries. Social media is losing its grip on inspiration as AI assistants take its place.
items.source: Boston Consulting Group, via PR Newswire

figures.label: Trust that Black Friday prices are lower
Social as a source of inspiration
Plan to use AI for sales shopping

keyPoints: Only 54% of shoppers in ten countries believe Black Friday prices are genuinely lower than usual, and one in five actively distrusts them.
22% plan to spend less or skip year-end sales because they think discounts are always available.
The discount that counts as a good deal has slipped to about 30%, from 32% in 2025.
Social media's role as a source of inspiration fell nine points to 46%, declining in every market, while AI rose in all ten.
Retailer reputation and money-back guarantees build trust; influencer endorsements and AI review summaries barely move it.
body: Year-end sales events are suffering from their own ubiquity. BCG's survey of 10,220 consumers, covering Singles' Day, Black Friday and Cyber Monday, finds that barely half believe the headline discounts, and more than a fifth intend to cut back because they assume a deal will always be available somewhere.

The routes to purchase are shifting too. Social media's role as a source of ideas has fallen sharply, while 56% of shoppers plan to use AI tools this season, up eight points; of those who already do, about 86% find them helpful and 78% say they make a purchase more likely. Comparing prices across retailers (39%) and product features (37%) are the tasks people trust AI with most.

The most telling finding is what builds trust. Retailer reputation and money-back guarantees score a net 65%, verified reviews 59%, while scarcity countdowns, AI-generated review summaries and influencer recommendations score in single digits.
items.relevance: Trust, not urgency, is the currency of this year's sales season. Retailers and brands can use broadcast-scale, visible media such as OOH to carry reputation and guarantee messages, rather than relying on countdown tactics and influencer pushes that shoppers now discount.

pitch.line: Only 54% of shoppers believe Black Friday prices are genuinely lower than usual, and one in five distrusts them (BCG, 10,220 consumers in 10 countries, November 2026).

items.headline: AI shopping agents fail four tests in ten, and still go ahead and buy
items.dek: Visa tested 22 AI models on 15 shopping challenges. More than half of the failed runs ended in a purchase anyway, a warning for brands planning for agentic commerce.
items.source: Visa, via Business Wire
keyPoints: AI shopping agents failed 42.8% of Visa's test runs, and 54% of those failures still ended in a purchase.
The best model passed 82.2% of challenges; the worst managed only 28.9%.
Only 34.2% of scenarios were passed consistently on all three attempts.
The five most expensive models passed 67.1% of runs, against 50.2% for the five cheapest.
body: Visa's Agentic Commerce Benchmark set 22 models from 12 AI labs loose on 15 shopping challenges, three attempts each. The overall pass rate was 57.2%, and the spread between models was wide, from 82.2% for the strongest to 28.9% for the weakest.

The more troubling result is behavioural: when agents got it wrong, they mostly did not stop. More than half of failed runs still completed a purchase. Models that were better at uncovering hidden buying factors, such as a shopper's unstated constraints, passed 70.2% of runs, against 44.4% for the bottom five.
Visa's separate US Trust Index for September found that 72% of consumers have used an AI assistant, but only 23% trust one to make payments for them.
items.relevance: Agentic shopping is arriving faster than it is maturing. Brands should keep investing in direct, memorable consumer awareness, the kind OOH builds, so that people still name the brand they want rather than leaving the choice to an unreliable agent.

pitch.line: AI shopping agents failed 42.8% of test runs, and 54% of failures still ended in a purchase (Visa Agentic Commerce Benchmark, 22 models, November 2026).
