items.pdfNote: AdImpact publishes its detailed figures to clients; no public PDF of the final tally was found.

items.headline: Sponsored creator posts reach seven times more people than gifted ones
items.dek: Digiday's 2026 Creator Marketing Index finds 96% of brands and agencies now use creators. Paid posts average 334,000 views, against 48,000 for gifted product.
items.source: Digiday+ Research, Creator Marketing Index 2026
keyPoints: 96% of surveyed US brands and agencies use creator partnerships for social content.
Instagram is used by 90%, Facebook by 80%, YouTube by 72% and TikTok by 63%.
Sponsored posts averaged 334,055 views; gifted posts averaged 48,008.
Reels achieved an 11% engagement rate on Instagram, against 7% for stills and 5% for carousels.
The analysis covered 1,755 posts from 20 branded campaigns, mostly in beauty.
body: Creator marketing is now near-universal among US marketers, Digiday's research suggests, but reach depends on paying for it. Across 20 campaigns analysed with Dash Social, sponsored posts delivered roughly seven times the average views of gifted product.
Style shots and product demonstrations were the strongest sponsored formats. Video continues to outperform still images on engagement, with Reels well ahead of carousels.
Read alongside Kantar's warning that very little creator content builds the brand itself, the findings suggest creator budgets are rising faster than evidence of their long-term effect.
items.relevance: Creators are absorbing beauty and fashion budgets, both core airport categories. Propose 'creator to street' plans that amplify a creator campaign on DOOH, giving paid reach the scale and fame social alone cannot.

pitch.line: Sponsored creator posts average about seven times the views of gifted posts, according to Digiday's 2026 Creator Marketing Index.

items.pdfNote: The full index is available to Digiday+ subscribers.

items.headline: Australia: word of mouth drives six times more product trial than paid advertising
items.dek: Social Soup's survey of 850 Australians finds personal recommendations dwarf all paid media combined in prompting grocery shoppers to try something new. Younger shoppers lean heavily on creators.
items.source: Social Soup, via Mediaweek

figures.label: Named a person as main influence
Bought within a week of first sighting

keyPoints: Recommendations drive more than six times as many new product trials as all paid advertising combined.
27% of main grocery buyers named another person as their biggest influence; only 4% named paid advertising.
79% tried a new food, drink or household product in the past three months, and 83% bought within a week of first seeing it.
18–34s are almost four times as likely as over-55s to name a creator as their main influence.
One in 30 shoppers used an AI tool to decide, rising to one in eight in household, personal care and health.
body: Social Soup, an influence agency, surveyed a nationally representative sample of Australians on how they come to try new FMCG products. The answer is overwhelmingly other people: friends, family and creators, most often in face-to-face conversation rather than on social media.
Decisions are fast. Half of shoppers bought on the spot and the vast majority within a week, and most triers then told others, reaching around 15 people each.

The agency naturally has an interest in the finding, and the 4% figure reflects what shoppers say rather than measured effects. But the speed of conversion points to the value of reaching people near the shelf.
items.relevance: Treat the 'paid ads barely register' claim with care, since stated influence understates advertising's role. The stronger point for APAC colleagues is speed: 83% buy within a week, which supports near-store and retail DOOH.

pitch.line: 83% of Australian shoppers who try a new grocery product buy it within a week of first seeing it (Social Soup, November 2026).

items.pdfNote: Social Soup presented the findings at a briefing; no public report PDF was found.

items.headline: India's marketers lead the world on events and creators, but lag on measurement
items.dek: Nielsen's India cut of its annual marketing report finds 94% of marketers plan to raise sponsorship and event spending. Only 42% measure ROI across traditional and digital media.
items.source: Nielsen, 2026 Annual Marketing Report, via MediaNews4U
keyPoints: 94% of Indian marketers expect to increase sponsorship and event spending over the next 12–24 months, against 75% in the US and 67% in Italy.
61% see sports sponsorship as a route to new audiences, compared with 54% in the US and 32% in Germany.
81% rate influencer and creator content as very or extremely effective, 27 points above the US.
Only 42% measure ROI holistically across traditional and digital media, the lowest of the markets discussed.
body: Nielsen's global survey of 1,200 marketers was released last month; this new market breakdown highlights India as the most bullish country on experiential and creator-led marketing.

Indian marketers are markedly more enthusiastic than their US and European peers about live events, sport and creators. Their measurement, however, has not kept pace, with fewer than half able to compare returns across all media.
That combination of rising spend and weak measurement is a familiar pattern in fast-growing markets, and one that tends to reward media owners who can supply audience data.
items.relevance: India's appetite for live events and sport suits event-led OOH packages around stadiums, airports and city centres. Lead with measurement: the 42% gap is an opening for audience-verified DOOH.

pitch.line: 94% of Indian marketers plan to increase sponsorship and event spending, the highest of six markets in Nielsen's 2026 survey.

chart.title: Marketers planning more sponsorship and event spend

items.pdfNote: Nielsen's report is available via a registration form on its website.

items.headline: John Lewis rediscovers its Christmas magic, by System1's reckoning
items.dek: 'Gloria and Pickles' scores 5.6 stars, the retailer's best since 'Excitable Edgar' in 2019. Kantar is cooler, finding the ad short on emotional punch.
items.source: System1, via Campaign Brief
keyPoints: John Lewis's 2026 ad, by Saatchi & Saatchi, scores 5.6 stars on System1's Test Your Ad, its highest since 2019.
61% of viewers felt happy, almost twice the UK TV average.
Ratings have climbed steadily from 3.1 stars in 2021 to 5.1 in 2025 and 5.6 this year.
Only 15% recalled the children as rude, despite online criticism of the storyline.
Kantar praised the humour and soundtrack but said the branding could be stronger.
body: The UK's Christmas advertising season has its first verdict. System1, whose star ratings predict long-term brand growth, judged John Lewis's latest campaign a clear return to form after several years of middling scores.

The ad provoked some social media backlash over its portrayal of children, but System1's panel largely did not share it. Kantar was more measured, noting the work lacked the emotional force of earlier classics.
The two readings underline a recurring point: emotional response and strong branding do not always arrive together.
items.relevance: Christmas is peak season for UK retail on OOH. Use System1's emphasis on happiness and Kantar's branding caveat to argue that OOH extensions, with bold brand cues, help an emotional TV ad land.

pitch.line: 61% of viewers felt happy watching John Lewis's 2026 Christmas ad, almost twice the UK TV average (System1).

chart.title: John Lewis Christmas ads, System1 stars

items.headline: France warms to retail media, but shoppers still want ads to earn their place
items.dek: iligo's fourth retail media barometer finds French shoppers seeing more in-store and shop-window screens, and more persuaded by them, as long as the message is useful.
items.source: iligo, Baromètre Retail Media 2026
keyPoints: 34% of French adults pass shop-window ad screens at least weekly, up from 30%, and 32% see in-store screens weekly.
55% say online retail media ads can make them want to buy, up four points in a year.
Attention remains the weak spot: only 15% say they watch in-store screen ads attentively.
A third (33%) would welcome more retail media online and 32% more in-store screen ads, but interest in new-product messages on window screens fell from 44% to 39%.
body: The survey of 2,011 adults aged 18 to 69 was carried out between 29 September and 7 October 2026. iligo defines retail media broadly: screens and posters in stores and shop windows, e-commerce sites and apps, and grocery retailers' own platforms.
Its conclusion is that retail media is shifting from multiplying touchpoints to proving relevance. Acceptance rises when ads carry practical value, such as promotions and useful information.
items.relevance: Proof that near-store and in-store screens are growing in reach and persuasion, but that creative must be useful to win attention. A good argument for dynamic, data-led DOOH copy close to the point of sale.

pitch.line: 55% of French shoppers say retail media ads can make them want to buy, up four points in a year (iligo, 2026).

items.headline: Kenya is the world's fastest-growing internet ad market, says PwC
items.dek: PwC's Africa Entertainment & Media Outlook finds South Africa, Kenya and Nigeria entering a new digital phase from very different starting points.
items.source: PwC, Africa Entertainment & Media Outlook 2026–2030
keyPoints: Kenya's internet advertising is forecast to almost double from $313m in 2025 to $603m in 2030: a 14.0% CAGR, nearly twice the 7.2% global rate.
Video internet advertising in Kenya grows 18.2% a year, driven by social platforms and connected TV.
Nigeria's internet advertising rises from $279m to $439m; retail paid search grows 17.2% a year and overtakes traditional paid search by 2028.
South Africa remains the largest market, with internet advertising reaching $3.1bn (R55.7bn) in 2030.
body: PwC describes three markets at different stages: South Africa with scale and sophisticated advertising infrastructure, Kenya with connectivity and digital payments, and Nigeria combining a large population with fast-growing digital audiences.
Connectivity will account for most entertainment and media revenue by 2030: about 60% in South Africa, 75% in Kenya and 66% in Nigeria.
items.relevance: Useful context for global clients asking where the next growth markets are. Africa's digital shift is rapid but uneven, so plans need to be market by market rather than continent-wide.

pitch.line: Kenya's internet advertising is forecast to grow 14% a year to 2030, nearly twice the global rate (PwC Africa E&M Outlook).

chart.title: Internet advertising revenue, 2030 (US$m)

items.headline: Frankfurt's new Terminal 3 lifts retail spend per passenger by 30%
items.dek: Fraport's nine-month results show Terminal 3 outperforming Terminal 2 on retail income per passenger, even as Middle East traffic fell. Frankfurt volumes were flat at 47.5 million.
items.source: The Moodie Davitt Report

figures.label: T3 retail income per pax vs T2 (Q3)

keyPoints: Retail income per passenger at Terminal 3 was 30% higher than at Terminal 2 in Q3, and 40% higher in September.
This came despite a 21% fall in Middle East traffic.
Retail & Real Estate revenue rose 3% to €419m over nine months; retail revenue per passenger was €3.24.
Frankfurt passengers were flat at 47.5m; the group handled about 146m, up 1.7%.
Fraport keeps its full-year outlook but blames high regulatory costs for restraining Frankfurt growth.
body: Frankfurt's Terminal 3 is proving its commercial worth. Fraport's results show passengers in the new building spending markedly more per head than those in Terminal 2, a gap that widened in September.

The wider picture is subdued. Frankfurt's traffic is flat, high-value customers were fewer and group net profit fell by almost 29%. Chief executive Stefan Schulte described a solid result in a difficult market.
The T3 premium suggests that modern terminal design, with better dwell areas and sightlines, raises commercial yields across the board.
items.relevance: Evidence that new terminals lift commercial yield is useful in any airport pitch. Cite the T3 premium when arguing for premium digital formats in new or refurbished terminals.

pitch.line: Retail income per passenger at Frankfurt's new Terminal 3 ran 30% above Terminal 2 in Q3 2026 (Fraport).

items.headline: Amman's Queen Alia airport puts its commercial concessions out to tender to 2039
items.dek: Airport International Group has launched an RFQ for master duty free, food and beverage and convenience concessions. Qualifications are due on 1 December.
items.source: The Moodie Davitt Report
keyPoints: The RFQ covers duty free, food and beverage and convenience retail, either separately or as a single master concession.
Concessions run until 2039, alongside an enhancement plan to raise passenger capacity by half.
Avolta, trading as Amman Duty Free, is the incumbent.
The RFQ follows an expressions-of-interest call in September; advertising is not included.
body: Jordan's main gateway is reshaping its commercial programme for the long term. Airport International Group is offering operators the option of a single integrated master concession, a model that is gaining ground as airports seek simpler, larger partnerships.

The tender is tied to a plan to expand capacity by 50%, with commercial areas growing in step. Advertising is not part of this RFQ, but a terminal expansion of that scale usually brings a new media programme in its wake.
items.relevance: Flag Queen Alia for the Middle East pipeline: a 50% capacity expansion and new retail layout will create new media sites. Worth an early conversation with AIG's commercial team.

pitch.line: Amman's Queen Alia International Airport plans a 50% increase in passenger capacity, with new commercial concessions running to 2039.

items.headline: Lamar's airport revenue grows 14% as programmatic surges 42%
items.dek: America's largest billboard owner had its best month ever in October and raised guidance. Outfront also grew revenue 9.3%, with transit up a fifth.
items.source: Lamar Advertising, via StockTitan and The Motley Fool
keyPoints: Q3 net revenue rose 6.6% to $624.5m, or 6.2% on an acquisition-adjusted basis.
Programmatic grew 42.4% in Q3; national and programmatic made up 24.6% of the book.
Airports were the fastest-growing sub-segment at 14.4%; transit grew 8.1%.
October revenue rose 14.1%, the best month in Lamar's history, helped by political spend of more than $40m this year.
Outfront's Q3 revenue rose 9.3% to $511.1m, with transit up 20.4% on World Cup demand.
body: Both listed US outdoor groups reported strong third quarters on 5 November. Lamar raised its full-year AFFO guidance and said renewals heading into 2027 look healthy. Its programmatic growth is among the fastest in the sector, although from a smaller base.

Outfront benefited from the FIFA World Cup in its transit business, where profit almost doubled. It expects 2026 to be a double-digit growth year, while it writes off further costs of New York's MTA screen roll-out.
Clear Channel Outdoor, now owned by Mubadala Capital, no longer reports publicly.
items.relevance: US OOH owners are growing programmatic fast, and airports lead Lamar's growth. Expect US clients to use these numbers as the benchmark for airport and programmatic OOH proposals.

pitch.line: Airport advertising was the fastest-growing OOH segment at Lamar in Q3 2026, up 14.4% on an acquisition-adjusted basis.

chart.title: US OOH Q3 2026 growth by segment

editions.take: AI is everyone's new gatekeeper and nobody's trusted adviser. Today's studies agree that people use it constantly, believe it rarely, and still trust what they can see for themselves, from a friend's tip to a poster in the street. That is the opening for real-world media.

numberOfDay.line: of consumers see AI as a highly trustworthy source of shopping advice, even though 81% use it every day.

steal.title: Joy beats tears
steal.text: John Lewis's return to form rests on happiness, not heartbreak: 61% of viewers felt happy. Kantar's caveat is weak branding. The idea worth stealing: pair the feel-good film with bold, brand-led OOH that does the remembering for it.

items.headline: JCDecaux breaks €1bn in Q3 as programmatic grows 37.5%
items.dek: Organic growth of 6.6% beat both the group's own guidance and the analysts' consensus. Digital now accounts for almost half of revenue, and the Q4 outlook has been raised to around 6%.
items.source: JCDecaux SE, via MarketScreener and GlobeNewswire
keyPoints: Revenue rose 9.1% on a reported basis and 6.6% organically to €1,010.5m, up from €926.1m a year earlier.
Digital revenue grew 15.3% organically and now accounts for 45.4% of the total.
Programmatic sales rose 37.5% and are now 13.3% of digital revenue.
Street Furniture grew 7.3% to €492.9m, Transport 7.7% to €387.3m and Billboard 1.4% to €130.3m.
Nine-month revenue reached €2,964.5m, up 6.0% organically. Q4 guidance is around 6%.
body: The world's largest outdoor advertising company comfortably beat its own forecast of around 5%. It also edged past the City, where Berenberg had pencilled in 6.5% and consensus stood at roughly 6.1%. Management credited double-digit digital growth and a final lift from the FIFA World Cup.

Transport was the standout, with double-digit gains in the UK and North America. Rest of the World fell by a high single-digit figure as the Middle East conflict continued to weigh. In France, a deliberate pruning of billboard inventory held that segment back.
On an IFRS basis, revenue was €935.9m. Full-year results are due on 11 March 2027.
items.relevance: The clearest read yet on OOH's digital shift: the sector's largest owner now earns almost half its revenue from screens, and programmatic is compounding fast. A useful benchmark for any OOH proposal, with one caveat to prepare for: the Middle East drag.

links.label: Analysis: digital drove ~96% of growth (PPC Land)

items.pdfNote: The Q3 2026 PDF is attached to the official release but hasn't yet appeared at a public direct link.

pitch.line: JCDecaux's programmatic revenue grew 37.5% organically in Q3 2026; digital is now 45.4% of group revenue.

chart.title: Q3 2026 organic growth by activity

items.headline: WARC: global adspend heads for $1.34trn, and outdoor is outgrowing TV
items.dek: WARC's autumn forecast has sharply upgraded 2026. OOH grows 8.1% and its digital arm 13.7%, while the three biggest platforms tighten their grip.
items.source: WARC Media, Global Ad Spend Forecast Q3 2026
keyPoints: The global market grows 11.9% this year, then slows to 8.4% in 2027 ($1.46trn) and 7.9% in 2028.
OOH is forecast at $63.3bn, and it grows a further 6.3% in 2027.
Social (+21.3% to $394.6bn), search and retail media together account for two-thirds of all spend.
Alphabet, Amazon and Meta take 59.7% of spend outside China, rising to 61.5% by 2028.
Travel and transport advertising rises 19.3% and automotive 17.8%.
body: This is a marked upgrade on June, when WARC had pencilled in 8.9% growth for 2026. WARC credits heavy corporate spending on AI and a crowded calendar of global events: the Winter Olympics, the World Cup and the US mid-terms.
The hangover arrives in 2027. Television, which manages just 1.2% growth this year, is forecast to shrink once those events have passed. Outdoor's growth slows but continues.
The full report is for subscribers only. The public release carries the headline channel table.
items.relevance: Outdoor growing nearly seven times faster than TV this year is a ready-made line for any global pitch. The strong travel forecast also supports the airport portfolio.
items.pdfNote: The full report is for WARC subscribers only. There's no public PDF.

pitch.line: Global OOH grows 8.1% in 2026 against just 1.2% for TV, says WARC.

chart.title: Forecast growth in 2026 by channel

items.headline: Nielsen: marketers have embraced AI but don't yet trust it
items.dek: Nielsen's annual survey of marketers finds AI use is now close to universal, but most still insist on a human check, and accuracy has become the watchword.
items.source: Nielsen, 2026 Annual Marketing Report
keyPoints: Nielsen variously puts AI use among marketers at 'nearly 90%' and 98%. On any reading it is now standard practice.
55% trust AI recommendations but require human review. Only about a third trust them outright.
The share of marketers who put measurement accuracy first has doubled in a year. Complaints about mismatched datasets are up 10 points.
49% use hybrid or full-funnel metrics, and 29% will prioritise brand-lift measurement over the next year.
58% have dedicated and growing budgets for creators. 43% see sport as a testing ground for new audiences.
body: The report's three chapters cover accuracy, proving outcomes and where everyday attention is going. Its central message is that more data has not meant more confidence: marketers are drowning in signals that don't agree.
Nielsen also finds 41% of US consumers count any video as 'TV', whatever the screen, which blurs the old channel lines. Sport remains a magnet for budgets.
items.relevance: Accuracy and proof of outcomes are exactly where OOH audience measurement and brand-lift studies can win the argument. Pitch outdoor as the verifiable, brand-safe reach layer in plans built on AI-driven buying.
items.pdfNote: The report and its chapters can be downloaded from nielsen.com via a registration form.

pitch.line: 55% of marketers trust AI recommendations only with human review: accuracy is the new priority.

items.headline: DoubleVerify: nearly all marketers plan to use AI, but few have built it into their work
items.dek: A global survey of more than 2,000 marketers finds plans to use AI are nearly unanimous, yet adoption across individual buying and planning tasks is patchy.
items.source: DoubleVerify, 2026 Global Insights Report: Beyond the Hype
keyPoints: 97% of marketers plan to use AI somewhere in media planning, buying or optimisation this year.
Using AI to summarise media briefs has risen from 28% in 2024 to 37% in 2025, and is expected to reach 40% in 2026.
When choosing AI tools, accuracy and effectiveness of recommendations is the most-cited consideration (35%).
The gap between intention and day-to-day use remains wide across most workflows.
body: DoubleVerify's report is the second in a fortnight to find enthusiasm for AI outrunning real-world use. Marketers are keen on automation in principle but wary of handing over the keys without proof that it works.
Taken with Nielsen's findings, the message is consistent: the next phase of AI in advertising will be won on verification and outcomes, not novelty.
items.relevance: As AI systems take over more media briefs and buying, outdoor inventory has to be machine-readable, programmatically accessible and backed by trusted data. That is a strong argument for investing in programmatic OOH and data.
items.pdfNote: The report is free to download from DoubleVerify's site, but behind a form.

pitch.line: 97% of marketers plan to use AI in media planning and buying in 2026, but adoption across workflows is uneven.

items.headline: Kantar: consumers are warming to ads while marketers lose their nerve
items.dek: Kantar's annual Media Reactions study, covering 23,000 consumers in 33 markets, finds hostility to advertising falling and impact increasingly coming from channels used together.
items.source: Kantar, Media Reactions 2026
keyPoints: Negative sentiment towards advertising fell from 20% to 17% in a year, with fewer complaints about repetition and overload.
Campaigns land about seven times harder with receptive audiences.
43% of campaign impact now comes from channels working together, up from 18% before 2014.
Four in ten marketers doubt they're getting the basics right, such as integrating channels and tailoring creative.
body: Kantar's annual ad-equity study is meant to inform 2027 planning. This year's edition looks at how AI assistants and creators are changing the way people discover brands.
In last year's edition, OOH ranked second and digital OOH third for consumer receptivity. Classic posters led among women and Gen Z, and digital screens among Gen X and boomers.
items.relevance: The '7× impact' and '43% from combinations' figures are made for positioning OOH as the amplifier in integrated, multi-market plans, especially with clients who are unsure about their media mix.
items.pdfNote: The 2026 report is gated on kantar.com. The PDF here is the free 2025 guide.

pitch.line: Campaigns land about seven times harder with receptive audiences, and 43% of impact comes from channels working together.

items.headline: Social is becoming the shop window, but AI influencers leave shoppers cold
items.dek: DoubleVerify's global study of 22,000 consumers finds short-form video drives purchases. Brands using AI-generated influencers face a backlash, and in Asia-Pacific brand safety is a growing worry.
items.source: DoubleVerify, Scroll, Stop and Shop: Walled Garden Trends

figures.label: APAC: brand suitability a major challenge

keyPoints: 38% of consumers say a social media ad can encourage them to buy, with short-form video drawing the strongest response.
37% react negatively to brands using AI-generated influencers. Fewer than three in ten react positively.
In Asia-Pacific, 35% of marketers rank brand suitability as a major challenge on social, second only to reaching the right audience.
Citing eMarketer, the report puts global social adspend at $408bn this year, growing twice as fast as other digital channels.
body: Social platforms are fast becoming full-funnel storefronts, from discovery through to checkout. Yet the more money pours in, the more nervous brands become about the content their ads appear next to. The concern is sharpest in APAC.
Human creators who use AI tools are received far better than synthetic influencers, another sign that authenticity carries a premium.
items.relevance: Brand safety and authenticity are two of outdoor's oldest strengths. Present OOH as the safe, real-world counterweight to social budgets, particularly with APAC and luxury clients.

pitch.line: 37% of consumers react negatively to AI-generated influencers; authenticity carries a premium.

items.headline: Mood over tracking: marketers bet on context, not cookies
items.dek: GumGum's global survey of more than 2,000 marketers finds behavioural data is losing ground to context and mindset. In the UK, just 4% now rank it first for effectiveness.
items.source: GumGum, The Marketers' Take on Mindset: 2026 Global Report
keyPoints: More than three-quarters of UK marketers say context (48%) or mood (28%) has the greatest impact on ad effectiveness.
Only 4% of UK respondents say behavioural data is the key lever.
Support for mindset-led targeting is growing globally, but many marketers admit they aren't yet acting on it.
body: The findings mark a quiet retreat from the surveillance-style targeting that dominated the past decade. Privacy rules and signal loss have played their part, but so has growing evidence that the moment matters as much as the person.
Of the 2,000-plus respondents, more than 500 were UK marketing professionals.
items.relevance: Context and mood are where outdoor is strongest: the commute, the airport, the shopping trip. Use this to pitch OOH on contextual relevance and moments, especially with dynamic and programmatic creative.

pitch.line: Only 4% of UK marketers rank behavioural data as the key to ad effectiveness; 76% say context or mood.

items.headline: Asia-Pacific: outdoor is the only traditional medium still growing
items.dek: Media Partners Asia sizes the region's adspend at $276bn this year. Retail media is now twice the size of linear TV, and OOH is the one traditional channel growing across the region.
items.source: Media Partners Asia, Asia Pacific Advertising Trends 2026
keyPoints: Across 14 markets, spend grows 5.3% to $276.1bn this year and reaches $335.5bn by 2031. Digital is 75% of the total.
OOH grows from $20.0bn to $25.3bn over the forecast period, expanding in 11 of the 14 markets.
Retail media reaches $75.5bn, twice the size of linear TV, and is forecast to hit $110bn by 2031.
Meta (15.9%), ByteDance (14.8%) and Google (13.0%) take 44% of regional spend between them.
India is the fastest-growing major market (+9.3% to $17.5bn). Japan grows 5.1% to $54.1bn, and China 5.3% to $152.6bn.
body: MPA's bottom-up study covers Australia, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. Its headline is less about the size of the market than about where the money is going: retail media and online video.
Australia is the region's most advanced connected TV market. Regional CTV spend is forecast to almost double to $20.6bn by 2031.
items.relevance: 'The only traditional medium growing across the region' is a powerful line for APAC conversations. Pair it with India's growth and Japan's record market when discussing regional plans with global clients.
items.pdfNote: The PDF and Excel database are available to MPA clients only.

pitch.line: OOH is the only traditional medium growing across Asia-Pacific, expanding in 11 of 14 markets.

chart.title: APAC OOH spend (US$bn)

items.headline: US television faces a record 15% collapse in ad revenue next year
items.dek: eMarketer forecasts that traditional TV ad spend will fall far faster than its audience in 2027, once the World Cup and the mid-terms have passed.
items.source: eMarketer, US TV Ad Spending 2027
keyPoints: Traditional TV ad spend is forecast to fall 15.0% in 2027, the steepest drop on record, while viewership slips only 3.4%.
Sport and political advertising increasingly decide the medium's fortunes.
eMarketer expects total US media adspend to grow 15.6% this year, then slow to 9.4% in 2027.
The IAB has also raised its 2026 US forecast, to 12.3% growth.
body: 2026 has been an unusually good year for American advertising, inflated by a home World Cup and the costliest mid-term cycle in US history. eMarketer warns that buyers who built budgets around those events, particularly in connected TV, should plan for spending to normalise.
The gap between audience and revenue suggests advertisers are leaving linear TV faster than viewers are.
items.relevance: This is a clear opening for US brand budgets coming out of linear TV in 2027. Position outdoor as the mass-reach replacement, alongside CTV, in conversations with US multinationals.
items.pdfNote: The full eMarketer report is for subscribers only.

pitch.line: US traditional TV ad spend is forecast to fall 15% in 2027, while viewership falls only 3.4%.

items.headline: Attention pays, but setting hard thresholds wastes the budget
items.dek: Integral Ad Science finds higher attention scores bring markedly better results, but rigid attention minimums wipe out inventory and drive up prices.
items.source: Integral Ad Science, via MediaPost
keyPoints: An IAS and YouGov survey finds 88% of US digital media professionals already measure attention, and 83% say a strategy for it is important.
In IAS's modelling, CPMs rise an estimated 29.4% for every 10-point gain in attention score.
The performance gains still outweighed the extra cost, as long as advertisers raised average attention gradually.
Strict minimum-attention rules eliminated most available inventory and inflated prices for what remained.
body: Attention has become the industry's metric of choice, but IAS warns against treating it as a pass-or-fail filter. Raising campaign averages works better than imposing hard minimums.
The analysis draws on a July 2026 dataset of campaign spend.
items.relevance: Attention is now part of the media-trading conversation in the US. Have OOH attention and dwell-time evidence ready, especially for airports and large-format sites, and present it as quality without prohibitive cost.

pitch.line: 88% of US digital media professionals already measure attention.

items.headline: UK marketing budgets rise at their fastest rate in more than two years
items.dek: The IPA Bellwether finds every category of marketing budget revised up in the third quarter, with main media at a nine-quarter high.
items.source: IPA / S&P Global, Q3 2026 Bellwether Report
keyPoints: A net 14.3% of companies raised their marketing budgets, up from 6.9% in Q2 and the highest reading since Q2 2024.
All seven categories grew, led by PR and events. Main media saw its strongest upward revision in nine quarters, with video at a two-year high.
Market research grew for the first time in seven quarters.
S&P Global raised its 2026 UK adspend forecast from 2.1% to 2.8%. Company and industry confidence remain cautious, though less negative.
body: The UK economy has beaten expectations this year, and boardrooms are responding by spending, despite fragile confidence ahead of the autumn Budget. Industry figures called it the most optimistic Bellwether in years.
The IPA's director general, Paul Bainsfair, welcomed the figures but warned brands against leaning too heavily on short-term promotions.
items.relevance: UK clients are spending again, and events and experiential are hot. That plays well for large-format and experiential OOH. Use it as proof the UK is a market to invest in now.
items.pdfNote: The full report is free to IPA members and paid for others.

items.headline: UK adspend jumps 11% to £12.3bn as AI money pours in
items.dek: The AA/WARC Expenditure Report shows the UK market comfortably ahead of forecast in the second quarter, with a record Christmas expected.
items.source: Advertising Association / WARC Expenditure Report
keyPoints: UK advertising investment rose 11.0% in Q2 to £12.3bn, 2.1 points ahead of the July forecast.
Search takes 36.9% (£4.5bn), social 28.3% (£3.5bn) and TV 10.3% (£1.3bn).
The World Cup helped, but WARC attributes the underlying growth to AI-related spending.
Trade press reports a record £14bn forecast for the festive quarter.
body: Separately, Outsmart's figures put UK OOH up 12.7% to a record £402.6m in Q2. Digital accounted for 68% of the total and grew faster than classic formats.
The AA/WARC full-year forecast, last published in July, is for 8.2% growth to £50.5bn, the first time UK adspend has topped £50bn.
items.relevance: Together with the Bellwether, this gives you two independent, credible sources showing UK momentum for client presentations.
items.pdfNote: The full AA/WARC report is for subscribers only. This PDF is the UK OOH figures for the same quarter.

pitch.line: UK ad spend rose 11% to £12.3bn in Q2 2026.

items.headline: JCDecaux will dress the Centre Pompidou until 2030
items.dek: JCDecaux Artvertising has won the right to run advertising on the façade of the Paris landmark throughout its renovation, helping to pay for the restoration.
items.source: Zonebourse / MarketScreener, ABC Bourse
keyPoints: Centre Pompidou chose JCDecaux Artvertising for advertising and decorative displays across its façade for the duration of the works.
The revenue helps fund the restoration, which follows the building's listing as a historic monument.
Immersive events and activations on Place Stravinsky may accompany the installations.
body: The Pompidou closed for renovation in autumn 2025 and is due to reopen in 2030. JCDecaux plans to use the façade as an artistic and advertising showcase for audiences around the Marais and Les Halles. The Centre's president, Laurent Le Bon, described the works as a creative moment of transformation.
The façade has form: Nike took it over during the Paris 2024 Olympics.
items.relevance: A rare multi-year Paris showpiece for luxury, fashion and entertainment brands, and a model for funding heritage restoration through advertising that could travel to landmarks in other cities.

pitch.line: JCDecaux Artvertising will run the Centre Pompidou façade until the building reopens in 2030.

items.headline: Schiphol's €426m advertising tender closes in a fortnight
items.dek: Royal Schiphol Group is handing its estate of more than 1,000 media assets to specialist concessionaires. Final bids are due on 20 November.
items.source: Moodie Davitt Report
keyPoints: Three lots: Amsterdam Schiphol (€364m); Eindhoven, Rotterdam The Hague and Lelystad (€32m); and 11 monopole billboards around Schiphol, including on the A4 (€30m).
Scoring is 50% price (a minimum annual guarantee plus a variable fee), 37.5% business plan and 12.5% implementation plan.
The second information memorandum is due on 9 November. The intended award is on 6 January 2027, with the final decision on 27 January.
Schiphol wants fewer but more impactful digital assets, more programmatic and better data, and aims to at least double its advertising revenue.
body: This is one of the largest airport media contracts to come up in Europe this year. It marks a shift from in-house sales to concession partnerships.
items.relevance: Watch the outcome closely: it sets a benchmark for airport media economics in Europe, and Gatwick is moving the opposite way.
items.pdfNote: The tender guide is on the Mercell platform, which requires registration.

pitch.line: Schiphol's €426m advertising tender closes on 20 November 2026.

items.headline: Gatwick goes it alone and takes its advertising in-house
items.dek: From April 2027 the UK's second-busiest airport will sell its own media, ending Global's concession.
items.source: Moodie Davitt Report
keyPoints: Gatwick is ending the five-year contract Global won in 2022 and will keep all advertising revenue itself.
The move follows government approval of the £2bn Northern Runway Programme, which could lift capacity to 80 million passengers a year.
Gatwick is controlled by VINCI Airports, so the rest of its network will be watching.
body: Industry observers quoted by the Moodie Davitt Report warn that execution is the real test. The in-house team will need to make buying easy for agencies of every size without Global's sales network and automated trading.
items.relevance: Airport landlords are weighing in-house sales against concessions. Have the counter-arguments ready: scale, global sales reach, programmatic and measurement.

pitch.line: Gatwick brings its advertising in-house from 1 April 2027.

items.headline: Clear Channel Outdoor reports today, with its takeover still pending
items.dek: Clear Channel Outdoor arrives at its results with momentum. Second-quarter revenue rose 8.7% and a $2.43-a-share take-private by a Mubadala-led consortium is pending.
items.source: Clear Channel Outdoor filings; Quartr, Yahoo Finance
keyPoints: Third-quarter results are scheduled for today, according to Quartr and Yahoo Finance.
In Q2, revenue grew 8.7% to $438.0m, airports grew 14%, and digital reached 44.6% of revenue, in line with the sector's leaders.
Stockholders approved the Mubadala Capital-led takeover in May, and CFIUS clearance has since been announced. CCO sold its Spanish business for $132.3m in August.
body: The deal was expected to close by the end of the third quarter, so check today's release to see whether it has completed. Heavy debt remains the constraint: cash interest was $205.8m in the first half alone.
items.relevance: A private, US-focused Clear Channel changes the competitive picture for US airport tenders and global client RFPs.

pitch.line: Clear Channel Outdoor's digital share reached 44.6% in Q2 2026.

brief: Advertising is booming globally ($1.34trn, +11.9%), and outdoor is growing several times faster than TV. WARC's forecast is the line to use this week.
AI is now standard practice for marketers but not yet trusted: Nielsen and DoubleVerify both find accuracy and verification are the new priorities.
JCDecaux beat expectations in Q3 (+6.6% organic, programmatic +37.5%). The US faces a 15% fall in TV ad spend in 2027, and outdoor is the only traditional medium growing across APAC.
Diary: Schiphol's €426m advertising tender closes on 20 November.
editions.take: Outdoor is the quiet winner of 2026: growing several times faster than TV worldwide, the only traditional medium still rising across Asia-Pacific, and the obvious home for brand money as US television braces for a 15% fall.

campaign.title: Liverpool FC says 'Nice One' to fans in 24 cities
campaign.where: 24 cities in 16 countries on five continents, around Official Liverpool Supporters Club locations (including Adelaide)
campaign.what: Liverpool FC's Christmas campaign, the biggest in the club's 134-year history, thanks supporters with a hero film in which Virgil van Dijk, Alisson Becker, Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz tell fans it is an honour to play for them. A global OOH campaign placed around supporters' club outposts carries the line 'to the world's greatest fans, nice one', backed by digital and social.
campaign.why: Instead of selling, the club uses OOH to thank fans where they actually gather, turning local posters into a shared global moment. Brands with dispersed communities can map OOH to their fans' meeting places rather than to generic reach.

campaignAlt.title: Celebrities urge parents to read aloud, in surgeries and stations
campaignAlt.where: Doctors' waiting rooms across Germany and Ströer digital screens in city centres and stations in seven large cities
campaignAlt.what: Peter Maffay, Judith Rakers and Bernhard Hoëcker appear in several languages asking 'Ich lese vor – du auch?', urging parents to read to their children ahead of Germany's Read-Aloud Day on 20 November. The spots run on waiting-room screens in medical practices after an earlier run on Ströer's station and city-centre screens.
campaignAlt.why: The reading foundation chose OOH precisely to reach people outside their online algorithms, and placed the message where parents wait with time to watch. Matching message to dwell-time context is a lesson any cause or brand can borrow.

campaignAlt.title: Holland & Barrett makes body parts speak
campaignAlt.what: Billboards for Holland & Barrett's 'Back Your Body' platform, shot by The Masons, use arranged human body parts to form both the imagery and the typography. The result gives the wellness retailer's message a literally human voice.
campaignAlt.why: Building the type out of the product's subject, the body, makes the brand idea legible in a glance, which is what roadside OOH needs. A reminder that a single, ownable visual device can carry a whole platform.

gallery.title: Wet Ones puts 'hand butts' on New York's streets
gallery.what: Extreme close-ups of fingers posed to look like bottoms ran across LinkNYC kiosks, bus shelters, newsstands, wild postings, bus wraps and a Times Square takeover, with interactive walls handing out wipes. When the MTA rejected the subway buy, the brand turned the refusal into a same-day Times Square response.
gallery.why: A cheeky visual gag that only works at scale in public spaces, and a rejection turned into earned media within hours: build the PR moment into the OOH plan.

gallery.title: Nintendo opens Birmingham's biggest OOH banner site
gallery.what: Nintendo is the launch advertiser on Ocean Outdoor's new Lancaster Circus site in Birmingham, a 500 sqm digital screen flanked by two 60 sqm portrait banners above one of the city's busiest junctions. The creative marks Nintendo's 40th anniversary and a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
gallery.why: Being first on a brand-new landmark site buys novelty and press coverage on top of the media itself. Anniversary and heritage stories suit a canvas big enough to feel like an event.

gallery.title: Tesco launches Christmas with a 72-metre DOOH domination
gallery.what: Tesco kicked off its festive season on Storm's Cromination, a 72-metre run of linked roadside screens bought as a full-hour domination. The food-led creative is dressed in bold Tesco red to signal that Christmas has arrived.
gallery.why: Owning every screen on a long roadside run turns a seasonal message into a moment drivers cannot miss. Simple food close-ups and one dominant brand colour read well at speed.

gallery.title: Petals turns parents' own words into OOH for Baby Loss Awareness Week
gallery.what: The baby-loss counselling charity Petals ran a two-week campaign on donated Ocean Outdoor screens in London, Birmingham and Manchester, built from real messages written by parents it has supported. Further contributions gathered through social and email are being fed into the artwork while the campaign runs.
gallery.why: Letting the audience write the copy gives a sensitive subject an authenticity no agency line could match. Building in live content updates keeps a short flight feeling fresh.

gallery.title: Balblair whisky takes over The Dome at Heathrow T3
gallery.what: International Beverage brought its Balblair single malt to Heathrow Terminal 3 with "Inner Still", a sensory space in The Dome where travellers smell four aroma cylinders before a guided tasting, plus a digital tasting unit at Gatwick North. A Manchester Terminal 2 leg is planned for the festive period from late November.
gallery.why: Airport dwell time lets a premium brand go beyond a poster and offer a full sensory trial right next to the till. Rolling the same concept across several hubs stretches one build into a season-long programme.

gallery.title: Garmin launches fēnix 9 with a climber abseiling from a motorway mast
gallery.what: To launch the fēnix 9 watch series in the Netherlands, a climber abseiled down an advertising mast beside the A12 near Utrecht. The stunt opened the Dutch version of Garmin's global Play Harder campaign, arguing that adventure can be found close to home.
gallery.why: Putting a real person on the structure turns a static roadside site into live theatre and gives social and PR a film to share. It localises a global platform with one bold, place-specific act.

gallery.title: Victoria's Secret teases its 2026 Fashion Show on One Times Square
gallery.what: Victoria's Secret used the digital billboard at One Times Square to tease its 2026 Fashion Show, putting the event's star line-up in front of tourists and fans. The placement was planned to ride the buzz ahead of the live broadcast.
gallery.why: An iconic site works as a trailer for a live event, and the photos people take become free social reach. Lead with the talent the audience already follows.

gallery.title: Clear Channel and Outfront unite for the Million Mammograms Challenge
gallery.what: Rival media owners Clear Channel Outdoor and Outfront ran thousands of digital billboards across the US during Breast Cancer Awareness Month to urge women to book screenings. The creative pairs the line "Cancer Isn't the Star of My Story" with a portrait of founder Mindie Kaplan taken six months after her double mastectomy.
gallery.why: A real face and a first-person line make a health message personal and lower the stigma around it. When competing owners pool inventory, a cause can achieve national scale quickly.

gallery.title: Amazon Now asks "Need it now?" across UAE roadside screens
gallery.owner: Phi Advertising / BackLite Media / Al Arabia OOH
gallery.what: Amazon promoted its fast grocery delivery service on digital roadside screens from three UAE media owners, with single everyday items such as onions, avocados and bananas against the line "Need it now?". Executions run in both Arabic and English.
gallery.why: One hero product plus a one-line question is perfect for screens seen at speed. Bilingual creative shows respect for the local audience while keeping the idea consistent.

gallery.title: Schweppes stacks a giant 3D can for Blueberry Mojito in Cairo
gallery.what: Coca-Cola Egypt launched Schweppes Blueberry Mojito on Cairo billboards featuring brand ambassadors Ahmed and Karim Fahmy, with a special build that stretches an outsized purple can across two stacked panels. Raised fruit and mint pieces sit beside the can to make the flavour tangible.
gallery.why: Breaking the frame with the pack itself makes a flavour launch impossible to miss. Repeating familiar ambassadors from an earlier campaign builds recognition from launch to launch.

gallery.title: Vitasoy runs a single Trans-Tasman OOH buy for "That's a Little Win"
gallery.what: Plant-milk brand Vitasoy ran bus and digital creative along key metropolitan corridors in both Australia and New Zealand, framing the daily commute as a chance for small wins. It is billed as the first fully integrated Trans-Tasman OOH campaign booked as one buy across QMS's network.
gallery.why: A single cross-border buy simplifies planning and keeps creative consistent for brands that treat two markets as one region. Tying the message to the commute makes the medium part of the idea.

gallery.title: Singapore's HPB opens a "Mouth Library" at HarbourFront MRT
gallery.what: For its "Less Salt Your Way" campaign, HPB built a Mouth Library of expressive mouths showing different ways to ask for less salt, sauce or gravy, with OOH and digital visuals turning plates and packs into speech bubbles. At HarbourFront MRT, commuters can scan a QR code to "try on" the mouths.
gallery.why: Giving people the exact words to use removes the awkwardness behind a behaviour change. A playful try-on mechanic in a busy station turns a health message into something people want to share.

gallery.title: Kaniva puts imperfect pets on Thai billboards
gallery.what: Pet food brand Kaniva launched "No Pet Beauty Standard" with billboards starring cross-eyed cats, kinked tails and mixed-breed dogs instead of show-ring animals. The same pets then appeared on the packaging, and owners across Thailand were invited to put their own pets forward.
gallery.why: Casting against category clichés makes a billboard instantly stand out and gives owners a reason to take part. Carrying the cast from street to pack links awareness directly to the shelf.
gallery.result: First packaging batch sold out in three days

gallery.title: Godzilla climbs onto a Colonne Morris on the Champs-Élysées
gallery.what: To mark the French cinema release of Godzilla Minus Zero, JCDecaux Live rebuilt the roof of a Colonne Morris at the top of the Champs-Élysées to carry a Godzilla sculpture, run with Anime Limited from 3 to 9 November. The creature's dorsal plates are backlit in blue after dark to echo its atomic breath, and the stunt sits within a wider campaign on Paris's Morris columns.
gallery.why: Turning a heritage street-furniture icon into part of the set makes one site do the work of a whole campaign and invites photos. Night-time lighting doubles the creative's life and rewards evening footfall.

gallery.title: JCDecaux UK launches 'Real makes you feel' on its own network
gallery.agency: Creative: in-house (creative directors Graham Pugh and Chris Walker; consultant Justin Gibbons; photographer Dan Tsantilis)
gallery.what: JCDecaux UK's first national brand campaign launches its 'Real World Media' positioning, with more than 20 executions featuring its own staff across roadside, retail, rail and airport environments. The line was chosen after focus groups and research with the public, agencies and marketers in which 30 lines were tested.
gallery.why: A media owner using its own panels to sell emotion rather than reach is a useful model for any brand repositioning: test lines with real audiences first, then cast real people. Running across every environment at once signals scale without saying it.

gallery.title: Supercell turns São Paulo's Sé station into 'Sé Royale'
gallery.agency: Gaming agency: Druid Creative Gaming · Scenography: Bizsys
gallery.what: For Clash Royale's tenth anniversary, Supercell, Druid Creative Gaming and JCDecaux dressed Sé metro station in 3D scenery, playing on the meeting of the Blue and Red lines to echo the game's blue-versus-red battles. Commuters can play in an 'Open Arena' on weekdays, while weekends host live broadcasts, creator challenges and university and brand eSports finals.
gallery.why: Borrowing a real-world feature of the location (two coloured lines crossing) makes the takeover feel native rather than pasted on. A rolling events calendar gives creators and fans reasons to come back, extending the media into content.
